candidates.title: Electric Arc Furnace (EAF) Steelmaking Area Source (Subpart YYYYY)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an electric arc furnace (EAF) steelmaking facility that is an area source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions, then you are subject to this subpart.
If the electric arc furnace is located at a steel foundry or the EAF is used to produce nonferrous metals, then this subpart does not apply to that facility.
If your facility is a research and development facility as defined in section 112(c)(7) of the Clean Air Act, then this subpart does not apply.
If the affected source commenced construction or reconstruction after September 20, 2007, then it is a new affected source (otherwise it is existing) for purposes of this subpart.

candidates.title: Iron and Steel Foundry Area Source (Subpart ZZZZZ)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an iron and steel foundry that is an area source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions, then you are subject to this subpart.

If your facility melts scrap, ingot, and/or other forms of iron and/or steel and pours the resulting molten metal into molds to produce final or near final shape products for introduction into commerce, then it meets the definition of an 'iron and steel foundry' (and may be subject to this subpart).

If your facility melts metal but does not pour the molten metal into molds to produce final or near-final shape products (for example, if molten metal is atomized to produce shot and grit), then the facility is not an 'iron and steel foundry' as defined in this subpart and this subpart does not apply.

If your affected source commenced construction or reconstruction before September 17, 2007 it is an existing affected source, and if on or after September 17, 2007 it is a new affected source for purposes of this subpart.

If you own or operate an existing affected source, then initial applicability as a small or large foundry is determined by calendar year 2008 metal melt production: 20,000 tons or less = small, greater than 20,000 tons = large.

If you own or operate a new affected source, then initial applicability as a small or large foundry is determined by annual metal melt capacity at startup: 10,000 tons or less = small, greater than 10,000 tons = large.
If your iron and steel foundry becomes a major source as defined in § 63.2 on or after January 2, 2008, then you must meet the requirements of 40 CFR part 63, subpart EEEEE.
If your facility is a research and development facility as defined in section 112(c)(7) of the Clean Air Act, then this subpart does not apply.

candidates.title: Iron and Steel Foundry Major Source Standards (Subpart EEEEE)

criteria.criterion: If you are an iron and steel foundry (new or existing) that is a major source of HAPs, then subpart EEEEE applies to your foundry as an affected source.

If you are not an iron and steel foundry (i.e., you do not melt and pour molten metal into molds to make final or near-final products for introduction into commerce), then subpart EEEEE does not apply to you as an iron and steel foundry affected source.

If your facility is an affected iron and steel foundry subject to this subpart, then subpart EEEEE covers emissions from metal melting furnaces, scrap preheaters, pouring areas and stations, automated conveyor and pallet cooling lines, automated shakeout lines, mold and core making lines, and fugitive emissions from foundry operations.
If your affected source commenced construction or reconstruction before December 23, 2002, it is existing for purposes of this subpart; if on or after December 23, 2002, it is new.

checklist: Do you operate an electric arc furnace (EAF) that produces molten steel? (verify equipment type and operation)

Is the EAF located at a facility that melts and pours molten metal into molds to produce final or near-final shaped castings for sale (i.e., operated as an iron and steel foundry)? (verify whether product is poured into molds)
Do you instead convert molten metal into shot, grit or other products by atomization or other non-pouring processes (verify process: water atomization vs pouring into molds)?
Is the molten-metal product introduced into commerce as castings or is it a non-casting product (verify product use and commercial distribution)?
Are you producing nonferrous metals with the EAF? (verify metal type/chemistry)
Is the facility a research and development operation as defined in CAA 112(c)(7)? (verify activity scope and R&D status)
Is the facility an area source or a major source of HAPs? (verify HAP emissions inventory against major source thresholds per 40 CFR 63.2)

If an iron and steel foundry, what was your calendar year 2008 metal melt production (for existing sources) or what is your annual metal melt capacity at startup (for new sources)? (verify tonnage to determine small vs large: 20,000 / 10,000 ton thresholds)
What are your construction/reconstruction dates relative to the subpart cutoffs (EAF subpart: Sept 20, 2007; foundry subpart: Sept 17, 2007; subpart EEEEE: Dec 23, 2002)? (verify dates)
If potentially subject to the EAF subpart, do you need to obtain a permit under 40 CFR part 70 or 71? (verify permitting obligations)

judge_text: {"score":1, "reason":"The answer includes the key EPA rationale that without pouring into molds the facility is not an iron & steel foundry per 40 CFR 63.10906 (so ZZZZZ does not apply) and it captures applicability of the EAF area source subpart (YYYYY). However, the EPA note’s point that the unit also remains subject to NSPS AAa is not mentioned in the provided criteria."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Area Sources: Industrial, Commercial, and Institutional Boilers

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an industrial, commercial, or institutional boiler that is located at or is part of an area source of hazardous air pollutants, then the boiler is subject to this subpart unless excluded under §63.11195.

If the boiler meets the definition of a gas-fired boiler (burns gaseous fuels and burns liquid fuel only during periods of gas curtailment, supply interruption, startups, or for periodic testing/maintenance/training and such liquid-fuel use does not exceed a combined total of 48 hours during any calendar year), then the boiler is not subject to this subpart.

If the boiler is an electric utility steam generating unit (EGU) as defined in this subpart (a fossil fuel-fired combustion unit of more than 25 megawatts that serves a generator producing electricity for sale or meeting the cogeneration thresholds), then the boiler is not subject to this subpart.
citations: 40 CFR 63.11237 (electric utility steam generating unit definition)

criteria.criterion: If the boiler is specifically listed as, or included in the definition of, an affected source in another standard(s) under 40 CFR part 63 or is specifically listed as an affected source under section 129 of the Clean Air Act, then the boiler is not subject to this subpart.

If the affected source is the collection of all existing industrial, commercial, and institutional boilers within a subcategory located at an area source, then applicability is determined at that affected-source collection and new/reconstructed/existing status follows the dates and rules in §63.11194.

checklist: Is the facility classified as an area source of HAPs (verify area-source designation under 40 CFR 63.2 / permitting/inspection records)?
Are the boilers 'industrial, commercial, or institutional' as defined in 40 CFR 63.11237 (i.e., used to provide steam, hot water, and/or electricity in those sectors)?
Do the boilers burn gaseous fuels as their primary fuel, and do they burn any liquid fuel only during gas curtailment, supply interruptions, startups, or for periodic testing/maintenance/training?

What is the combined total number of hours per calendar year that each boiler burns liquid fuel for periodic testing, maintenance, or operator training (verify it does not exceed 48 hours per boiler per year)?

Do the boilers burn liquid fuel during gas curtailment or interruptions beyond periods 'beyond the control of the facility' (confirm that oil use during curtailment qualifies as a 'period of gas curtailment or supply interruption' per the definition)?
Do any boilers meet the EGU definition (serve a generator producing electricity for sale and are >25 megawatts, or meet the cogeneration thresholds and fossil-fuel firing percentages)?
Are the boilers explicitly listed as an affected source in another Part 63 subpart or under section 129 (check permits and regulatory applicability determinations)?
Were the boilers constructed, reconstructed, or commenced operation before or after June 4, 2010 (to determine existing vs. new/reconstructed per §63.11194)?
Do any other exclusions in §63.11195 apply (e.g., hazardous-waste boilers, electric boilers, hot water heaters, temporary or residential boilers)?

judge_text: {"score":1,"reason":"The answer includes the 63.11195(e)/63.11237 gas-fired boiler exclusion and the oil‑only‑during‑curtailment and limited‑testing (48‑hour) conditions cited by EPA, but it does not capture EPA’s additional point that those limiting conditions should be made enforceable (locked in) via permit limits."}

candidates.title: Industrial, Commercial, and Institutional Boilers and Process Heaters NESHAP

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an industrial, commercial, or institutional boiler or process heater that is located at, or is part of, a major source of HAP, then the unit is subject to this subpart except as specified in §63.7491.
If the boiler or process heater is one of the types listed in paragraphs (a) through (n) of §63.7491, then the unit is not subject to this subpart.

If the boiler or process heater is part of an affected source subject to another subpart of this part (for example boilers and process heaters used as control devices to comply with subparts JJJ, OOO, PPP, and U), then the unit is not subject to this subpart.

If the boiler or process heater is used as a control device to comply with another subpart of this part, or part 60, part 61, or part 65 of this chapter, and at least 50 percent of the average annual heat input during any 3 consecutive calendar years is provided by regulated gas streams that are subject to another standard, then the unit is not subject to this subpart.

candidates.title: Area Source Boilers NESHAP

criteria.criterion: If the boiler is specifically listed as, or included in the definition of, an affected source in another standard under this part, then the boiler is not subject to this subpart.
If the boiler is a gas-fired boiler as defined in this subpart, then the boiler is not subject to this subpart.

If the boiler is used as a control device to comply with another subpart of this part, or part 60, part 61, or part 65 of this chapter, and at least 50 percent of the average annual heat input during any 3 consecutive calendar years is provided by regulated gas streams that are subject to another standard, then the boiler is not subject to this subpart.
If the boiler is required to have a permit under section 3005 of the Solid Waste Disposal Act or is covered by subpart EEE, then the boiler is not subject to this subpart.

candidates.title: Plywood and Composite Wood Products (PCWP) NESHAP

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a PCWP manufacturing facility located at a major source of HAP, then this subpart applies to each affected source at the facility.

If an affected source includes drying operations and the combustion unit exhaust stream is routinely used to direct-fire process unit(s) (including dryers), then that combustion unit exhaust stream and associated units are included in the affected source subject to this subpart.
If the facility does not meet the PCWP facility definition or is not located at a major source of HAP, then this subpart does not apply to the source.

checklist: Is the facility a plywood and/or composite wood products (PCWP) manufacturing facility as defined in 40 CFR 63.2231(a) (types of products and processes performed)?
Is the PCWP facility located at a major source of HAP (potential to emit ≥ 9.07 Mg/yr (10 tpy) of any single HAP or ≥ 22.68 Mg/yr (25 tpy) of combined HAP)?

Does any combustion unit exhaust from the gasification system get routinely used to direct-fire dryers or other process units (i.e., is the hot gas routed through dryers as part of normal operations)?
Is any part of the gasification/combustion system specifically listed as or included in the definition of an affected source in another NESHAP (per 40 CFR 63.11195(a) or similar)?

Is the gasification/combustion unit being used as a control device to comply with another subpart of 40 CFR part 63 (or parts 60, 61, or 65)? If so, for any rolling 3 consecutive calendar years, is at least 50% of the average annual heat input to the unit provided by regulated gas streams subject to another standard?

What fraction (annual average heat input percentage) of the unit's fuel/heat input is from regulated gas streams that are subject to another standard (to evaluate the 50% test in 40 CFR 63.7491(i) and 63.11195(g))?

Is the unit one of the exemption categories listed in 40 CFR 63.7491(a)-(n) or 40 CFR 63.11195(a)-(k) (e.g., recovery boiler, hazardous waste boiler covered by subpart EEE, electric boiler, residential, temporary, etc.)?

Are the dryers and other PCWP process units currently managed and operated under the PCWP NESHAP compliance measures (confirming the assertion that dryers 'comply with the plywood and composite wood products NESHAP')?

judge_text: {"score":1,"reason":"Some EPA reasons are captured (the answer includes that combustion gas routed directly through dryers is part of the PCWP (DDDD) affected source per 63.2232(b) and therefore not subject to the boilers/process heaters subpart). However the key EPA point that gas used for indirect heat transfer (heating thermal oil) is not covered by the PCWP exemption and therefore the gasifiers and the SCC process heaters are subject to the Boilers/Process Heaters MACT (and the relevant provision at 63.7575) is not reflected. The answer also lists §63.7491(h) as a potential exemption but does not capture EPA’s specific conclusion that §63.7491(h) does not apply to this system."}

candidates.title: Plywood and Composite Wood Products (PCWP) NESHAP

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a plywood and/or composite wood products (PCWP) manufacturing facility (which explicitly includes dry veneer and lumber kilns located at any facility), then this subpart applies to your facility.

If the PCWP manufacturing facility is located at a major source of HAP emissions (i.e., emits or has the potential to emit ≥10 tons per year of any single HAP or ≥25 tons per year of combined HAP), then this subpart applies to the facility.

If this subpart applies to the facility, then it applies to each new, reconstructed, or existing affected source at the PCWP facility, where an affected source is the collection of dryers, refiners, blenders, formers, presses, board coolers, and other process units associated with manufacturing (and specifically includes lumber kilns).

If an area source increases its emissions or its potential to emit such that it becomes a major source of HAP, then the source must be in compliance with this subpart by October 1, 2007 or upon initial startup of the affected source as a major source, whichever is later.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If a relevant standard has been established under part 63 for a source category (for example Subpart DDDD), then the owner or operator of an affected source must comply with that standard and with the applicable provisions of this subpart A.

If a stationary source emits or has the potential to emit any hazardous air pollutant and is subject to any standard, limitation, prohibition, or other federally enforceable requirement established pursuant to part 63, then the provisions of this part apply to the owner or operator of that stationary source.

If an area source becomes a major source (including situations where an area source that previously was a major source becomes a major source again), then the source is subject to the applicable major-source requirements established under this part immediately upon becoming a major source again, provided the compliance date for those major-source requirements has passed.

If a major source reclassifies to area source status, then the source remains subject to any applicable major-source requirements under this part until the reclassification becomes effective, and after the reclassification becomes effective the source is subject to any applicable area-source requirements provided their compliance dates have passed.

checklist: Do you own or operate a plywood and/or composite wood products (PCWP) manufacturing facility, or do you perform activities listed in PCWP (e.g., bonding wood with resin under heat and pressure)?
Do you operate lumber dry kilns at this facility (note: lumber kilns are explicitly included in PCWP affected sources even if located at other facility types)?
Is the facility part of a contiguous area and under common control with other stationary sources that together could be counted toward source emissions?

Calculate current actual and potential to emit (PTE) methanol (and other HAPs) for the facility considering all enforceable limitations and controls; does any single HAP PTE meet or exceed 10 tons/year or combined HAPs meet or exceed 25 tons/year?
Are there federally enforceable permit limits, work-practice limits, or operational limits that restrict potential to emit (if yes, include them when calculating PTE)?
What is the facility's current classification in permitting records (area source or major source) and has it previously been classified as a major source?
If you will increase production, when will the increased-emissions conditions begin (startup date) and will that change the facility's PTE to above major-source thresholds?
If classification will change, when will any title V or part 70 permit revision or other permit action become effective relative to the date the emissions/potential-to-emit change occurs?
Which specific pieces of equipment/processes (e.g., which kilns, dryers, refiners, presses) would be part of the affected source collection if Subpart DDDD applies?

Identify applicable compliance dates and notification requirements (e.g., initial notification under subpart A/§63.9 and any notifications referenced in Subpart DDDD such as §63.2280) and whether those dates have already passed for your affected-source status.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"All key points in the EPA NOTES are reflected: the criteria cite the 10 tpy single-HAP major-source threshold (40 CFR 63.2231(b), 63.2), that lumber kilns are included as affected sources under Subpart DDDD (40 CFR 63.2232(b)), and that an area source becoming a major source is subject to the major-source requirements upon reclassification/effective date (Subpart A provisions and 40 CFR 63.2233(c) cited). Thus the EPA reasoning is captured by the listed criteria and citations."}

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator of a stationary source emits or has the potential to emit any hazardous air pollutant and is subject to any standard under part 63, then the provisions of part 63 apply to that owner or operator.

If an area-source standard under part 63 explicitly exempts the category of area sources from the Title V permitting requirement, then those area sources are not required to obtain a Title V permit under that standard.
If an area-source standard under part 63 fails to specify the permitting requirements for affected area sources, then those area sources are subject to the requirement to obtain a Title V permit.

If a stationary source's emissions or potential to emit, considering controls, meet or exceed the major source thresholds (10 tpy any single HAP or 25 tpy combined HAP), then the source is a major source rather than an area source.

candidates.title: Chemical Manufacturing Area Sources (Subpart VVVVVV)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a chemical manufacturing process unit (CMPU) located at an area source and Table 1 HAP are present in the CMPU at the concentrations specified in paragraphs (a)(2)(i)–(iv), then the CMPU is subject to this subpart.

If your operations fall within any of the exemptions listed in paragraph (c) (for example specified area-source categories subject to other area source standards, certain NAICS 325 productions, R&D facilities, QA/QC labs, ancillary activities, or metal HAP in structures/articles), then this subpart does not apply to those operations.

If an area source installed a federally-enforceable control device on an affected CMPU and that control device is necessary to maintain the source's emissions at area-source levels, then the area source is required to obtain a permit under 40 CFR part 70 or 40 CFR part 71.

If a CMPU meets the criteria in paragraphs (a) and (b), then the affected source is the facility-wide collection of CMPUs and associated heat exchange and wastewater systems and this subpart applies to that affected source (new or existing) as described in paragraph (d).

candidates.title: Chemical Preparations Area Sources (Subpart BBBBBBB)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a chemical preparations facility that is a stationary area source and has at least one chemical preparations operation in target HAP service, then the facility is subject to this subpart.

If your facility is subject to this subpart, then you are exempt from the obligation to obtain a permit under 40 CFR part 70 or 40 CFR part 71 provided you are not otherwise required by law to obtain such a permit.
If the chemical preparations operations at your facility are subject to subpart VVVVVV or subpart CCCCCCC, then you are exempt from the requirements specified in this subpart BBBBBBB.

checklist: Determine whether the facility is an area source or a major source under 40 CFR 63.2, including whether potential-to-emit is to be calculated considering control devices (i.e., confirm PTE with and without controls).

Identify whether the specific operations are chemical manufacturing process units (CMPUs) as defined (NAICS 325 products, included unit operations, and associated tanks, transfer operations, surge control vessels, bottoms receivers).

For each CMPU, verify presence and concentrations of Table 1 HAP in feedstock, byproduct, product, process or waste streams against the thresholds in 63.11494(a)(2)(i)–(iv) (e.g., quinoline >1.0% wt, other Table 1 organics >0.1% wt).

Confirm whether any operations are among the exemptions listed in 63.11494(c) (specific listed chemical manufacturing categories, excluded NAICS activities, R&D, QA/QC labs, ancillary activities, metal HAP in structures/articles).
Document whether a federally-enforceable control device has been installed on any affected CMPU (identify device, installation date, and the CMPU it serves) as described in 63.11494(e).

If a federally-enforceable control device exists, determine and document whether that device is necessary to maintain the facility's emissions at area-source levels (i.e., would removal or bypass of the device cause PTE to exceed major-source thresholds?).

Confirm whether federally-enforceable limits (permits, consent agreements, SIP/FIP, part 70/71 permit terms, or other enforceable mechanisms) restrict emissions or PTE for the facility and whether those limits were established prior to the effective date of the applicable area-source standard.

Check whether the facility meets the definition and applicability criteria for subpart BBBBBBB (chemical preparations), including whether any operations are 'chemical preparations operations in target HAP service'.

Verify whether Ohio's Title V permitting authority has any state-specific implementation (e.g., exercised option to exclude or defer area sources under 63.1(c)(2)(i)–(ii)) or whether the subpart VVVVVV explicitly triggers Title V as per 63.11494(e).

If the facility installed controls or accepted federally-enforceable limits, assemble supporting records (permits, permit conditions, control device performance data, engineering assessments) to demonstrate whether controls are 'necessary' to remain an area source and to support any Title V applicability determination.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"Yes. The EPA's two key reasons — (1) the source became an area source via pre-existing federally enforceable operational limits established before the rule's effective date, and (2) the source does not rely on control devices to remain below major-source thresholds — are both captured by the answer (checklist item 7 and the VVVVVV control-device criterion 63.11494(e) plus checklist items 5–6)." }

candidates.title: Lead acid battery manufacturing and component manufacturing

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a lead acid battery manufacturing plant or a lead acid battery component manufacturing plant that is an area source of HAP emissions, then the plant is subject to this subpart.

If the affected source is a lead acid battery manufacturing plant, then the affected source includes all grid casting, paste mixing, three-process operations, lead oxide manufacturing, lead reclamation, and any other lead‑emitting operation associated with the plant (i.e., the ovens may be part of the affected source).

If an existing affected source has previously conducted a performance test using the same methods specified in this section and no process changes have been made since that test, or the source can demonstrate the prior test results (with or without adjustments) still reliably demonstrate compliance, then that existing source is not required to conduct a new initial performance test.

If you elect to conduct subsequent performance tests on representative affected sources instead of every unit, then the grouped affected sources must be the same process type and have the same type of air pollution control device.

If you plan to use representative emission units for subsequent performance testing, then you must prepare and submit a testing plan to the Administrator or delegated authority for review and approval no later than 90 days prior to the first scheduled performance test and include the lists and schedule specified in the rule.

candidates.title: General Provisions (performance testing requirements and waivers)

criteria.criterion: If required to do performance testing by a relevant standard, then the owner or operator must perform such tests within 180 days of the compliance date unless a waiver of performance testing is obtained under this section.

If the owner or operator submits a written application for a waiver and the Administrator, in his/her judgment, finds the source is meeting the relevant standard(s) on a continuous basis (or the source is under an extension of compliance or an extension is pending), then an individual performance test may be waived.

If requesting a waiver of an initial or subsequent performance test and a site-specific test plan is not submitted, then the application for the waiver must be submitted at least 60 days before the performance test (or accompany an extension request as specified).

candidates.title: Extension of compliance, and performance test, monitoring, recordkeeping and reporting waivers and alternatives

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator files a written application for a waiver, then the Administrator may waive individual performance tests if, in the Administrator's judgment, the source is meeting the relevant standard(s) on a continuous basis, or the source is operating under an extension of compliance, or an extension request is pending.

If an application for a waiver of an initial performance test is made and a site-specific test plan is not submitted, then the waiver application must be submitted at least 60 days before the performance test; for a subsequent test the waiver application also must be submitted at least 60 days before the performance test if a site-specific test plan is not submitted or accompany required reports as specified.

If the owner or operator requests a waiver, then the Administrator will approve or deny the waiver when he/she approves or denies an extension of compliance, approves/disapproves a site-specific test plan, makes a determination of compliance following required reports, or determines suitable progress toward compliance, as applicable.

checklist: Confirm the facility is a lead acid battery manufacturing plant or a lead acid battery component manufacturing plant and whether it is an area source of HAPs.
Document construction/reconstruction dates for the plant and for the two new Humidity Curing and Drying Oven Chambers to determine new vs existing source status under §63.11421/§63.11422.
Identify whether the new ovens are part of the affected source (i.e., whether they are a lead‑emitting operation included in the plant-level affected source).

Compile records of any prior performance tests for the existing ovens: test methods used (e.g., EPA Methods 12 or 29 for lead and Method 9 for opacity or approved alternatives), dates of tests, raw results, and whether the same methods will apply to the new ovens.

Determine whether any process changes have occurred since the prior tests (equipment changes, operating conditions, control device changes) that would affect whether prior test results reliably demonstrate compliance for the new ovens.

List the process type of each oven and the type of air pollution control device serving each (e.g., fabric filter, HEPA, scrubber), and whether the new ovens will use the same control type and be ducted similarly to existing units.

If you plan to claim similarity and test a representative unit, prepare a testing plan that lists all emission units grouped, identifies the representative unit, lists process and control device types, and provides dates of last tests and a testing schedule (to be submitted per §63.11423(c)(5)(iii)).

Assemble monitoring and compliance records showing continuous compliance (e.g., daily pressure drop, opacity observations, monitoring logs) to support a waiver application demonstrating the source is meeting standards continuously.
Locate any prior waiver(s) or Administrator correspondence regarding performance testing for existing ovens and document the basis and conditions of that waiver.

Determine scheduling deadlines for submitting a waiver application or testing plan (at least 60 days before the scheduled performance test if no site‑specific test plan is submitted; submit representative test plan per §63.11423(c)(5)(iii) at least 90 days prior to first scheduled test) and who the delegated authority is for submission/approval.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA’s stated basis — that the facility meets the regulatory criteria for a waiver of performance testing — is reflected in the submitted criteria. The answer cites the relevant waiver provisions (40 CFR 63.7(h)(2) and 63.1112(b)(2)), the lead‑acid subpart provisions on reliance on prior tests and representative unit testing (63.11423(c)(1) and (c)(5)), and includes checklist items (continuous compliance records, prior test documentation, similarity of units, and timing/submission requirements) that capture the key reasons in the EPA Notes."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Stationary Combustion Turbines (Subpart YYYY)

criteria.criterion: If your stationary combustion turbine is not equipped with an oxidation catalyst, then you must petition the Administrator for operating limitations that you will monitor to demonstrate compliance with the formaldehyde emission limitation (or alternatively petition for approval of no additional operating limitations), and you must measure these operating parameters during the initial performance test and continuously thereafter.

If you petition the Administrator for approval of additional operating limitations to demonstrate compliance with the formaldehyde emission limitation, then your petition must identify the specific parameters proposed, discuss the relationship between those parameters and HAP emissions and how limits will serve to limit HAPs, explain how upper/lower parameter values will be established, identify measurement and monitoring methods and instrument accuracy/precision, and identify instrument recalibration frequency and methods.

If you petition the Administrator for approval of no additional operating limitations, then your petition must identify operational parameters that could change, discuss any relationship between parameter changes and HAP emissions, explain why establishing limitations is not possible or feasible, identify measurement and monitoring methods and instrument accuracy/precision for parameters that could increase HAP emissions, specify recalibration frequency and methods, and explain why it is infeasible/unreasonable/unnecessary to adopt parameters as operating limitations.

If you are using an oxidation catalyst to comply with the formaldehyde emission limitation, then you must continuously monitor catalyst inlet temperature as specified in the operating limitations in Table 2 and Table 5 of this subpart.

If you are not using an oxidation catalyst, then you must continuously monitor any parameters specified in your approved petition to the Administrator in order to comply with the operating limitations in Table 2 and Table 5 of this subpart.

If you must conduct the required performance test(s), then each performance test must be conducted at high load defined as 100 percent plus or minus 10 percent, must consist of three separate test runs with each run lasting at least 1 hour, and (before Sep 8, 2020) must not be conducted during startup, shutdown, or malfunction while (after Sep 8, 2020) tests must be under representative conditions excluding startup and shutdown and not during malfunctions.

If you are required to use a continuous monitoring system (CMS) after September 8, 2020, then you must develop and implement a CMS quality control program with written procedures per §63.8(d)(1)-(2) and keep the written procedures on record for the life of the affected source or until no longer subject to the part.

If you perform parametric monitoring to demonstrate continuous compliance, then you must conduct all parametric monitoring at all times the stationary combustion turbine is operating except during monitor malfunctions, associated repairs, and required QA/QC activities, and you must not use data recorded during those excluded periods to meet subpart requirements.

checklist: Confirm turbine type (lean premix gas-fired) and whether it is new or reconstructed (construction date relative to Jan 14, 2003).
Verify whether an oxidation catalyst is installed on the turbine (yes/no).

Decide whether you will petition the Administrator for additional operating limitations or petition for approval of no additional operating limitations and prepare to submit the required petition before conducting the initial performance test (do not conduct initial test until petition approved/disapproved per 63.6120(e)).

If petitioning for additional operating limitations (e.g., %Load and inlet air temperature T1), prepare documentation identifying the specific parameters and demonstrating the quantitative relationship between each parameter and formaldehyde (HAP) emissions.
If petitioning for additional operating limitations, prepare documentation explaining how upper and/or lower parameter limits will be established for each proposed parameter.

Document the measurement and continuous-monitoring methods and the instruments proposed for each parameter (location, accuracy, precision), and the frequency and methods for instrument recalibration and QA/QC.
Ensure capability to measure the proposed parameters during the initial performance test and to continuously monitor them thereafter (data logging, record retention, real-time alarms if applicable).

Plan initial performance test timing and conditions: schedule three separate test runs at high load (100% ±10%), each at least 1 hour long, and confirm tests will not occur during startup, shutdown, or malfunction (and meet representative conditions per 63.6120(c)).
If a CMS will be used after Sep 8, 2020, prepare a CMS quality control program with written procedures per §63.8(d)(1)-(2) and retain records as required.

Confirm monitoring will be operated at all times the turbine operates (except during monitor malfunctions, repairs, and required QA/QC activities) and establish procedures to exclude and document data from excluded periods per 63.6135(b).

Confirm whether any of the following fuel conditions apply (which would impose additional monitoring): firing landfill or digester gas or gasified MSW at ≥10% gross heat input annually, or use of any distillate oil at the major source (if yes, prepare required fuel usage monitoring/recording as specified in 63.6125(c)-(d)).

Prepare records and be ready to make available to the Administrator documentation supporting that initial test conditions represent normal/representative operation and any petition justification materials upon request.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Municipal Solid Waste Landfills

criteria.criterion: If the landfill meets the collection and control system removal criteria in § 63.1957(b) (closed landfill, 15-year minimum operation or demonstration of inability to operate 15 years, and NMOC < 50 Mg/yr on three successive test dates), then the collection and control system may be capped, removed, or decommissioned.

If the landfill is a closed landfill (as defined in § 63.1990) and a closure report has been submitted to the Administrator as provided in § 63.1981(f), then the closed-landfill criterion is satisfied for removal actions under § 63.1957(b)(1).

If the gas collection and control system has been in operation a minimum of 15 years, or the owner/operator demonstrates the system will be unable to operate for 15 years due to declining gas flow, then the 15-year operation criterion of § 63.1957(b)(2) is met.

If, following the procedures in § 63.1959(c), the calculated NMOC emission rate is less than 50 Mg/yr on three successive test dates (each test at least 90 days apart and no more than 180 days apart), then the NMOC emission-rate criterion for removal in § 63.1957(b)(3) is met.

If the owner/operator determines NMOC mass emission rate for removal purposes by using Equation 3 and measures QLFG at the common header and CNMOC from the common header prior to any gas moving or condensate removal equipment according to § 63.1959(c)(1)-(2), then the NMOC calculation for removal eligibility is being performed as required.

If the landfill has a design capacity equal to or greater than 2.5 million Mg and 2.5 million m3, then the owner/operator must either comply with § 63.1959(b)(2) (install/operate an appropriate collection and control system) or calculate NMOC emissions using the procedures in § 63.1959(a) and recalculate annually.

If the owner/operator intends to remove or cease operation of control equipment, then an equipment removal report must be submitted to the Administrator 30 days prior containing the closure report, performance-test documentation demonstrating the 15-year control period has expired or information demonstrating inability to operate 15 years due to declining flow, and dated copies of three successive NMOC emission rate reports as specified in § 63.1981(g).

checklist: Verify the landfill's maximum design capacity (in megagrams and cubic meters) from the most recent state/local/tribal permit or the most recent design capacity report (40 CFR 63.1990; 40 CFR 63.1981(a)(2)).

Confirm whether the landfill is closed (no additional solid waste will be placed without filing a notification of modification) per the definition of 'closed landfill' in 40 CFR 63.1990 and record the date waste acceptance ceased.
If closed, confirm that a closure report was submitted to the Administrator in accordance with 40 CFR 63.1981(f) (closure report timing and contents).

Determine the date the gas collection and control system (and specifically well EW-308A) was installed and first put into operation (EW-308A installation: May 2018) to assess whether the system has been in operation ≥ 15 years, and gather any initial performance test reports and operation history required by 40 CFR 63.1981(i).

If the system has not been in operation 15 years, assemble documentation that would demonstrate the gas collection and control system will be unable to operate for 15 years due to declining gas flow (flow records, well productivity analyses, performance test data) as referenced in 40 CFR 63.1957(b)(2) and 40 CFR 63.1981(g)(1)(ii).

Obtain three successive NMOC emission rate reports showing NMOC < 50 Mg/yr, and verify each test date is at least 90 days apart and no more than 180 days apart, calculated following the procedures of 40 CFR 63.1959(c) and 40 CFR 63.1957(b)(3).

For the removal-purpose NMOC calculation, verify measurement capability and records: total landfill gas flow rate measured at the common header using a device calibrated per EPA Method 2E (40 CFR 63.1959(c)(1)), and NMOC concentration sampled from the common header prior to any gas movers or condensate removal and analyzed per EPA Method 25 or 25C (40 CFR 63.1959(c)(2)).

Confirm whether removing or decommissioning EW-308A constitutes 'removal or cessation of operation of the control equipment' that triggers the equipment removal report requirement in 40 CFR 63.1981(g), and prepare to submit the equipment removal report at least 30 days prior with the required attachments (closure report, performance test or demonstration of inability to operate 15 years, and dated NMOC reports).

Assemble and be ready to submit any required design-plan, performance-test, or NMOC report records electronically via CEDRI/CDX per the reporting procedures in 40 CFR 63.1981(l), and be prepared for the Administrator to request additional information per 40 CFR 63.1981(g)(2).

judge_text: {"score": 2, "reason": "EPA's note only states the landfill is subject to the MSW landfill NESHAP. OUR ANSWER includes the relevant Subpart AAAA criteria that establish when a landfill is subject (design capacity ≥2.5 million Mg/2.5 million m3 and associated monitoring/collection/control requirements) and the specific removal/decommissioning and reporting provisions (§63.1957, §63.1959, §63.1981) — so the key reason in the EPA notes (that the landfill is subject to the standard) is captured."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Plywood and Composite Wood Products (PCWP)

criteria.criterion: If an equipment is a process unit (for example, a reconstituted wood product press or a reconstituted wood product board cooler) at an affected source, then you must meet one compliance option for each process unit and you cannot combine compliance options in paragraphs (a) and (b) of §63.2240 for a single process unit.

If you choose the production-based compliance option for a process unit, then you must comply with the production-based total HAP compliance options in Table 1A and you may not use an add-on control system or a wet control device to meet the production-based option.

If you choose an add-on control system concentration-based compliance option (options 2, 4, or 6 in Table 1B) for a reconstituted wood product press at a new or existing affected source or for a reconstituted wood product board cooler at a new affected source, then you must have a capture device that either meets the wood products enclosure definition in §63.2292 or achieves a capture efficiency ≥ 95 percent.

If you operate a reconstituted wood product press at a new or existing affected source or a reconstituted wood product board cooler at a new affected source, then you must either use a wood products enclosure as defined in §63.2292 or measure the capture efficiency of the capture device for the press or board cooler using Methods 204/204A–204F of 40 CFR part 51, appendix M (as appropriate), or the alternative tracer gas method in appendix A, and submit documentation of the enclosure design or capture efficiency verification with your Notification of Compliance Status.

If your facility is a plywood and composite wood products (PCWP) manufacturing facility with an affected source, then this subpart applies to each new, reconstructed, or existing affected source at the facility.

If you need to determine which compliance tables and deadlines apply to a process unit, then you must determine whether the affected source commenced construction or reconstruction on or before May 18, 2023 (or after) because tables 1C–1E and the associated compliance dates in §63.2240(d) apply based on that date.

If you must demonstrate initial compliance with the compliance options and operating requirements, then you must conduct performance tests and establish site-specific operating requirements according to §63.2262 and table 4 to this subpart, except that combustion units that accept process exhausts into the flame zone are exempt from the performance testing to show compliance with the compliance options in Table 1B or 1C and the operating requirements for thermal oxidizers.

checklist: Confirm whether your facility is a PCWP manufacturing facility and whether the press and board cooler are part of the affected source (definition of affected source).
Verify that the press and the board cooler are classified as separate process units (reconstituted wood product press; reconstituted wood product board cooler).
For each process unit, decide which compliance path you will use: production-based (Table 1A) or add-on control system (Table 1B); remember the requirement is applied per process unit.
If selecting production-based compliance for a unit, confirm you will not rely on any add-on control system or wet control device for that unit.

If selecting an add-on control concentration-based option (options 2, 4, or 6 in Table 1B) for a reconstituted wood product press (new or existing) or a board cooler (new), verify the capture system is either a wood products enclosure or achieves capture efficiency ≥95%.

If claiming a wood products enclosure, document that the enclosure meets the design criteria in §63.2292 (natural draft openings distance, total opening area ≤5% of enclosure surface, average facial velocity ≥3,600 m/hr (200 ft/min) into the enclosure, doors/windows closed during routine operation, designed/maintained to capture all emissions).

If demonstrating capture efficiency, plan to perform capture efficiency testing using Methods 204/204A–204F (40 CFR part 51, appendix M) or the alternative tracer gas method in appendix A and collect the test report for the Notification of Compliance Status.
Determine construction or reconstruction date of the affected source relative to May 18, 2023 to identify which compliance tables (1A/B vs 1C/1D/1E) and compliance dates apply.

Prepare for initial compliance demonstration testing and establishment of site-specific operating requirements per §63.2262 and table 4, and confirm whether any combustion units that accept process exhaust into the flame zone are present (those are exempt from certain performance tests).

Assemble and plan to submit the Notification of Compliance Status with required documentation: initial compliance test results, capture efficiency verification or wood products enclosure documentation, and established site-specific operating requirements.

judge_text: {"score": 2, "reason": "EPA’s key point—that the rule does not allow summing/combining compliance options to demonstrate compliance—is reflected in the answer: it states you must meet one compliance option for each process unit and that the requirement is applied per process unit (citing §63.2240), and the checklist reiterates that compliance is determined for each unit rather than by summing units."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Rubber Tire Manufacturing

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a rubber tire manufacturing facility that is located at, or is a part of, a major source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions, then you are subject to this subpart.

If your stationary source emits or has the potential to emit (considering controls) any single HAP at a rate of 9.07 megagrams (10 tons) or more per year or any combination of HAP at a rate of 22.68 megagrams (25 tons) or more per year, then it meets the definition of a major source for purposes of this subpart.
If your facility engages in the manufacture of rubber tires or their components, then this subpart applies to each existing, new, or reconstructed affected source at the facility.

If processes at your facility use or process cements and solvents as defined in §63.6015 (including listed operations such as tire repair operations), then those processes constitute the tire production affected source subject to this subpart.

If you own or operate a tire cord production affected source but the primary product produced at that affected source is determined to be subject to another subpart as of the effective date of that other subpart or startup, then that tire cord affected source is not subject to this subpart.

If your rubber tire manufacturing affected source is a research and development facility operated under close supervision of technically trained personnel and not engaged in manufacture of products for commercial sale except de minimis, then that affected source is not subject to this subpart.

candidates.title: General Provisions (40 CFR part 63 Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If you are subject to this subpart, then the applicable portions of the General Provisions in §§63.1 through 63.15 identified in Table 17 to this subpart apply to you.

checklist: Determine whether the facility is a rubber tire manufacturing facility (production of rubber tires or integral components) versus only performing retreading/repair.
Calculate actual and potential-to-emit HAPs (tons/year) for the entire contiguous facility under common control, considering controls, to see if single HAP ≥ 10 tpy or combined HAPs ≥ 25 tpy.

Inventory processes and materials to confirm whether operations use or process 'cements and solvents' as defined in 40 CFR 63.6015 (examples: undertread/tread cements, green tire spray, slab dip, painting, repair paints, marking inks, equipment cleaning solvents).
Confirm whether tire repair/retreading operations at your site use/process the cements/solvents listed above (63.5982(b)(1) explicitly lists tire repair operations).
Verify whether any tire cord production occurs and, if so, whether the primary product at that affected source is determined subject to another subpart as of that subpart's effective date or startup.

Determine whether the facility (or affected source) is a research and development facility as described in 63.5981(b)(2) (operated under close supervision, not commercial manufacture except de minimis).
Establish whether affected sources are new, existing, or reconstructed by comparing construction/reconstruction dates to October 18, 2000 (see definition of new affected source in 63.5982(c)).
If subject to the subpart, consult Table 17 to this subpart to identify which General Provisions (§§63.1–63.15) apply and what compliance/notification/recordkeeping requirements apply (see 63.6013).

Document and quantify specific operations listed in 63.5982(b) at your site (tire production processes, tire cord production, puncture sealant application, rubber processing) to map which affected-source categories (if any) exist on-site.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's sole key reason—that the facilities are not major sources of HAPs—is captured: the answer includes the major-source emission thresholds (≥10 tpy single / ≥25 tpy combined) and a checklist item to calculate actual and potential-to-emit for the contiguous facility, so the EPA note is reflected in the criteria."}

candidates.title: Petroleum refinery catalytic cracking units

criteria.criterion: If your catalytic cracking unit regenerator vent does not introduce any other gas streams into the catalyst regeneration vent (i.e., is a complete combustion unit with no additional combustion devices), then you may use the alternative hourly actual exhaust gas flow calculation (Equation 1) in §63.1573 provided you install and operate continuous parameter monitoring of regenerator air flow and gas temperature as specified.

If you have a gas analyzer installed in the catalytic cracking regenerator exhaust vent prior to the addition of air or other gas streams (you may measure upstream or downstream of an electrostatic precipitator but must measure upstream of a carbon monoxide boiler), then you may use the alternative flow calculation (Equation 2) in §63.1573 as an alternative to calculating Qr required in Equation 1 of §63.1564 provided you also install and operate the required continuous parameter monitoring and gas analyzer measuring CO2, CO, and O2.

If you elect to comply with the NSPS PM coke burn-off emission limit (Option 1b) or the PM per coke burn-off emission limit (Option 2), then you must compute PM emission rate using Equations 1–3 in §63.1564(b)(4)(i) and you may use the alternative Qr calculation procedures in §63.1573 to obtain the volumetric flow (Qr) used in those equations.

If you intend to use the §63.1573 alternatives for calculating exhaust gas flow or coke burn-off related monitoring, then you must install, operate, and maintain the applicable continuous emission, continuous opacity, and continuous parameter monitoring systems according to the requirements (sampling frequency, data reduction, minimum data availability, and recordkeeping) in §63.1572.

If you do not use the §63.1573 alternative to calculate Qr, then the volumetric flow rate Qsd used to compute PM emission rate must be measured by Method 2 in appendix A-1 to part 60 as required in §63.1564(b)(4)(i).

checklist: Confirm the unit is a catalytic cracking unit (FCCU) and identify the specific catalyst regenerator vent(s).

Determine whether the regenerator vent is subject to the NSPS PM requirements in 40 CFR 60.102 or 60.102a (i.e., whether you are an NSPS unit and which NSPS option you plan to elect: Option 1a/1b/1c/2/3/4).

Verify whether the regenerator vent introduces any other gas streams into the catalyst regeneration vent (e.g., oxygen-enriched air, nitrogen, or other additions); if yes, note that §63.1573(a)(1) alternative (Equation 1) may not be allowed.

If considering the §63.1573(a)(2) alternative, confirm you have (or can install) a gas analyzer in the regenerator exhaust vent that measures CO2, CO, and O2 and is located prior to the addition of air/other gases and upstream of any CO boiler (measurement may be upstream or downstream of an ESP).
Decide which PM compliance option you will elect (e.g., NSPS Option 1b or Option 2) because Equations 1–3 in §63.1564 apply to those options and reference Qr.
Decide whether you will use the §63.1573 alternative to determine Qr or will measure Qsd by Method 2 (Method 2 required in §63.1564(b)(4)(i) absent the alternative).

Ensure capability to install and operate continuous parameter monitoring as required by §63.1573(a)(1)(i) and §63.1572 (e.g., continuous volumetric air flow to regenerator, gas temperature near control device, and required sampling/recording frequencies and data availability).

Confirm you will meet the §63.1572 requirements for performance evaluations, cycle times, minimum valid data availability (e.g., 75% hourly data), data reduction, and recordkeeping for the applicable CEMS/CPMS/COMS.
If you plan to request alternative monitoring or use an automated data compression system, prepare the submittal materials and demonstrations required in §63.1573(f) and §63.1573(d) as applicable.

If relying on alternatives, document measurement locations relative to add-on controls (ESP, CO boiler) and retain supporting calculations and control-room instrumentation sources for Qa and Qoxy used in the equations.

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's note states the alternatives for coke burn-off and exhaust flow are acceptable under the cited regulations (with conditions). OUR ANSWER includes the key conditions and limitations (eligibility for §63.1573 alternatives, monitoring/CEMS/CPMS requirements, measurement location restrictions, and the Method 2 fallback) with appropriate citations, so the EPA reasoning is captured."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Petroleum Refineries (Refinery MACT)

criteria.criterion: If the plant site is a major source as defined in CAA section 112(a) and a petroleum refining process unit at the site emits or contains one or more HAPs listed in table 1 of this subpart, then the provisions of subpart CC apply to those petroleum refining process units and related emission points at the site.

If a wastewater stream at a petroleum refinery has a total annual benzene loading of 10 megagrams/year or greater, a flow rate of 0.02 liters per minute or greater, a benzene concentration of 10 parts per million by weight or greater, and is not exempt under 40 CFR part 61 subpart FF, then that stream meets the definition of a Group 1 wastewater stream under this subpart.

If a Group 1 wastewater stream is managed in a piece of equipment that is also subject to the provisions of 40 CFR part 60, subpart QQQ, then after the compliance dates specified in this subpart the Group 1 wastewater stream is required to comply only with subpart CC (i.e., not with subpart QQQ).

If a Group 1 or Group 2 wastewater stream is conveyed, stored, or treated in a wastewater stream management unit that also receives streams subject to the subpart G wastewater provisions (§§ 63.133–63.147), then the wastewater stream must comply as specified in § 63.640(o)(2)(i) or (ii), and that compliance constitutes compliance with subpart CC for that stream.

If an emissions point is a wastewater stream associated with a petroleum refining process unit at a plant site that meets the subpart CC applicability criteria, then that wastewater stream is part of the affected source covered by subpart CC.

checklist: Confirm whether the plant site is a major source under CAA section 112(a).
For the specific wastewater stream, verify total annual benzene loading (≥10 megagrams/year) using the calculation procedures (reference: 40 CFR part 61, subpart FF procedures).
Verify wastewater flow rate (is it ≥0.02 liters per minute?) and benzene concentration (is it ≥10 ppm by weight?).
Confirm whether the wastewater stream is exempt from control requirements under 40 CFR part 61, subpart FF.
Determine whether the equipment that manages/treats the wastewater stream is also subject to 40 CFR part 60, subpart QQQ (identify the unit type and check subpart QQQ applicability).
Confirm whether the compliance dates in subpart CC have passed for the applicable controls/units at your facility.

If the wastewater stream is managed in a unit that also receives streams governed by subpart G wastewater provisions, determine whether you will follow §63.640(o)(2)(i) or (o)(2)(ii) and document which subpart G and/or subpart FF provisions will be used for treatment/control.

If planning to control the stream under the Benzene Waste Operations NESHAP (part 61, subpart FF), document which control measures will be used and whether those measures are installed in equipment that is also covered by subpart QQQ or subpart G provisions.

If a flare will be used as the control device for the wastewater vapors, verify applicable flare requirements and applicable compliance date (see subpart CC §63.670 references and the Jan 30, 2019 applicability trigger).

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's key reason—that the facility may reclassify a Group 2 stream as a Group 1 under the Refinery MACT and thus subpart CC applicability follows—is reflected in the answer (references to 40 CFR 63.641 for Group 1 definition and 40 CFR 63.640(a)/(o) for CC applicability and interaction with subpart QQQ)."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Chemical Recovery Combustion Sources

criteria.criterion: If the unit is an existing kraft or soda recovery furnace, smelt dissolving tank, or lime kiln at a kraft or soda pulp mill, then it is subject to the Subpart MM standards and must comply by the applicable compliance date.

If an owner/operator is required to conduct the initial or periodic performance test, then the tests must be conducted using the test methods and procedures listed in this subpart (including the methods in §63.865(b) such as Method 5, Method 29, or Method 17 with the specified sampling time/volume and oxygen corrections) and must be conducted under representative normal operating conditions (excluding startup, shutdown, or malfunction) with process information recorded to document those conditions.

If the owner/operator seeks to use prior performance test data (e.g., tests conducted after promulgation but before the compliance date) to establish operating limits or demonstrate compliance, then those prior tests may be used only if they were performed using the required test methods and procedures in this subpart and the owner/operator certifies that control techniques and processes have not been modified since the testing.

If a performance test is to be used to set emission or monitoring operating limits, then the owner/operator must be able to provide the process data measured during the performance test (e.g., volumetric gas flow rates, oxygen concentrations, black liquor solids firing rates, CaO production rates) and must perform oxygen and flow corrections as required by this subpart.

checklist: Confirm the affected unit type(s): recovery furnace, smelt dissolving tank (SDT), and/or lime kiln (see definitions in 40 CFR 63.861).
Confirm the unit is an existing unit (subject to the March 13, 2004 compliance date) and record startup date and whether it is subject as an existing source (40 CFR 63.863(a), 63.862(a)).
Record the date(s) of the November 2003 particulate tests and verify they occurred prior to the compliance date (compare test date to 63.863(a)).

Verify which test methods were used in the November 2003 tests (Method 5, 29, or 17) and whether required adjustments were applied (e.g., add 0.009 g/dscm to Method 17 results and stack temp ≤205 °C if Method 17 was used) per 40 CFR 63.865(b)(1).
Verify each test run met the minimum sampling time and sample volume requirements (≥60 minutes and ≥0.90 dscm per Method 5/29/17) per 40 CFR 63.865(b)(1).

Verify oxygen concentration measurements and corrections were performed using required methods (Method 3A/3B or ANSI/ASME alternative) and that PM and flow were corrected to the proper reference oxygen (8% for recovery furnaces, 10% for lime kilns) per 40 CFR 63.865(b)(2)–(4).

Confirm volumetric flow rates, oxygen concentrations, and black liquor solids firing rates (and CaO production rate for lime kilns) were measured and recorded during the tests to allow calculation of ER (Equations in 63.865(a)(1) and (a)(2)(i)–(v)).

Confirm the performance tests were conducted during representative normal operating conditions (not during startup, shutdown, or malfunction) and that process information and an explanation supporting normal operation were recorded and retained per 40 CFR 63.865 (intro).

Determine whether any physical or operational modifications to the air pollution control device or control techniques have occurred since November 2003; if so, prior test data may not be used to establish current operating limits without re-testing (40 CFR 63.864(j)(2) and 63.862(a)(1)(ii)(D)(1)).

If intending to use prior test data to set monitoring operating limits, prepare certification that control techniques/processes have not been modified since the testing, and ensure the test methods/procedures used match the methods required by this subpart (40 CFR 63.864(j)(2)).

Assemble supporting records to make available to the Administrator upon request: raw test reports, traverse and sampling logs, Method documentation, process operating data during each run (flow, O2, BLS, CaO), and the owner's certification regarding modifications (40 CFR 63.865; 40 CFR 63.864(j)(2)).

judge_text: {"score":2, "reason":"EPA’s sole stated basis was conditional approval of the Nov 2003 tests — i.e., they may be used only if they meet Subpart MM testing and recording requirements and if the owner certifies no changes (methods, representative normal operation, O2/flow corrections, required process data, and no modifications). Those conditions are all reflected in the provided criteria and checklist."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Portland Cement Manufacturing (Subpart LLL)

criteria.criterion: If the facility is a major source subject to Subpart LLL, then the affected sources listed in 40 CFR 63.1345 (raw material, clinker, or finished product storage bins; conveying system transfer points; bagging systems; bulk loading or unloading systems; raw and finish mills; and existing raw material dryers) must not discharge gases with opacity exceeding 10 percent.
If your source is a raw or finish mill at a major or area source subject to this subpart, then the applicable opacity limit is 10 percent (Table 1).

If kiln exhaust and clinker cooler exhaust are commingled in a single stack, then the commingled stream must be included in the applicable emission/opacity testing (i.e., you must test the commingled exhaust stream), and opacity testing must be performed using Method 9 per the subpart's performance test requirements.
If the exhaust streams of a kiln with an inline raw mill and a clinker cooler are comingled, then the commingled exhaust stream must be tested with the raw mill on and with the raw mill off.

If you are subject to the opacity limitation under §63.1345, then you must demonstrate compliance by Method 9 using the maximum 6-minute average opacity during the performance test (3 hours/30 six-minute averages; the test duration may be reduced to 1 hour only if the conditions in §63.1349(b)(2)(i)-(ii) are met).

If you are subject to opacity limits under §63.1345, then you must perform monthly Method 22 visible emissions checks and, if visible emissions are observed, conduct Method 9 opacity testing within 1 hour as specified in the monitoring requirements.

checklist: Determine whether your facility is a 'major source' subject to Subpart LLL (check Title V/MACT applicability and permitting status).
Confirm whether the clinker cooler at your facility is treated as an affected source under Subpart LLL and whether opacity limits in §63.1345 apply to it.
Confirm that kiln exhaust and clinker cooler exhaust are commingled in a single stack (document stacks and ducting).
Identify whether the kiln has an inline raw mill and record the fraction of operating time the raw mill is ON vs OFF (raw mill on/off duty cycle).
Quantify the fraction or flow of clinker cooler exhaust that bypasses the inline kiln/raw mill (you report ~20% on average; verify flow measurement basis and variability).
Determine whether any other streams (alkali bypass, coal mill) are commingled with the kiln/clinker cooler and document their stacks and flows.
Identify whether the affected commingled exhaust is routed through a PM control device (baghouse/ESP) and where the sampling/monitoring point would be located (upstream/downstream of control).
Determine whether the kiln and clinker cooler are new or existing units (affects other pollutant limits but verify for recordkeeping).
Verify current opacity monitoring approach: monthly Method 22 schedule, presence/use of COMS or BLDS, and whether you must/are using Method 9 performance testing.
If commingled and an inline raw mill exists, plan to perform performance tests with raw mill ON and OFF (and record the time-weighting basis you will use).

Locate and document the representative sampling location for Method 9/Method 22 and ensure Method 9 test duration and reading aggregation (30 6-minute averages or allowed 1-hour reduction conditions).
Check permit and historic test records to see if a site-specific operating limit or monitoring plan under §63.1350(p) has already been established for opacity or related CPMS/CEMS.
