candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Pharmaceuticals Production

criteria.criterion: If the facility produces a material that meets the definition of a "pharmaceutical product" (for example, materials described by SIC code 2833 or 2834; materials whose manufacturing process is described by NAICS 325411 or 325412; finished dosage forms; active ingredients or precursors produced at a facility whose primary operations are SIC 2833 or 2834; or, at a facility whose primary operations are not SIC 2833/2834, a material whose primary use is as an active ingredient or precursor), then the operations are pharmaceutical manufacturing operations and may be subject to Subpart GGG.

If equipment and unit operations constitute a pharmaceutical manufacturing process unit (PMPU) as defined (process equipment used to produce a pharmaceutical product, plus associated storage tanks and listed components), then that PMPU is within the scope of Subpart GGG.

candidates.title: Miscellaneous Organic Chemical Manufacturing (MCPU / MON Rule)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing process units (MCPU) that are located at, or are part of, a major source of HAP, then you are subject to the requirements of Subpart FFFF.

If a process unit produces materials described by the listed SIC or NAICS codes (e.g., organic chemicals classified under 1987 SIC 282–289 or 1997 NAICS 325) (or other listed categories), and the MCPU processes, uses, or generates any organic HAP listed in section 112(b) or hydrogen halide/halogen HAP, and that MCPU is not an affected source under another Part 63 subpart, then that unit meets the MCPU definition and is subject to Subpart FFFF.

If the operation is an exempt category listed in paragraph (c) (for example, a research and development facility or other operations specifically listed), then the requirements of Subpart FFFF do not apply.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for HCl Production Facilities

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an HCl production facility that produces a liquid HCl product at a concentration of 30 weight percent or greater during normal operations and the facility is located at, or is part of, a major source of HAP, then the HCl production facility is subject to Subpart NNNNN.

If the HCl production facility is also subject to NESHAP under one of the listed subparts (including Subpart GGG for pharmaceuticals), then the HCl production facility is not subject to Subpart NNNNN.

checklist: Determine the facility's official primary SIC code and NAICS code (is facility categorized as SIC 2833 or 2834 or NAICS 325411/325412?).

Confirm whether the product manufactured (glucosamine hydrochloride) is produced/marketed as a pharmaceutical active ingredient, precursor, or finished dosage form, or primarily used as an active ingredient.
Determine whether the production operations constitute a pharmaceutical manufacturing process unit (PMPU): list unit operations, associated storage tanks, and components used in manufacture.
Inventory whether any process at the site produces, uses, or generates organic HAP listed in CAA section 112(b) or hydrogen halide/halogen HAP (e.g., hydrogen chloride) and quantify amounts.
Establish whether any on-site activity is an HCl production facility that produces liquid HCl product at ≥30 wt% during normal operations (versus simply using or storing purchased HCl).

Determine whether the HCl production (if any) is occasional/episodic or continuous and whether it meets the HCl production facility definition beginning at the point a gaseous HCl stream enters the unit.
Prepare a facility-level HAP emissions inventory and evaluate major-source status (potential to emit ≥10 tpy of any single HAP or ≥25 tpy total HAP).

Verify whether the MCPU criteria are met: (a) the material produced is described by the SIC/NAICS lists in §63.2435(b)(1) (or other listed categories), (b) the unit processes/uses/generates organic HAP or hydrogen halide HAP, and (c) the unit is not already an affected source under another Part 63 subpart.
Check for applicability exclusions: e.g., is the operation a research and development facility or otherwise listed in §63.2435(c)?

If considering Subpart NNNNN applicability, verify whether the HCl unit (or whole facility) is already subject to Subpart GGG (pharmaceuticals) or other subparts listed in §63.8985(b), because that would exclude Subpart NNNNN.

If emissions include halogenated vent streams or hydrogen halide HAP, identify vent characteristics and calculate halogen atom emission rate per Subpart FFFF/definitions (to evaluate Group/halogenated stream treatment).
Document whether glucosamine HCl is produced from an in-house HCl-synthesis HCl production unit or from externally purchased HCl (purchased use is different than HCl production applicability).

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA NOTES state the MON Rule applies; OUR ANSWER includes Subpart FFFF (MON) with the relevant applicability criteria (MCPU at a major source, production/processing of organic HAPs or hydrogen halide HAP such as HCl, and not being covered by another Part 63 subpart), so the key reason given in the notes is captured."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Site Remediation

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate a facility at which you conduct a site remediation (as defined in §63.7957) and that site remediation (1) cleans up a remediation material, (2) is co-located at your facility with one or more other stationary sources that emit HAP and meet an affected-source definition in a source category regulated by another subpart under 40 CFR part 63, and (3) your facility is a major source of HAP, then the site remediation is subject to this subpart
if the site remediation only cleans up material that does not contain any of the HAP listed in Table 1 of this subpart, then the site remediation is not subject to this subpart

if the total quantity of the HAP listed in Table 1 contained in the remediation material excavated, extracted, pumped, or otherwise removed during all site remediations conducted at your facility is less than 1 megagram (Mg) annually, then the site remediation activities are not subject to the requirements of this subpart except for the recordkeeping requirement

if your site remediation is completed within 30 consecutive calendar days according to the conditions in §63.7884(b)(1) through (3), then that site remediation is not subject to the standards in §63.7884(a) (i.e., not subject to the subpart's standards for that remediation)
if the site remediation is conducted at a gasoline service station to clean up remediation material from a leaking underground storage tank, then the site remediation is not subject to this subpart
if the site remediation is conducted at a farm or residential site, then the site remediation is not subject to this subpart
if the site remediation is conducted at a research and development facility that meets the requirements under CAA section 112(c)(7), then the site remediation is not subject to this subpart

if a remediation-material handling unit at your site is part of an affected remediation material management unit (per §63.7882), then you must select and meet one of the control or compliance options in §63.7886(b) for that unit (e.g., unit-specific standards, demonstrate VOHAP <500 ppmw, comply with another applicable subpart, or meet specified biological-treatment performance and monitoring requirements)

if an equipment component contains or contacts remediation material with total HAP (Table 1) ≥ 10 percent by weight and the component is intended to operate in remediation-material service for 300 hours or more per calendar year, then that component is part of the affected-source group for equipment leaks under this subpart
if the remediation activity includes process vents associated with in-situ or ex-situ remediation processes, then the entire group of those process vents is an affected source under this subpart
if a pressure relief device is in remediation material service, then that pressure relief device is an affected source under this subpart

if you complete all remediation activities subject to this subpart and notify the Administrator in writing that all subject remediation activities are completed, then future completed remediation activities are not subject to the requirements of this subpart (but you must maintain records of compliance for each remediation activity that was subject)

checklist: Do you conduct a 'site remediation' as defined at 40 CFR 63.7957 (activities that remove, destroy, degrade, transform, immobilize, or otherwise manage remediation material)?
Does the excavated soil meet the definition of 'remediation material' (i.e., contain one or more HAP listed in Table 1 of Subpart GGGGG)?
What is the speciated HAP content (VOHAP) of the excavated soil (measure per §63.7943 / §63.7957 methods) and does it exceed 500 ppmw?
What is the total annual quantity (mass) of the Table 1 HAP contained in all remediation material removed at the facility this year (is it ≥ or < 1 Mg/yr)?
Is your facility a major source of HAP (potential to emit ≥10 tpy of any single HAP or ≥25 tpy total HAP) per 40 CFR 63.2?
Is the remediation co-located with one or more other stationary sources at your facility that emit HAP and meet an affected-source definition under another part 63 subpart?
Will the soil excavation, storage, and backfill be completed within 30 consecutive calendar days according to the criteria in §63.7884(b)(1)–(3)?
Will the excavated soil be shipped off-site, and if so will shipping documentation include statements required by §63.7884(b)(2) and §63.7936?

How will you store/manage the contaminated soil on-site (e.g., stockpile on ground, roll-off container, truck bed, tank, transfer system) and does that unit qualify as a remediation material management unit under §63.7957?

Will any equipment components (pumps, valves, connectors, pressure relief devices) contact the remediation material, and do any of those components contain ≥10% Table 1 HAP and operate ≥300 hours/year (to determine equipment-leaks affected-source applicability)?
Will any recovered free product be returned to the manufacturing process (if yes, that material may no longer be subject to this subpart)?
Is the site a gasoline service station, farm, residential site, or an R&D facility covered by CAA §112(c)(7) (which would be exemptions under §63.7881(b)(4)–(6))?
Have you prepared or can you prepare the written documentation required to support a <1 Mg determination (methodology, data) if claiming the de minimis exemption per §63.7881(c)(2)?

If claiming a unit exemption under §63.7886(d) (total HAP in exempted units <1 Mg/yr), have you identified and marked or notified the Administrator of the exempted units and prepared the initial HAP quantity determination?

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA’s sole key reason is that reuse of soil as backfill without any cleanup is not a “site remediation.” Our Answer includes the Subpart GGGGG applicability condition that the activity must 'clean up a remediation material' (and asks whether the activity qualifies as a site remediation per §63.7957), so the EPA rationale is captured by the provided criteria/checklist."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Organic Liquid Distribution (Non-Gasoline) Operations

criteria.criterion: if you own or operate an organic liquid distribution (OLD) operation that is located at, or is part of, a major source of HAP emissions, then you are subject to this subpart
if the organic liquid distribution operation is located at a research and development facility (as consistent with CAA section 112(c)(7)), then you are not subject to this subpart

if the activities and equipment used to process, store, or transfer organic liquids are at oil and natural gas production field facilities or natural gas transmission and storage facilities (as defined in the referenced subparts), then those activities are not subject to this subpart

if the affected source is the collection of activities and equipment used to distribute organic liquids into, out of, or within a major source (including storage tanks, transfer racks, equipment leak components associated with those tanks/racks/pipelines, all transport vehicles while loading/unloading at transfer racks, and all containers while loading/unloading at transfer racks), then those items are part of the affected source and subject to this subpart

if storage tanks, transfer racks, transport vehicles, containers, or equipment leak components are non-permanent and are used in special situation distribution loading and unloading operations (such as maintenance or upset liquids management), then those items are excluded from the affected source and are not subject to this subpart

if the liquid involved meets the subpart's definition of organic liquid (for example, non-crude/non-condensate liquids or liquids containing ≥5 percent by weight of the organic HAP listed in Table 1, or crude oils/condensates downstream of the first custody transfer), then the subpart's applicability tests for OLD operations may apply

if transfer equipment and operations are physically separate (do not share common piping, valves, and other equipment), then they are considered separate transfer racks for purposes of determining affected source coverage

checklist: Is the plant a major source of HAP emissions (meeting the regulatory definition/thresholds for a major source)?
Are the activities in question part of an organic liquid distribution (OLD) operation (storing, transferring, blending, packaging organic liquids) as defined in the subpart?

Do the liquids transferred meet the subpart's definition of 'organic liquid' (e.g., ≥5% by weight organic HAP, or crude/condensate downstream of first custody transfer), and are they not excluded liquids (e.g., gasoline, diesel) listed in §63.2406?

Are the transfers performed at a designated transfer rack (i.e., a single system used to load/unload transport vehicles or containers with shared piping/valves), or are they ad hoc/non-permanent hose/valve connections?
Are the containers and hoses/valves permanent or non-permanent/portable, and are they being used in routine distribution versus 'special situation' operations (maintenance, upset, liquid management)?

Are the container-to-container and truck-to-container transfers routine, recurring distribution activities (subject to control), or are they temporary/special-situation operations that would qualify for the non-permanent equipment exclusion in §63.2338(c)(2)?
Are the transfers occurring at an oil and natural gas production field facility or a natural gas transmission and storage facility (which are excluded under §63.2334(c))?
Are the transfer operations located at a research and development facility claiming the R&D exclusion in §63.2334(b)?

If transfers occur at a transfer rack, what is the facility's total actual annual facility-level organic liquid loading volume and does it meet the Table 2 loading-volume criteria for control (verify against Table 2 to determine whether transfer racks/storage tanks are subject to control)?
Are the containers involved acting as transport vehicles (cargo tanks/tank cars) subject to DOT/vapor-tight definitions, or are they portable containers/drums as defined in §63.2406?

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA noted two key points: the activities meet the transfer rack definition (so subpart EEEE may apply) and they may be exempt if they qualify as 'special situation' operations using non‑permanent equipment. The submitted criteria/checklist explicitly include the transfer rack definition/coverage and the non‑permanent/special‑situation exclusion (§63.2338(c)(2)), so both key reasons from the EPA notes are captured."}

candidates.title: Subpart MM

criteria.criterion: If your smelt dissolving tank is an affected source under Subpart MM and is equipped with a wet scrubber, then you must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate a CPMS that can determine and record the pressure drop across the scrubber and the scrubbing liquid flow rate at least once every successive 15-minute period.

If you wish to establish operating limits for monitoring parameters under Subpart MM, then those operating limits must be established during the initial or periodic performance test or be based on values recorded during previous performance tests (or from additional performance tests conducted for that purpose) using the test methods and procedures required in the subpart.

If your smelt dissolving tank uses a dynamic wet scrubber that operates at ambient pressure or is a low-energy entrainment scrubber where fan speed does not vary, then you may use fan amperage or fan RPM measurement as an alternative to pressure drop measurement.

If you propose monitoring alternative control device operating parameters in place of the parameters specified in the subpart, then you must obtain prior written approval by the Administrator and include the manner in which the parameter operating limit is to be set.

candidates.title: Subpart TTTTT

criteria.criterion: If a wet scrubber is applied to meet any PM, PM10, chlorine, HCl, or dioxins/furans emission limit under Subpart TTTTT, then you must maintain the hourly average pressure drop and scrubber liquid flow rate at or above the minimum level established during the initial or subsequent performance test.

If a wet scrubber is subject to operating limits for pressure drop and scrubber water flow rate under Subpart TTTTT, then you must establish site-specific operating limits by measuring and recording pressure drop and flow with the CPMS at least every 15 minutes during each run of the particulate matter performance test and taking the lowest average individual pressure drop and flow from the compliant runs.

If a wet scrubber is subject to the operating limits in § 63.9890(b), then you must at all times monitor the hourly average pressure drop and liquid flow rate using a CPMS according to the applicable CPMS requirements.

candidates.title: Subpart RRRRR

criteria.criterion: If a wet scrubber is subject to performance testing under Subpart RRRRR, then site-specific operating limits for pressure drop and scrubber water flow rate must be established as the lowest average pressure drop and lowest average scrubber water flow rate corresponding to any of the three compliant test runs (measured every 15 minutes and averaged per run).

If you want to change (lower or revise) the operating limits for any air pollution control device under Subpart RRRRR, then you must submit written notification to the Administrator to conduct a new performance test, conduct the performance test to demonstrate compliance, and establish revised operating limits according to the applicable procedures.

If a rod-deck venturi scrubber is applied to an indurating furnace (specific to that equipment), then you may establish a lower average pressure drop operating limit using historical average pressure drop data from a certified performance test completed on or after December 18, 2002, provided the corresponding PM concentration from that test meets the applicable limit.

checklist: Confirm which NESHAP subpart(s) your smelt dissolving tank and its scrubber are regulated under (Subpart MM, Subpart TTTTT, Subpart RRRRR, or other).
Verify whether the scrubber was used to meet PM, PM10, chlorine, HCl, or dioxins/furans limits (triggers Subpart TTTTT requirements).

Determine whether an initial or subsequent performance test(s) exists for your scrubber and obtain the test reports showing the 1-hour or run-average pressure drop and scrubbing liquid flow rate values.
If no suitable performance test exists, confirm whether you are willing/able to conduct a new performance test per the applicable subpart procedures to establish revised operating limits.

If your dynamic wet scrubber operates at ambient pressure or is a low-energy entrainment scrubber with constant fan speed, verify whether fan amperage or RPM monitoring is an acceptable alternative to pressure drop for your unit.

Confirm CPMS availability and capability: that pressure-drop and flow monitors meet the accuracy and recording-frequency requirements specified by the applicable subpart and that hourly/15-minute averaging as required can be produced.

If you plan to request alternative monitoring parameters or a change without a new performance test, prepare documentation for prior written approval by the Administrator (description of control device, test history, proposed parameter and manner to set limits).

Check whether any subpart-specific allowances (e.g., historical test data for specified scrubbers) apply to your equipment type and whether those historical tests meet the emission limits required by the subpart.

judge_text: {"score": 2, "reason": "EPA's key reason—that 40 CFR 63.864(j) only allows setting new/expanded operating limits after a performance test at the new limit—is captured by the MM criterion citing 40 CFR 63.864(j)(1),(j)(2) (and related CPMS/alternative-parameter criteria are also included)."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Steel Pickling—Hydrochloric Acid Pickling and Hydrochloric Acid Regeneration Plants

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator operates a new, reconstructed, or existing steel pickling facility or hydrochloric acid regeneration plant, then the facility is subject to the monitoring requirements of Subpart CCC.

If a wet scrubber is used as the emission control device, then the owner or operator must install, operate, and maintain systems to measure and record the scrubber makeup water flow rate and, if applicable, recirculation water flow rate, with these flow rates monitored continuously and recorded at least once per shift while the scrubber is operating.

If a wet scrubber's minimum makeup and recirculation flow rates were established during the performance test(s), then operation of the wet scrubber with excursions of those flow rates below the performance-test-established minimum values will require initiation of corrective action as specified in the maintenance requirements of the subpart.

If an emission control device other than a wet scrubber is used, then the owner or operator must install, operate, and maintain systems for measurement and recording of the appropriate operating parameters for that device.

If performance testing is conducted for a wet scrubber to establish operating parameter values, then during the performance test each operating parameter must be monitored continuously and recorded with sufficient frequency to establish a representative average value but no less frequently than once every 15 minutes.

If monitoring devices are used, then each monitoring device must be certified by the manufacturer to be accurate to within 5 percent and must be calibrated in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions at least annually.

If the owner or operator fails to record each of the operating parameters listed for a wet scrubber (makeup and recirculation flow rates), then that failure is a violation of the monitoring requirements of this subpart.

If the facility is subject to the subpart, then the owner or operator must conduct performance tests either annually or on an alternative schedule approved by the permitting authority but no less frequently than every 2.5 years or twice per title V permit term.

If subject to the subpart, then the owner or operator must keep records (including scrubber makeup and recirculation flow rates, calibration and manufacturer certification, performance test results, and maintenance records) for 5 years, and the most recent 2 years of records must be kept on site.

checklist: Confirm whether each of your two continuous pickling lines and the acid regeneration plant meet the regulatory definitions of 'continuous pickling line' and 'hydrochloric acid regeneration plant' (40 CFR 63.1156).
Determine whether a wet scrubber is used as the emission control device on each pickling line and/or on the acid regeneration plant.
If wet scrubbers are present, confirm whether they operate with recirculation (identify makeup and recirculation flow paths separately).
Document whether initial and subsequent performance tests have been conducted for each emission control device and the dates/frequencies of those tests.
Obtain the performance-test-established minimum scrubber makeup water flow rates and minimum recirculation water flow rates (site-specific values established during testing).
Verify how the scrubber flow rates are currently monitored (device type) and whether monitoring is continuous.

Verify the current recording frequency for scrubber makeup and recirculation flow rates during operation (must be at least once per shift under normal operation; during performance tests values must be recorded no less frequently than every 15 minutes).
Confirm that each monitoring device is certified by the manufacturer to be accurate within ±5% and that there is a calibration schedule and records showing calibration at least annually.

Check whether procedures for initiating corrective action (and the operation & maintenance plan) exist, who is the responsible maintenance official, and that corrective action initiation occurs within the timeframe required by the maintenance requirements.

Confirm that records required by the subpart (performance tests, monitoring data, calibration and certification, maintenance and corrective actions) are retained for 5 years and that the most recent 2 years are available on site.

Confirm whether the operation and maintenance plan for each emission control device has been prepared and incorporated by reference into the facility's Title V permit, and that it contains the minimum scrubber-specific elements (pressure-drop monitoring once per shift, inspection intervals, cleaning/repairs, etc.).

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA Notes hinge on two key points—continuous monitoring of scrubber flow rates and that recording is only required once per shift. Those specific requirements are explicitly captured in the provided criteria (continuous monitoring and ‘recorded at least once per shift’ plus related performance-test monitoring frequency), so the key reasons in the EPA Notes are present."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Miscellaneous Coating Manufacturing

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate miscellaneous coating manufacturing operations that (1) are located at or are part of a major source of HAP, (2) manufacture coatings, (3) process, use, or produce HAP, and (4) are not part of an affected source under another subpart, then you are subject to this subpart.
If a unit at the facility is a process vessel used to manufacture coatings, then that process vessel is part of the miscellaneous coating manufacturing affected source.

If the vessel or operation is part of affiliated operations located at an affected source subject to subparts GG, KK, JJJJ, MMMM, or SSSS, then the requirements of this subpart do not apply to that vessel/operation.

If a process vessel is stationary and has capacity greater than or equal to 250 gallons, then you may elect to comply using the emissions averaging alternative for stationary process vessels at existing sources.
If a process vessel is stationary and you elect emissions averaging, then all stationary process vessels in the averaging group must be equipped with a tightly-fitting vented cover.

If a process vessel is less than 250 gallons or is not a stationary process vessel, then it is not eligible for the emissions averaging alternative that applies to stationary process vessels >=250 gallons.

If you produce coatings with HAP content less than 0.05 kg per kg product (approximately 5 weight percent) and elect the alternative, then you may comply with the 5 weight percent HAP limit alternative for process vessels at your affected source.

checklist: Is the facility a major source of HAPs as defined in Clean Air Act section 112(a)?
Do you manufacture coatings as defined in 40 CFR part 63 (verify definition in §63.8105)?
Does the mixer/process vessel process, use, or produce HAPs (identify which HAPs and quantities)?

Is the 125-gallon mixer used as a process vessel in the coating manufacturing steps (mixing ingredients to make coatings) or used only for other purposes (e.g., R&D, QA/QC, modifying purchased coatings)?
Is the mixer part of or owned by an affected source already covered under subparts GG, KK, JJJJ, MMMM, or SSSS (affiliated operations)?
Is the mixer stationary or portable (can it be moved without disassembly)?
What is the vessel capacity in gallons (confirm 125 gallons) and is it less than 250 gallons?
Do you plan to use the emissions averaging alternative (note: only applies to stationary vessels >=250 gal)?
Are the coatings produced in that vessel below 0.05 kg/kg (5 wt%) HAP such that the 5 weight percent alternative might be elected?
If considering emissions averaging, do all vessels in the proposed averaging group meet the requirement to have tightly-fitting vented covers?
Is the mixer used in automatic cleaning operations (which are subject to emission limits) or only manual cleaning?
Is the operation a research and development facility or otherwise excluded under §63.7985(d) (e.g., QA/QC lab, ancillary equipment, or modifying purchased coatings)?

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"The EPA reasons (mixer is not a process vessel and capacity <250 gallons/portable) are reflected in the answer: the criteria require the unit be a process vessel to be part of the affected source and explicitly address vessel capacity and stationary vs. portable status (125 gal <250 and portability are in the checklist), so the key reasons are captured."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Site Remediation

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a facility at which you conduct a site remediation that (1) cleans up a remediation material, (2) is co-located with one or more other stationary sources that emit HAP and meet an affected-source definition in another subpart, and (3) your facility is a major source of HAP, then the site remediation at your facility is subject to this subpart.
If the site remediation only cleans up material that does not contain any of the HAP listed in Table 1 of this subpart, then the site remediation is not subject to this subpart.
If the site remediation is conducted at a gasoline service station to clean up remediation material from a leaking underground storage tank, then the site remediation is not subject to this subpart.
If the site remediation is conducted at a farm or residential site, then the site remediation is not subject to this subpart.
If the site remediation is conducted at a research and development facility that meets the requirements under CAA section 112(c)(7), then the site remediation is not subject to this subpart.

If the total quantity of the HAP listed in Table 1 contained in remediation material removed during all site remediations at your facility is less than 1 megagram annually and you prepare and maintain written documentation of the methodology and data used, then the site remediation activities are not subject to the requirements of this subpart except for the recordkeeping requirement.

If all remediation activities at your facility subject to this subpart are completed and you notify the Administrator in writing that all remediation activities subject to this subpart are completed, then the site remediation is not subject to the requirements of this subpart (but you must maintain records of compliance).

If a unit at your site is a process vent, remediation material management unit, equipment component meeting the equipment-leak criteria, or a pressure relief device in remediation material service, then that unit is an affected source subject to the subpart's requirements for affected sources.

If an equipment component contains or contacts remediation material with total HAP (Table 1) equal to or greater than 10 percent by weight and is intended to operate 300 hours or more per calendar year in remediation material service, then that equipment component is part of the affected-source equipment-leaks group; if either condition is not met, it is not part of the affected-source equipment-leaks group.

If the potentially regulated unit(s) are located on contiguous or adjoining property under common control (including owned, leased, or operated by the same entity, parent, or subsidiary), then those units are considered part of your facility for purposes of this subpart; if they are owned by a different company and not under common control, they are a different facility.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Off-Site Waste and Recovery Operations (cross-reference guidance)

criteria.criterion: If you implement this subpart using cross-referenced sections in subpart DD, then any reference in subpart DD to 'HAP listed in Table 1 of this subpart' should be read as referring to Table 1 of Subpart GGGGG for your site remediation.
If you implement this subpart using cross-referenced sections in subpart DD, then any reference in subpart DD to 'off-site material' should be read as 'remediation material' as defined in §63.7957.

checklist: Do you legally own or operate the facility where the remediation units are located, or does another legally distinct entity retain ownership and operational responsibility under a Consent Order?
Are the remediation units located on property that is contiguous or adjoining and under common control with your other operations (ownership/lease/operator relationship)?
Do you (or the other entity on-site) conduct the remediation activities, or are all remediation actions conducted by the other entity without your operational control?
Do the remediation materials being managed contain any of the HAP listed in Table 1 of Subpart GGGGG?
Is the facility a major source of HAP (single HAP ≥ 10 tpy or combined HAPs ≥ 25 tpy) when you aggregate emissions as required for a major-source determination?
Are the remediation units co-located with one or more other stationary sources at the facility that emit HAP and meet an affected-source definition in another Part 63 subpart?

What is the total annual mass of Table 1 HAP removed/handled in all site remediations at the facility (is it < 1 megagram/year)? Do you have written documentation of the methodology and data if claiming the <1 Mg exemption?
Have all remediation activities subject to Subpart GGGGG been completed and, if so, has the Administrator been notified in writing?
For equipment components: do any components contain remediation material with total Table 1 HAP ≥ 10% by weight, and do such components operate 300 hours or more per calendar year?
Are any of the remediation units (process vents, tanks/impoundments/containers, separators, transfer systems, pressure relief devices) the types of affected sources listed in §63.7882(a)?

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's sole key reason — that Boeing (the other company) retains legal responsibility for the remediation activities and thus the site remediation NESHAP does not apply to the permittee — is captured in OUR ANSWER by the criterion/checklist items addressing legal ownership/operation and whether another legally distinct entity retains ownership/operational responsibility (including reference to Consent Orders) and the facility/common-control definition."}

candidates.title: Hazardous waste incinerators (Subpart EEE)

criteria.criterion: If the hazardous waste combustor includes more than one combustion chamber (for example a rotary kiln and a secondary combustion chamber), then you must measure the temperature of each combustion chamber and establish a minimum hourly rolling average combustion chamber temperature limit for each chamber based on the average of the performance test run averages.

If you are establishing combustion chamber temperature limits, then you must measure temperature at a location that best represents, as practicable, the bulk gas temperature in the combustion zone and document that measurement location in the performance test plan.

If you wish to waive an operating parameter limit (such as the minimum combustion chamber temperature), then you must submit an application to the Administrator (not later than with the comprehensive performance test plan) that documents why neither that operating parameter limit nor an alternative limit is needed to ensure compliance and obtain Administrator approval before operating without the limit.

If the automatic waste feed cutoff (AWFCO) is triggered by an exceedance of the minimum combustion chamber temperature operating limit, then you may not ramp down the waste feed (ramp down is prohibited when AWFCO is triggered by minimum combustion chamber temperature).

If the area contains controlled flame combustion of hazardous waste, then that area meets the definition of a combustion chamber and is subject to the per-chamber monitoring and operating parameter requirements.

If operating parameter limits for a given parameter are derived from independent performance tests performed at different times or for different standards, then the most stringent limit for that parameter derived from those independent tests applies.

checklist: Confirm whether the rotary kiln and the secondary combustion chamber each contain controlled flame combustion of hazardous waste (i.e., whether each is a separate 'combustion chamber').
Determine whether hazardous waste is fed to both the rotary kiln and the secondary combustion chamber, and the locations where waste is fed.
Verify whether previous or planned comprehensive performance tests measured temperature and other operating parameters for each chamber simultaneously or separately.

Document proposed temperature measurement locations for each combustion chamber (locations must represent the bulk gas temperature in the combustion zone) and include them in the performance test plan.

Check whether minimum combustion chamber temperature is currently interlocked to the AWFCO for either chamber and whether AWFCO ramp-down procedures would be triggered by a min-temperature exceedance.

If seeking to waive the minimum combustion chamber temperature limit, assemble data and justification and prepare an application to the Administrator to submit with the comprehensive performance test plan (include technical data showing the limit is not needed or that an alternative provides equivalent assurance).
Confirm timing: the waiver/alternative monitoring application must be submitted not later than with the comprehensive performance test plan.

Verify hazardous waste residence time calculations and that any changes in design/operation are documented (per performance test plan and Notification of Compliance) because changes may require new testing or limits.
Identify whether any previously approved alternative monitoring or waivers exist for this source (and obtain the Administrator's written approval if operating without the limit).

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's key reason — the kiln and secondary chamber are separate combustion chambers and therefore a minimum combustion chamber temperature limit is required for each — is explicitly captured (see criteria citing 40 CFR 63.1209(j)(1) and the combustion chamber definition 40 CFR 63.1201(a)), plus related per-chamber measurement and waiver procedures are included."}

candidates.title: Surface Coating of Metal Furniture

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a new, reconstructed, or existing affected source (as defined in §63.4882) for surface coating of metal furniture and that affected source is a major source, is located at a major source, or is part of a major source of HAP emissions, then the source is subject to this subpart.
If the surface coating uses only coatings, thinners, and cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP, then the surface coating is not subject to this subpart (exemption).

If you claim the exemption that materials contain no organic HAP, then the determination that coatings, thinners, and cleaning materials contain no organic HAP must be made following the procedures in §63.4941 (e.g., Method 311, Method 24, or reliable supplier/manufacturer formulation data), and if that condition is met then the source is not subject under the §63.4881(c)(1) exemption.

If the surface coating meets any of the criteria in §63.4881(c)(2)–(6) (for example, coating of metal components of wood furniture covered by subpart JJ; research or laboratory facilities; janitorial/building/facility maintenance; coating only small items; on-site repair/maintenance not for commerce unless HAP emissions reach major-source thresholds; or coatings at Armed Forces installations), then the surface coating is not subject to this subpart.

If your operations include the collection of items listed in §63.4882(b) used for surface coating of metal furniture (all coating operations, storage/mixing vessels for coatings/thinners/cleaning materials, conveying equipment/piping, and storage/handling of coating-related wastes), then those items constitute the affected source to which this subpart's applicability and requirements apply (subjectness still depends on major-source status per §63.4881(b)).

checklist: Do you perform surface coating of metal furniture (see examples in §63.4881(a)(2))? (i.e., application of coatings to metal furniture or metal furniture components using spray, dip, etc.)
Is your facility a major source of HAPs (potential to emit ≥ 9.07 Mg/yr of any single HAP or ≥ 22.68 Mg/yr combined HAP)?

Does the plant own or operate an affected source as defined in §63.4882(b) (identify whether you have coating operations, storage/mixing vessels for coatings/thinners/cleaning materials, conveying pumps/piping/equipment, and waste handling for coating operations)?

Do any of the coatings, thinners, or cleaning materials you currently use contain any organic HAP? (Verify using supplier/manufacturer formulation data or testing per §63.4941(a) — e.g., Method 311, Method 24, or approved alternatives.)
If you claim materials contain no organic HAP, do you have supporting documentation/tests for each coating, thinner, and cleaning material in the condition received (see §63.4941(a)–(e))?
Are any coatings applied to metal components of wood furniture that are part of an operation subject to subpart JJ (wood furniture NESHAP)?

Are any of your coating activities research/laboratory, janitorial/building/facility maintenance, coating only small items (knobs/hinges/screws), on-site repair not for commerce, or performed at Armed Forces installations (exempt categories in §63.4881(c)(2)–(6))?
If you previously reclaimed or reused cleaning materials, were those materials shown to comply with the compliant-material criteria in their condition as received (per §63.4941(e))?

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's sole rationale was that the facility meets 40 CFR 63.4881(c)(1) (use of coatings/thinners/cleaning materials containing no organic HAP). OUR ANSWER explicitly lists that exemption (§63.4881(c)(1)) and the required verification procedures (§63.4941/Method 311/24 and supplier data) in both criteria and checklist, so the key reasons are captured."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Secondary Lead Smelting

criteria.criterion: If your facility recycles lead-bearing scrap material into elemental lead or lead alloys by smelting, then your facility meets the definition of a 'secondary lead smelter' and can be subject to this subpart.

If you own or operate at a secondary lead smelter any affected source (blast, reverberatory, rotary, or electric furnaces; refining kettles; agglomerating furnaces; dryers; process fugitive emissions sources; buildings containing lead-bearing materials; or fugitive dust sources), then you are subject to this subpart.
If you are a primary lead processor, lead refiner, or lead remelter, then you are not subject to this subpart.

If your affected sources have process vents, then you are subject to this subpart and must meet the lead compound emissions limits specified for process vents (existing sources: ≤1.0 mg lead/dscm per vent and a facility flow-weighted average ≤0.20 mg lead/dscm; new sources: ≤0.20 mg lead/dscm).

If you meet the applicability criteria in §63.541 (i.e., you operate affected sources at a secondary lead smelter), then you are also subject to Title V permitting requirements under 40 CFR parts 70 or 71.

If you are subject to the emissions limits in §63.543 and you use baghouses or similar particulate controls for those sources, then you are subject to the baghouse standard operating procedures, bag leak detection, inspection, and monitoring requirements in §63.548.

checklist: Does the facility recycle lead-bearing scrap into elemental lead or lead alloys by smelting (i.e., perform smelting: chemical reduction in high-temperature furnaces >980 °C)?

Which equipment and process units are present at the facility (check for blast, reverberatory, rotary, electric furnaces; refining kettles; agglomerating furnaces; dryers; battery breakers; dryer transition pieces)?
Does the facility have buildings containing lead-bearing materials, process fugitive emissions sources, or fugitive dust sources (storage piles, material handling, roadways, transfer points)?
Is the facility a primary lead processor, lead refiner, or lead remelter (if yes, note potential exemption)?

Are there process vents or stacks associated with the listed affected sources, and what are the vents' flow rates and measured lead compound concentrations (mg lead per dry standard cubic meter) for each vent?
Is the facility a new or reconstructed source that commenced construction or reconstruction after May 19, 2011?

What is the facility-wide flow-weighted average lead concentration across process vents (12-month rolling average, calculated monthly) and the individual vent concentrations compared to the limits (1.0 mg/dscm per vent; 0.20 mg/dscm flow-weighted average; new source limit 0.20 mg/dscm)?

What air pollution control devices are used (baghouses, HEPA secondary filters, wet scrubbers, wet electrostatic precipitators), and are bag leak detection systems, CEMS, or digital differential pressure monitors installed or planned?
If baghouses are used, do you have (or will you prepare) a standard operating procedures manual covering inspection, maintenance, bag leak detection, and corrective action as required?

If using wet scrubbers for particulate/metal control, can you monitor and record pressure drop and water flow rate at least hourly and maintain levels no lower than 30% below the values measured during the initial performance test?

Do you have or plan to perform the required performance testing and monitoring schedules for lead, total hydrocarbons, and dioxins/furans (initial and periodic tests, annual tests, and CEMS if applicable)?
Does the facility currently hold a Title V operating permit (or is the facility subject to permitting under 40 CFR parts 70 or 71)?

judge_text: {"score": 2, "reason": "EPA's key reason—that the facility recycles lead-bearing scrap material and thus meets the definition of a 'secondary lead smelter' subject to the Secondary Lead Smelting MACT—is directly captured by criterion 1 (and the corresponding checklist item) in OUR ANSWER (40 CFR 63.542)."}

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If you are the owner or operator of an affected source subject to this part, then you must maintain files of all information required by this part and retain those files for at least 5 years with the most recent 2 years of data retained on site.

candidates.title: Storage Vessel Recordkeeping (Subpart WW)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate storage vessels subject to Subpart WW, then you must keep a record of vessel dimensions, capacity analysis, and identification of the liquid stored for as long as the liquid is stored.
If you operate external floating roofs subject to Subpart WW, then you must keep inspection records including, for EFR seal gap measurements, the raw data obtained and any calculations performed.
If records are required under paragraphs (b), (c), or (d) of §63.1065, then those records must be kept for at least 5 years and be readily accessible within 24 hours.

candidates.title: Subpart DD recordkeeping (tank controls)

criteria.criterion: If your source is subject to Subpart DD, then you must comply with the recordkeeping requirements in §63.10 of subpart A as specified in Table 2 of Subpart DD.

If you use an external floating roof to comply with the tank control requirements in Subpart DD, then you must prepare and maintain records for each seal gap inspection that include the date of measurements, the raw data obtained, and the calculations of the total gap surface area.

candidates.title: Recordkeeping for Storage Vessels (Subpart HHHHHHH)

criteria.criterion: If you are subject to Subpart HHHHHHH and have internal or external floating roof storage vessels, then you must maintain the records required in §63.1065 of Subpart WW (including raw data for EFR seal gap measurements).

If you are subject to Subpart HHHHHHH, then you must keep copies of each notification and report you submit to comply with that subpart and the current versions of specified site plans and monitoring plans.

checklist: Determine whether each storage tank is an external floating roof (EFR) tank and whether that tank is subject to Subpart WW, Subpart DD, or Subpart HHHHHHH.
Verify whether your facility is an "affected source" under Part 63 for the applicable NESHAP(s) (i.e., whether the tanks fall within the scope of the specific subpart standards).

For each EFR inspection, confirm that records include: tank identification, inspection date, description of any defects, description and date of repairs, and (for seal gap measurements) the raw measurement data and any calculations.

Confirm how long each type of record must be retained at your site: (a) vessel dimensions/capacity records retained as long as the liquid is stored; (b) inspection, seal gap, floating roof landing, and related records retained for at least 5 years; and (c) other Part 63 records retained for at least 5 years with the most recent 2 years on site.
Verify that your electronic records contain all elements of the raw data and calculations (dates, identifiers, measurement values, and any calculations) before discarding original field data sheets.
Confirm that records (electronic or hard copy) are maintained in a manner that allows them to be readily accessed within 24 hours.

If your facility is in a State with delegated authority, verify any state-specific retention or submission requirements and whether copies must be sent to the State or EPA Regional Office as described in §63.10(a)(4).
If you use Subpart DD or HHHHHHH to comply, confirm cross-references (e.g., that you are meeting §63.10 requirements invoked by §63.696(a) or maintaining §63.1065 records invoked by §63.11990(b)(5)).

However it does not capture the EPA QA guidance point in the notes that original field records themselves must be preserved (the answer suggests discarding originals after transferring data if electronic records contain the elements), so one key reason from the EPA NOTES is missing."}

candidates.title: Area Source Standards for Plating and Polishing Operations

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a plating and polishing facility that is an area source of HAP and the facility performs non-chromium electroplating, electroless plating, other non-electrolytic metal coating (e.g., chromate conversion coating), electroforming, electropolishing, or dry mechanical polishing and the facility uses or emits plating and polishing metal HAP, then the facility is subject to this subpart.

If a tank at your facility contains one or more plating and polishing metal HAP and is used for non-chromium electroplating, electroforming, electropolishing, electroless plating, or other non-electrolytic metal coating operations, then that tank is an affected source under this subpart.

If a process unit at your facility is subject to the requirements of 40 CFR part 63 subpart N (chromium electroplating or chromium anodizing), then this subpart (WWWWWW) does not apply to that process unit.

If any plating or polishing process uses process materials that contain cadmium, chromium, lead, or nickel (as the metal) in amounts less than 0.1 percent by weight and manganese in amounts less than 1.0 percent by weight (as used), then that plating or polishing process is not subject to this subpart.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Chromium Emissions from Hard and Decorative Chromium Electroplating and Chromium Anodizing Tanks

criteria.criterion: If a tank at your facility is a chromium electroplating or chromium anodizing tank at a facility performing hard chromium electroplating, decorative chromium electroplating, or chromium anodizing, then the provisions of this subpart apply to that tank (it is an affected source).

If the process in the tank meets the definition of chromium anodizing (use of a chromic acid solution with the part acting as the anode and electrical current applied) or chromium electroplating, then the tank meets the applicability in paragraph (a) and is subject to this subpart.

If a process tank is an etching tank or otherwise a tank in which neither chromium electroplating nor chromium anodizing is taking place (for example, a rinse, etching, or cleaning tank, or a tank containing a chromium solution but with no electrolytic process/current), then that tank is not subject to this subpart.
If the process unit is used for research and laboratory operations (as defined), then it is exempt from the provisions of this subpart while those operations are being performed.
If you are an owner or operator of an affected source subject to this subpart, then you must also comply with the requirements of subpart A of part 63 as identified in this subpart.

checklist: Determine whether the tank liquid is chromic acid (CrO3) or contains chromium compounds (check bath formulation or SDS).
Verify whether an electrical current is applied and whether the workpiece acts as the anode (i.e., confirm whether the process is electrolytic and whether the part is anode vs cathode).
Determine whether the process is being used to etch/clean (non‑electrolytic etching) versus performing chromium anodizing or chromium electroplating (compare operation to 40 CFR 63.341 definitions).
If the tank is electrolytic with chromic acid and the part is the anode, treat it as possible chromium anodizing and evaluate applicability to Subpart N (63.340(a)).

If the process is not chromium electroplating/anodizing, determine whether it is non-chromium electroplating, electroless plating, electropolishing, electroforming, other non-electrolytic metal coating, thermal spraying, or dry mechanical polishing listed in 63.11504/63.11505.
Estimate the facility potential to emit (PTE) for each HAP and combined HAP to determine area source vs major source status (area source if single HAP PTE < 10 tpy and total HAP PTE < 25 tpy).

For processes not clearly excluded, determine the plating and polishing metal HAP content of bath/process materials (use testing, engineering estimate, or SDS) to see if Cd/Cr/Pb/Ni < 0.1% and Mn < 1.0% which would exempt under 63.11505(d)(6).
Confirm whether the tank/process is used for research/laboratory or strictly educational activities or for repair operations, which can be exemptions under the respective subparts.
If the tank may be subject to Subpart N, review whether any prior designation or controls apply and whether Subpart A requirements also apply per 63.340(b).

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA’s key reason is that the process meets the regulatory definition of electropolishing and thus the Area Source Plating and Polishing standard applies. OUR ANSWER explicitly lists electropolishing among the covered operations and includes checklist steps to determine whether the process meets the electropolishing definition, so the EPA rationale is captured."}

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If a facility is subject to Subpart MMMMMM then the Subpart A provisions in §§63.1 through 63.5 and §§63.11 through 63.16 apply to that facility.

candidates.title: Area Sources: Carbon Black Production

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a carbon black production facility that is an area source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions then you are subject to this subpart.

If the carbon black production affected source was constructed or reconstructed on or before April 4, 2007 then it is an existing source; if constructed or reconstructed after April 4, 2007 then it is a new source.
If you are a research and development facility as defined in CAA section 112(c)(7) then this subpart does not apply to you.
If you own or operate an area source subject to this subpart then you must obtain a permit under 40 CFR part 70 or 40 CFR part 71.
If you are subject to this subpart then you must meet all the requirements in §63.1103(f) of subpart YY.
If you need definitions for terms in this subpart then the definitions in §§63.1101 and 63.1103(f)(2) apply.

candidates.title: Source category-specific applicability, definitions, and requirements

criteria.criterion: If a carbon black production process unit is located at a major source (as defined in section 112(a) of the Act) then the affected source comprises each carbon black production process unit and associated waste management units, maintenance wastewater, and equipment that contain or contact HAP.
If the process produces carbon black by the furnace, thermal, acetylene decomposition, or lampblack processes then it meets the definition of carbon black production for this subpart.

If the HAP concentration of a carbon black production main unit filter process vent or other carbon black process vent (as determined using the process-vent applicability procedures) is equal to or greater than 260 parts per million by volume then, beginning by the compliance dates, the vent must be controlled by a flare meeting subpart SS requirements or by venting through a closed vent system to control devices achieving 98 weight‑percent reduction (or to 20 ppmv), as specified in the carbon black Table 8 requirements.

If a carbon black process vent subject to Table 8 is instead routed to a boiler or process heater for use as fuel gas then, beginning by the compliance dates, annual boiler/process heater tune-up requirements apply.

checklist: Determine whether the facility is an area source or a major source of HAPs (i.e., verify whether the facility meets the section 112(a) major-source thresholds).

Verify whether your tire-reclamation process produces carbon black by furnace, thermal, acetylene decomposition, or lampblack methods (confirm process type and whether the recovered material is carbon black).
Confirm whether the facility is a research and development facility as defined in CAA 112(c)(7).
If subject to Subpart MMMMMM, confirm construction/reconstruction date of the affected source(s) relative to April 4, 2007 to determine new vs existing source status.

Measure or determine the HAP concentration (ppmv) of the main unit filter process vent and other carbon black process vents (and whether vents are before/after the dryer) using the process‑vent applicability procedures referenced in 63.1103(f)(3)(iv)/(v).

Determine whether any process vent emissions are routed to a boiler/process heater (fuel gas) or to a closed vent/flare/control device; if routed to boiler/process heater, note that annual tune-up requirements apply.

If subject to Subpart MMMMMM, verify permitting obligations under 40 CFR part 70 or 71 and document associated waste management units, maintenance wastewater, and equipment that contain or contact HAP for the affected source determination.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Surface Coating of Plastic Parts and Products

criteria.criterion: If you choose the emission rate with add-on controls option for any coating operation, then you must include emissions reductions achieved by emission capture systems and add-on controls and meet the operating limits in § 63.4492 (except for solvent recovery systems using liquid-liquid material balances) and the work practice standards in § 63.4493.

If you use an add-on control device that is not a solvent recovery system (for example a boiler receiving captured emissions), then you must calculate the organic HAP emission reduction by applying the emission capture system efficiency and the add-on control device destruction or removal efficiency to the mass of organic HAP in the materials routed to that control device, and assume zero efficiency during any deviations specified in § 63.4563(c) or (d) unless approved otherwise.

If you use the emission rate with add-on controls option and a controlled coating operation (other than solvent recovery with liquid-liquid balances), then you must establish operating limits for the emission capture and add-on control systems during the performance tests required in § 63.4560 and meet the established operating limits at all times thereafter as required by § 63.4492 and § 63.4561(b).

If you use an add-on control device other than those listed in Table 1 to this subpart, or if you wish to monitor an alternative parameter and comply with a different operating limit, then you must apply to the Administrator for approval of alternative monitoring under § 63.8(f).

If a device reduces pollution in an air stream by destruction or removal before discharge to the atmosphere, then it meets the subpart's definition of an 'add-on control' (and may be considered for the emission rate with add-on controls option, subject to the subpart's testing, operating limits, and monitoring requirements).

If you use a solvent recovery system for which you conduct liquid-liquid material balances according to § 63.4561(j), then you may determine emission reduction using the liquid-liquid material balance procedures in § 63.4561(j) and are excepted from the operating limit requirements of § 63.4492 that otherwise apply to add-on control devices.

checklist: Decide whether each of your two plastic parts coating lines will be evaluated under the emission rate with add-on controls option (vs. the compliant-material or emission-rate-without-controls options).

Confirm that methanol in your coatings/thinners/cleaning materials is an organic HAP to be included in the emission calculations, and compile monthly data: volume used, density, and mass fraction of organic HAP for each coating, thinner/additive, and cleaning material.
Confirm whether the boiler will receive captured coating emissions (i.e., emissions are routed from a capture system to the boiler) and document the capture system configuration.

Check Table 1 of Subpart PPPP to determine whether the boiler (or the specific type of combustion device you plan to use) is listed among approved add-on control device types; if Table 1 is not definitive, plan to request alternative monitoring approval under § 63.8(f).

Plan and budget to perform the required performance test(s) (per § 63.4560) to measure capture efficiency and the boiler's organic HAP destruction or removal efficiency (DRE) and to establish operating limits per § 63.4567.

Verify you can continuously monitor and record the parameter(s) required to demonstrate compliance with the operating limits established for the capture system and the boiler (or obtain Administrator approval for alternative monitoring if needed).

Prepare to calculate monthly organic HAP emission reductions using Equation 1 procedures (capture efficiency and DRE) for non-solvent-recovery controls and to compute the rolling 12‑month emission rate per § 63.4561(f)–(m); include protocol for treating deviations (assume zero efficiency unless approved otherwise).

If you intend to use solvent recovery instead of the boiler, verify you can install and maintain the required device to measure cumulative volatile organic matter recovered monthly and perform the liquid-liquid material balances per § 63.4561(j)(1)–(7).

Develop and maintain the required work practice plan and initial-compliance documentation for coating operations using add-on controls (per §§ 63.4493 and 63.4561(c), (n)), and retain the records required to demonstrate compliance.

Confirm that operation and maintenance of the boiler and any capture/monitoring equipment will be conducted in a manner consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices as required by § 63.4500(b).

candidates.title: Subpart PPPPP

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an engine test cell/stand located at a major source of HAP emissions then the affected source is subject to this subpart.
If construction of the affected source commenced after May 14, 2002 then the affected source is a new affected source under this subpart.
If reconstruction of the affected source (as defined in §63.2) was commenced after May 14, 2002 then the affected source is a reconstructed affected source under this subpart.

If changes to an existing affected source were made primarily for the purpose of complying with revisions to engine testing requirements under 40 CFR parts 80, 86, 89, 90, 91, or 92 then those changes are not considered a modification or reconstruction for purposes of this subpart.

If the changes include passive measurement and control instrumentation and electronics then those passive instrumentation and electronics are not included as part of any affected source reconstruction evaluation.

If any portion of a new or reconstructed affected source is used exclusively for testing internal combustion engines with rated power of less than 25 hp then that portion does not have to meet the requirements of this subpart except for the initial notification requirement in §63.9345(b).

If any portion of the affected source is used exclusively for testing combustion turbine engines, rocket engines, research and teaching activities that are not commercial, or for testing/evaluating fuels, transmissions, or electronics then that portion does not have to meet the requirements of this subpart.

candidates.title: Subpart A

criteria.criterion: If the replacement of components of an affected source causes the fixed capital cost of the new components to exceed 50 percent of the fixed capital cost that would be required to construct a comparable new source and it is technologically and economically feasible for the reconstructed source to meet the relevant standards, then the activity meets the definition of reconstruction.

If an owner or operator has undertaken a continuous program of construction or reconstruction or has entered into a contractual obligation to undertake and complete a continuous program of construction or reconstruction within a reasonable time, then construction or reconstruction is considered to have commenced.

If removal and reinstallation of an affected source occurs, then the costs of replacing minor ancillary equipment (including piping, ductwork, and valves) must be considered in determining whether the existing affected source is reconstructed.

candidates.title: Subpart KK

criteria.criterion: If an affected source has undergone reconstruction then the reconstructed affected source is subject to the requirements for new affected sources under this subpart.
If costs were incurred for the purchase and installation of air pollution control equipment then those costs are not considered in determining whether the affected source has been reconstructed.
If costs were incurred for retrofitting or replacement of equipment that was installed specifically to comply with this subpart then those costs are not considered reconstruction costs.

checklist: Determine whether the plant is a major source of HAPs (>= 10 tpy of any single HAP or >= 25 tpy combined).
Confirm whether the units in question are engine test cells/stands that test uninstalled engines (i.e., engines not installed in the final product).

List each engine test cell/stand and whether it is used exclusively for testing engines <25 hp, combustion turbine engines, rocket engines, research/teaching (non-commercial), or for testing/evaluating fuels, transmissions, or electronics.
Establish the dates when construction, modifications, replacements, or additions to each cell/stand began (document start dates, contracts, and work schedules) and compare to May 14, 2002.

Determine whether changes were part of a continuous program of reconstruction or were undertaken under a contractual obligation to perform continuous reconstruction (evidence: contracts, project plans, procurement orders, executed scopes of work).
Prepare an itemized list of replaced or added components (including equipment, instrumentation, electronics, piping, ductwork, valves) and gather invoices, purchase orders, and installation costs.

Calculate the fixed capital cost of the new components and compare to the estimated fixed capital cost to construct a comparable new source to determine whether the new-component cost exceeds 50% (per §63.2 reconstruction test).

Identify and separate costs for passive measurement and control instrumentation and electronics and note that, per §63.9290(a)(3), those costs are excluded from the affected source reconstruction evaluation under Subpart PPPPP.

Identify and separate costs for air pollution control equipment and for retrofitting/replacement of equipment installed specifically to comply with any subpart, since §63.826(c) excludes those costs from reconstruction calculations for Subpart KK.

Determine whether any changes were made primarily to comply with revisions to engine testing requirements under 40 CFR parts 80, 86, 89, 90, 91, or 92 (if yes, such changes are not considered a modification or reconstruction under §63.9290(a)(3)).
Document which replaced items (if any) qualify as 'minor ancillary equipment' per §63.2 and whether their replacement costs were included or excluded in calculations.
Collect engineering drawings, cost estimating worksheets, capital project justifications, and title V / permitting records that support the reconstruction/commencement and cost calculations.

The answer also includes relevant exclusions (passive instrumentation, control equipment) referenced in the subpart criteria."}

candidates.title: Asphalt Processing and Asphalt Roofing Manufacturing

criteria.criterion: if a control device (for example, your mist eliminator) is used to comply with the particulate matter, total hydrocarbon (THC), opacity, or visible emission standards of this subpart then you must conduct periodic performance tests and demonstrate compliance with the emission limitations as specified in § 63.8691(e) (and the referenced test procedures in § 63.8687 and Table 4 to this subpart)

if monitoring of an operating limit or emission limitation is required then you must install, operate, and maintain a continuous parameter monitoring system (CPMS) according to the requirements in § 63.8688(a) (including completing a cycle at least once every 15 minutes and using the specified procedures to determine 3‑hour averages), unless you elect to install a CEMS or COMS that meets § 63.8 as allowed in § 63.8688(f)

if you monitor pressure drop across a control device then the pressure measurement device must meet the requirements of § 63.8688(c), including locating the sensor to provide a representative measurement, using a gauge/transducer with the required sensitivity, daily pressure tap pluggage checks, at least quarterly accuracy checks (or after deviations), monthly integrity/leak checks, and at least quarterly visible inspections if redundant sensors are not used

if the control device is used to comply with the particulate matter standards in this subpart then you may establish the pressure drop operating limits (minimum and maximum) across the control device using the manufacturer's specifications in lieu of establishing site‑specific operating limits under § 63.8689(b)

if you are subject to this subpart and to the monitoring requirements then you must develop and make available a site‑specific monitoring plan that addresses measurement locations (e.g., on or downstream of the last control device), equipment specifications, performance evaluation procedures, and the ongoing operation/QA/recordkeeping procedures described in § 63.8688(g) and (h) and implement the site plan as required by § 63.8688(i) and (j)

if the affected source is operating then you must monitor and collect data at all times in accordance with § 63.8690(b) (subject to the applicability dates and exceptions described in § 63.8685 for periods before/after September 9, 2020 and for periods of nonoperation)

checklist: Confirm whether the mist eliminator on the Group 2 asphalt storage tank is a control device used to meet PM, THC, opacity, or visible emission standards under Subpart LLLLL.
Determine which specific emission limitations and operating limits in Subpart LLLLL (and referenced Tables 1–5) apply to your Group 2 asphalt storage tank and control device.
Verify whether you have already established site‑specific operating limits for the control device or intend to use the manufacturer's pressure‑drop specifications as allowed by 40 CFR 63.8689(d).
Obtain the manufacturer's recommended minimum and maximum pressure drop specifications for the mist eliminator (if relying on manufacturer specs for operating limits).
Confirm whether you currently have a CPMS, CEMS, or COMS monitoring pressure drop/opacity and, if not, whether you will install one or use the manufacturer pressure‑drop option.

If monitoring pressure drop, verify the installed pressure sensor meets the sensitivity requirements (gauge min sensitivity 0.12 kPa or transducer min 5% of range) and that the sensor location provides a representative measurement (on or as close as possible to the measurement point) per § 63.8688(c)(1) and (2).

Confirm current monitoring/QA practices: daily pressure tap pluggage checks, frequency of accuracy checks (at least quarterly or after deviations), monthly leak/integrity checks, and quarterly visible inspections if no redundant sensors, per § 63.8688(c)(3)–(6).

Check whether you have a written site‑specific monitoring plan that documents measurement locations (on/downstream of last control device), equipment specs, performance evaluation procedures, ongoing operation and QA, and recordkeeping/reporting procedures as required by § 63.8688(g) and (h).

Verify your schedule for periodic performance tests (first and subsequent tests) per § 63.8691(e) and whether any previous tests can be used as the initial periodic performance test per § 63.8691(e)(1) and § 63.8689(a)–(b).

Determine whether daily visible emissions (VE) checks are an approved monitoring method or part of the required procedures in Table 5 to this subpart or in your site‑specific monitoring plan (check Table 5 and Table 3/4 requirements referenced in §§ 63.8687–63.8691).
Confirm whether you will use COMS/CEMS as an alternative to CPMS and, if so, ensure they meet § 63.8 and the performance specifications referenced in § 63.8688(f).
Verify the operational status and dates relevant to the monitoring obligations (including applicability of requirements before vs. on/after September 9, 2020) per §§ 63.8690(b) and 63.8685(a)–(b).
Ensure procedures are in place to record results of each inspection, calibration, and validation check as required by § 63.8688(a)(3).
