candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator is required by a relevant standard to perform a performance test and has not obtained a waiver, then the owner or operator must perform the test within 180 days of the compliance date (subject to extensions),

If the owner or operator applies for a waiver and the Administrator, in the Administrator's judgment, determines the source is meeting the relevant standard(s) on a continuous basis (or the source is under an extension of compliance or an extension request is pending), then an individual performance test may be waived by the Administrator

If a request for waiver of an initial or subsequent performance test is submitted, then the application must be submitted at least 60 days before the performance test date (unless the site-specific test plan is submitted or other timing exceptions apply)

If a force majeure delays testing beyond the regulatory deadline, then the owner or operator must notify the Administrator as soon as practicable and may request an extension, which the Administrator may approve or disapprove in the Administrator's sole discretion

If the owner or operator demonstrates by other means to the Administrator's satisfaction that the affected source is in compliance with the relevant standard, then the Administrator may waive the requirement for performance tests

candidates.title: NESHAP for Industrial, Commercial, and Institutional Boilers Area Sources

criteria.criterion: If a boiler has a heat input capacity of 10 million Btu per hour or greater, then you must conduct all applicable performance (stack) tests according to § 63.11212 on a triennial basis (completed no more than 37 months after the previous performance test)

If a boiler uses a continuous emission monitoring system (CEMS) for carbon monoxide (CO), then that boiler is exempt from the initial CO performance testing in Table 4 to this subpart and from the oxygen concentration operating limit requirement in Table 3 to this subpart

If performance stack tests are required under this subpart, then they must be conducted according to § 63.7(c), (d), (f), and (h) (including development of a site-specific test plan and following the waiver procedures in § 63.7 where applicable)

If you intend to request a waiver of a required performance stack test under this subpart, then you must submit the Notification of Intent to conduct a performance test at least 60 days before the scheduled performance stack test (or follow the timing in §63.7 when a site-specific test plan is submitted) and include required justification/documentation with the waiver request

If an existing affected boiler has not operated on solid fossil fuel, biomass, or liquid fuel since the previous compliance demonstration and more than 3 years have passed since the previous demonstration, then you must complete the subsequent compliance demonstration no later than 180 days after the re-start of the affected boiler on those fuels

checklist: For each boiler: confirm the maximum heat input capacity (MMBtu/hr) to determine whether it is >= 10 MMBtu/hr (40 CFR 63.11220(a))
For each boiler: identify whether a CO CEMS is installed and operational (exemption for initial CO testing under 40 CFR 63.11212(b))

For each boiler: record the date of the last performance (stack) test, the pollutant(s) tested, and the test results (to determine triennial due date and whether prior tests showed continuous compliance) (40 CFR 63.11220(a))
For each boiler: determine whether the last performance test was an initial or subsequent test (affects timing and waiver submission timing) (40 CFR 63.11220, 63.7(h))

For each boiler/facility: if planning to permanently cease coal by April 30, 2020, confirm the planned cessation date and whether any boiler will restart on solid fossil fuel, biomass, or liquid fuel within 180 days or within 3 years of the last compliance demonstration (40 CFR 63.11220(e))

Compile documentation evidencing continuous compliance since the last performance test (monitoring records, operating records, tune-ups, past test reports) to support a waiver application to the Administrator (40 CFR 63.7(h)(2))

If seeking a waiver: prepare the waiver application and supporting justification (technical/economic/practical infeasibility or proof of continuous compliance) and note that the application must be submitted at least 60 days before the scheduled performance test unless a site-specific test plan is submitted (40 CFR 63.7(h)(3)(ii); 40 CFR 63.11225(a)(3))

If a force majeure might delay testing: document the event, date first known, rationale attributing the delay to force majeure, measures to minimize delay, and proposed new test date, and be prepared to notify the Administrator as soon as practicable (40 CFR 63.7(a)(4)(i)-(ii))

Ensure records and notifications specified in the subpart are available (e.g., Notification of Intent, Notification of Compliance Status, and test reports) and be prepared to submit performance test results within the required timeframe if testing is conducted (40 CFR 63.11225(a)(3), 40 CFR 63.7(g))

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Halogenated Solvent Cleaning

criteria.criterion: If an individual batch vapor, in-line vapor, in-line cold, or batch cold solvent cleaning machine uses any listed halogenated HAP solvent (methylene chloride, perchloroethylene, trichloroethylene, 1,1,1-trichloroethane, carbon tetrachloride, or chloroform) at a total concentration greater than 5 percent by weight as a cleaning and/or drying agent, then that machine is subject to this subpart.
citations: 40 CFR 63.461 (definition of halogenated hazardous air pollutant solvent)

criteria.criterion: If no solvent cleaning machines at the facility use halogenated HAP solvents above 5 percent by weight (including fresh, recycled, or used solvent that has been cleaned of soils), then those machines are not subject to this subpart.

If you own or operate a batch vapor or in-line solvent cleaning machine that is complying with the provisions of §63.463, then you must submit an annual report by February 1 of the year following the reporting year containing the items specified in §63.468(f).

If you own or operate a batch vapor or in-line solvent cleaning machine that is complying with the provisions of §63.464, then you must submit a solvent emission report every year containing the items specified in §63.468(g).

If your facility qualifies as an affected facility as defined in §63.471(a) (i.e., the applicable set of solvent cleaning machines at a major or area source as described, subject to the facility-wide limits), then the facility must submit a solvent emission report every year as required by §63.471(h).

If the facility-wide 12-month rolling total emissions of PCE, TCE, and methylene chloride (weighted per §63.471(b)(2) and (c)) exceed the applicable Table 1 limit, then an exceedance has occurred and must be reported as required in §63.468(h).

If a solvent cleaning machine meets the applicability criteria of §63.460(a), then the General Provisions in subpart A apply to that owner or operator except as noted in appendix C to this subpart (i.e., Subpart A reporting/recordkeeping provisions may also apply).

checklist: Inventory all solvent cleaning machines on site and identify machine type (batch vapor, batch cold, in-line vapor, in-line cold, continuous web).

For each machine, determine whether any solvent used (fresh, recycled, or 'clean liquid solvent') contains any listed halogenated HAP (methylene chloride, PCE, TCE, 1,1,1-TCA, carbon tetrachloride, chloroform) and whether the halogenated HAP content is greater than 5 percent by weight (use EPA Method 18, MSDS, or engineering calculations).
Verify whether any remaining machines are being used for wipe cleaning only (rags, spray cleaners) which are excluded from this subpart.
Determine whether each machine is complying under §63.463 or §63.464 (identify applicable compliance approach and control methods in use).

Determine whether the facility is an 'affected facility' per §63.471(a) (assess major vs area source status and the listed exclusions such as aerospace, narrow tubing, continuous web, and cold batch for area sources).

Check whether you have previously submitted initial notifications, initial statements of compliance, or prior annual/solvent emission reports and the dates of those submissions (to track continuing reporting obligations).
Confirm whether you intend to reintroduce any listed halogenated HAP solvents in the foreseeable future (plans to resume use may trigger reporting/notification).

If subject, ensure logs of solvent additions and deletions, monthly emission calculations, 12-month rolling totals, and required records/monitoring are in place as specified in §§63.471(c)–(e) and 63.467.

candidates.title: Organic Liquids Distribution (OLD)

criteria.criterion: If the facility is a major source of HAP and has transfer racks that load or unload organic liquids (including hexane) into or out of transport vehicles, then those transfer racks and transport vehicles are part of the OLD affected source and Subpart EEEE applies.

If the storage tanks, transfer racks, transport vehicles, containers, and equipment leak components are part of an affected source subject to another 40 CFR part 63 NESHAP, then those items are excluded from the Subpart EEEE affected source (i.e., Subpart EEEE would not apply to them as OLD equipment).

If a transfer rack is subject to 40 CFR part 61, subpart BB and that transfer rack is in OLD operation, then after the applicable compliance dates the transfer rack must meet all of the requirements of Subpart EEEE when in OLD operation during the loading of organic liquids.

candidates.title: Solvent Extraction for Vegetable Oil Production

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a vegetable oil production process that is a major source of HAP (or is collocated at a plant site that is individually or collectively a major source) and the process uses direct-contact solvent extraction of listed oilseeds (e.g., hexane), then Subpart GGGG applies to that vegetable oil production process.

If the vegetable oil production process includes solvent storage and working tanks, vessels storing solvent-laden materials, solvent recovery equipment (for example mineral oil absorption systems, condensers, and distillation units), or other continuous process equipment listed in § 63.2872, then those components are part of the Subpart GGGG affected source.

If the process uses only mechanical extraction (no organic solvent), uses only batch solvent extraction and batch desolventizing equipment, processes only agricultural products not listed oilseeds, or functions only as a non-major research and development facility, then Subpart GGGG does not apply.

checklist: Is the plant a major source of HAP (>=10 tons/year of any single HAP or >=25 tons/year total)?
Do you operate a vegetable oil production process as defined in 40 CFR 63.2872 (continuous process that removes oil from listed oilseeds by direct contact with an organic solvent such as hexane)?
Which oilseeds are processed at the facility (are they among the listed oilseeds: corn germ, cottonseed, flax, peanut, rapeseed/canola, safflower, soybean, sunflower)?
Is hexane (or another organic solvent) used in direct-contact solvent extraction at the facility, and what is the solvent composition/HAP fraction for delivered solvent?

Are the transfer racks and dedicated transport unloading equipment permanently assigned to and operated as part of the vegetable oil production process (e.g., unloading solvent to process solvent storage/working tanks) or are they part of a separate distribution operation?
Are the transfer racks, storage tanks, transport vehicles, or equipment leak components already assigned to or regulated under another 40 CFR part 63 NESHAP at this site?
Are the transfer racks/transport vehicles non-permanent or used only for special situations or maintenance (which could exclude them from OLD per §63.2338(c)(2)-(3))?
Is any transfer rack at the site subject to 40 CFR part 61 subpart BB or other specific part 60/63 subparts that might affect which subpart's requirements apply to specific components?

Are pumps, valves, or sampling connections at the transfer rack in organic liquids service and subject to other part 60 or part 63 subparts (which may affect whether you must comply with multiple subparts or may elect coverage)?

candidates.title: Subpart S (Pulp and Paper Industry)

criteria.criterion: if an owner or operator is subject to the standards specified in §§ 63.443(c) and (d), 63.444(b) and (c), 63.445(b) and (c), 63.446(c), (d), and (e), 63.447(b), or § 63.450(d), then the monitoring requirements of § 63.453 apply to the affected source, including closed-vent and enclosure inspection provisions

if an enclosure opening is used to comply with § 63.450(b) or a closed-vent system is used to comply with § 63.450(a), then each enclosure opening and each closed-vent system must be visually inspected at least once every 30 days

if a pulping process condensate closed collection system is used to comply with § 63.446(d), then that closed collection system shall be visually inspected every 30 days and comply with the referenced inspection and monitoring requirements

if an owner or operator proposes to use a control device, technique, or alternative monitoring parameter or frequency other than those specified in paragraphs (b) through (l), then the owner or operator must install any required CMS (if applicable) and provide the Administrator the rationale, data, and proposed monitoring frequency and receive Administrator approval as specified

candidates.title: Subpart A (General Provisions)

criteria.criterion: if an owner or operator wishes to use an alternative monitoring procedure (minor, intermediate, or major change) or otherwise change monitoring frequency or method, then the Administrator must approve the alternative under § 63.8(f) before it may be used and the owner/operator must submit the information and performance evaluation plan required by § 63.8(f)(4)

if an owner or operator submits a request to use an alternative monitoring method, then the Administrator will notify the applicant of approval or intended denial within 30 calendar days after receipt of the original request and any supplementary information as specified in § 63.8(f)(5)

candidates.title: Subpart UUUU (Calendar-period and time-period provisions)

criteria.criterion: if a provision in this subpart specifies a period of time for completing required tasks (e.g., monthly), then those terms refer to standard calendar periods and you may change time periods specified in this subpart by mutual agreement with the Administrator as specified in subpart A

if an affected source is operating, then monitoring required by this subpart must be performed continuously or at all required intervals at all times the affected source is operating, except for monitor malfunctions, repairs, and required QA/QC activities

candidates.title: Subpart EEEEE (Procedures to apply for alternative monitoring methods)

criteria.criterion: if an owner or operator requests approval to use an alternative monitoring method to demonstrate compliance, then the owner or operator must submit a monitoring plan describing the control technique or pollution prevention technique, the continuous monitoring system or method, operating parameters, test results, operating limits, and measurement frequency and must obtain Administrator approval before using the alternative

candidates.title: Subpart H (Closed-vent systems and control devices inspection and repair requirements)

criteria.criterion: if a closed-vent system is constructed of hard-piping, then the owner or operator must conduct an initial inspection and thereafter conduct annual visual inspections for visible, audible, or olfactory indications of leaks

if the vapor collection or closed-vent system is constructed of ductwork, then the owner or operator must conduct an initial inspection and thereafter conduct annual inspections according to the procedures in the subpart

if a closed-vent system contains bypass lines that could divert a vent stream away from the control device, then the owner or operator must either install a flow indicator taking a reading at least once every 15 minutes or secure the bypass valve with a car-seal or lock-and-key and perform a visual inspection of the seal or closure mechanism at least once every month

if an instrument reading shows a leak greater than 500 ppm above background or visual indications of a leak are observed, then a first repair attempt must be made as soon as practicable but no later than 5 calendar days and repair completed no later than 15 calendar days unless delay is allowed under the subpart

checklist: Confirm which Part 63 subparts your mill is listed as being subject to (specifically whether Subpart S applies to your affected sources and whether Subpart H, UUUU or any other subpart also apply).

Identify which closed collection systems/enclosures at your mill are used to comply with § 63.450 or § 63.446(d) (e.g., pulping process condensate closed collection systems) and note whether they are hard-piped or ductwork.
Document whether any closed-vent systems contain bypass lines and whether bypass valves are secured (car-seal/lock-and-key) or monitored with a flow indicator.

Verify current inspection interval language in the applicable NESHAP provision (e.g., "at least once every 30 days" vs. "once each calendar month") and determine whether the change sought is from a 30-day rolling interval to a calendar-month interval.

Assemble initial and subsequent performance test and monitoring data (parameter records, CMS data, leak surveys, 500 ppm instrument readings, etc.) to support a rationale that a calendar-month inspection schedule provides continuous compliance equivalently to a 30-day schedule, per § 63.453(n)(2)–(4).

Prepare a written monitoring/inspection alternative request or monitoring plan that includes descriptions of the systems, proposed operating/inspection frequency, supporting data and calculations, and any requested averaging times or definitions (follow content guidance in § 63.7747(c) and § 63.8(f)(4)).

Plan to submit the alternative monitoring application/monitoring plan to the Administrator and note the approval timelines in § 63.8(f)(5) (Administrator will notify approval or intended denial within 30 days after receipt).

If relying on mutual-agreement timing changes for 'standard calendar periods,' confirm whether the applicable subpart recognizes standard calendar periods and whether a mutual agreement with the Administrator per § 63.5560(d)(1) (and § 63.8 process) is available for your affected source.

Confirm that any alternative monitoring method is not implemented until Administrator approval is received (unless the application meets the conditions allowing conduct of performance evaluation using the specified method as described in § 63.8(e)(5)(v)).

Document procedures for corrective actions and repair timing (first attempt within 5 days, completion within 15 days) for detected leaks >500 ppm as required by the applicable subpart (e.g., § 63.172(h) and § 63.453(k)(6)).

judge_text: {"score":2,"reason":"EPA's note indicates a conditional (partial) approval; OUR ANSWER includes the governing provisions requiring Administrator approval for alternative monitoring (40 CFR 63.453(m), 63.8(f), 63.7747), the need to submit a monitoring plan/data, and references to calendar-period/mutual-agreement provisions (63.5560) and applicable inspection/repair requirements — i.e., the key basis for a conditional approval is captured."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Polymers and Resins (Polymers and Resins - Subpart JJJ)

criteria.criterion: If the plant site is a major source and contains one or more thermoplastic product process units (TPPUs) producing a thermoplastic product, then the TPPU and associated equipment constitute an affected source subject to Subpart JJJ.

If pressure relief devices are equipment associated with a TPPU and are in organic HAP service, then the owner/operator must comply with the operating, pressure release, and pressure release management requirements specified in §63.1331(a)(9)(i)–(iii).

If a pressure relief device in organic HAP service is designed and operated to route all pressure releases through a closed vent system to a control device, process, or drain system that meets the referenced requirements, then the owner/operator is not required to comply with paragraphs (a)(9)(i), (ii), or (iii) of §63.1331.

candidates.title: Equipment Leaks / Pressure Relief Devices Standards (Subpart H)

criteria.criterion: If a pressure relief device is in organic HAP gas or vapor service (or light liquid service), then except during pressure releases it must be operated with an instrument reading of less than 500 ppm above background as measured by the method specified in §63.180(c).

If a pressure release occurs from a pressure relief device in organic HAP gas or vapor service, then the device must be returned to a condition indicated by an instrument reading of less than 500 ppm above background as soon as practicable, but no later than 5 calendar days after the pressure release, and monitored within 5 calendar days after returning to service (unless the device includes a rupture disk and the alternative in §63.165 applies).

If all releases and potential leaks from a pressure relief device are routed through a closed vent system to a control device, back into the process, to the fuel gas system, or to a drain system that meets the referenced requirements, then the owner/operator is not required to comply with the operating and post-release monitoring requirements of paragraphs (a) and (b) (and the analogous paragraphs in (e)).

If a pressure relief device is equipped with a rupture disk upstream, then it is exempt from the operating and post-release monitoring requirements of paragraphs (a) and (b) provided a replacement rupture disk is installed as soon as practicable but no later than 5 calendar days after each pressure release.

If a pressure relief device is in organic HAP service, then the owner/operator must equip each affected device with a device(s) or monitoring system capable of identifying the pressure release, recording the time and duration of each pressure release, and notifying operators immediately that a pressure release is occurring.

If any affected pressure relief device releases to the atmosphere as a result of a pressure release event, then the owner/operator must calculate the quantity of organic HAP released and must perform root cause and corrective action analyses and implement corrective actions according to the timelines and requirements specified in paragraphs (e)(3)(iii), (e)(6), and (e)(7).

If a pressure relief device is in heavy liquid service, is a thermal expansion relief valve, is pressure relief on mobile equipment, or meets other listed exemptions, then that device is not subject to the pressure release management requirements in paragraph (e)(3).

checklist: Determine whether your plant site is a major source (i.e., meets the major-source threshold for HAPs) and therefore whether TPPUs at the site can be an affected source under Subpart JJJ.
Determine whether the process unit(s) producing polyurethane copolymer are designated as a thermoplastic product process unit (TPPU) under §63.1310(f) (primary-product test or flexible-unit rules).
Confirm whether the portable containers with pressure relief devices are part of equipment associated with a TPPU or a waste management unit included in the affected source per §63.1310(a)(4)(i).

Verify whether each portable container’s pressure relief device is intended to operate in organic HAP service (i.e., contains organic HAP knowingly introduced into the process) and whether it operates in organic HAP service 300 hours or more during the calendar year (relevant to Subpart H applicability per §63.160).

For each pressure relief device, document whether releases are routed to a closed-vent system to a control device, back to the process, to the fuel gas system, or to a drain system and whether those control/drain systems meet the requirements referenced in the rule (e.g., the closed-vent/control requirements cited in §63.165 and §63.1331).
For each device, document whether a rupture disk is installed upstream of the pressure relief valve (and, if so, whether procedures exist to install a replacement disk as required after a release).

Determine whether any pressure relief devices are on mobile equipment, are thermal expansion relief valves, are in heavy liquid service, or are pilot-operated with primary valve routed to a closed vent (possible exemptions in §63.165(e)(5)).
Inventory the number of pressure relief devices (you stated ~200–300) and map which are associated with TPPUs versus other plant operations to assess workload and applicability.

Confirm the monitoring method(s) available (Method 21 vs. §63.180(c) method specified) and whether you intend to use instrument monitoring or an alternative monitoring plan; identify which devices you propose to cover under any alternate plan.

Verify recordkeeping and reporting capabilities: ability to record release events (time/duration), notify operators immediately, calculate mass of organic HAP released per event, and perform/record root-cause and corrective-action analyses within the specified timeframes.

Thus only some key reasoning from the EPA notes is captured."}

candidates.title: Subpart S - National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for the Pulp and Paper Industry

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator uses a control device, technique, or an alternative operating parameter other than those specified in § 63.453(b) through (l), then the owner or operator shall install a continuous monitoring system (CMS) and establish appropriate operating parameters to be monitored that demonstrate, to the Administrator's satisfaction, continuous compliance with the applicable control requirements.

If the owner or operator seeks to establish or reestablish the value for any operating parameter required to be monitored (or to establish site-specific parameters), then the owner or operator must continuously record the parameter during the initial or subsequent performance test and provide for the Administrator's approval the rationale, data, and selected operating parameter value, monitoring frequency, and averaging time.

If the owner or operator proposes to use an alternative analytical or monitoring method to measure total HAP or methanol concentration for vent gases or liquid streams, then the owner or operator may use any other method that has been demonstrated to the Administrator's satisfaction in lieu of the specified methods.
If the owner or operator is subject to the emissions limitations in §§ 63.443–63.447, then an initial performance test is required for the affected emission sources.

If the owner or operator will treat kraft pulping condensates or demonstrate condensate treatment compliance, then total HAP concentration for condensates shall be measured as methanol (and for biological systems certain additional compounds must be measured as specified).

candidates.title: Subpart MM - National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Kraft and Soda Recovery Furnaces, Smelt Dissolving Tanks, and Lime Kilns

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator of an affected kraft or soda recovery furnace, kraft or soda lime kiln, or other affected unit uses a wet scrubber, then the owner or operator must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate a continuous parameter monitoring system (CPMS) able to determine and record the scrubber pressure drop and scrubbing liquid flow rate at least once every successive 15-minute period with specified accuracy.

If the owner or operator uses an air pollution control system other than an ESP, wet scrubber, RTO, or fabric filter, then the owner or operator must submit an alternative monitoring request to the Administrator that describes the control device, presents test results verifying performance, proposes appropriate operating parameters and limits, and includes proposed performance specifications and quality assurance procedures for the monitors.

If the owner or operator intends to set operating limits for CPMS or other monitored parameters, then those operating limits must be established during the initial or periodic performance test or based on prior performance test data and follow the procedures in § 63.864(j).

candidates.title: Subpart EEEEE - National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Iron and Steel Foundries (procedures for alternative monitoring plans)

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator requests approval to use an alternative monitoring method (for continuous emissions monitoring) to demonstrate compliance, then the owner or operator must submit a monitoring plan that includes a description of the control or prevention technique, a description of the continuous monitoring system or method and the operating parameters to be monitored, test results demonstrating compliance, operating limit(s) derived from those test results, the measuring/recording frequency to establish continuous compliance, and applicable O&M requirements, and must obtain Administrator approval before use.

checklist: Confirm which Subpart S emission standards (§§ 63.443–63.447) apply to your kraft pulping equipment (identify the specific equipment/equipment systems: digesters, brownstock washers, oxygen delignification, bleach plant, steam strippers, condensate streams, black liquor storage, etc.).

Determine whether you plan to use the monitoring parameters and control-device monitoring approaches specified in § 63.453(b)–(l) or propose alternative control/monitoring parameters (i.e., will you rely on specified temperature, pH, flow, methanol concentration, etc., or propose others).

Identify all control devices used for HAP emissions (thermal oxidizer/RTO, wet scrubber, closed‑vent system, biological treatment, steam stripper, ESP, fabric filter) and whether any are non‑standard/alternative.
Verify whether you will propose to measure total HAP as methanol (for condensates) or as the sum of individual HAPs (for vent gases/bleaching) consistent with § 63.457(g) and (h).

Plan and document initial performance testing for all affected emission sources subject to §§ 63.443–63.447 as required by § 63.457(a)(1) (test methods, number of runs, run durations, representative conditions).

If proposing alternative monitoring parameters, compile continuous parameter records from the applicable performance test(s) to support establishing operating limits and prepare the rationale/data required by § 63.453(n) (include engineering assessments and manufacturer recommendations).

Prepare the alternative monitoring request/monitoring plan contents: description of control technique, description of CMS/method, operating parameters to be monitored, test results demonstrating compliance, proposed operating limits, measurement/recording frequency, and O&M and QA/QC procedures (per § 63.7747(c) and § 63.864(e)(14)).

If proposing alternative analytical methods for vent gas or liquid HAP/methanol measurement, document method validation and demonstrate to the Administrator's satisfaction how the method provides equivalent or adequate measurement (per § 63.457(b)(5)(iii) and § 63.457(c)(3)(iii)).

If the facility has a recovery furnace, smelt dissolving tank, or lime kiln subject to Subpart MM, verify whether control devices are ESP, wet scrubber, RTO, or fabric filter; if not, prepare an alternative monitoring request per § 63.864(e)(14).

For any wet scrubber CPMS proposed, verify that pressure-drop and liquid-flow monitors meet the manufacturer accuracy requirements (±500 pascals for pressure, ±5% for flow) and that monitoring frequency and averaging conform to § 63.864(e)(10) and (f).
For open biological treatment systems or archived inlet/outlet samples, ensure sample storage at 4 °C (40 °F) and daily sampling/archive procedures as required by § 63.453(j) and § 63.457(n).

Assemble recordkeeping and reporting elements referenced in Subpart S (e.g., documentation required under § 63.453(n), § 63.454, and § 63.455) to support an alternative monitoring approval and future compliance demonstrations.

Confirm the submission vehicle and timing: whether the alternative monitoring plan will be submitted as part of a notification of construction/reconstruction or at any time (note § 63.7747(b) allows either), and do not begin using the alternative monitoring until the Administrator approves it.

The provided criteria and checklist fully capture the key conditional elements — requirement to submit/obtain Administrator approval, CMS/CPMS specs, initial performance testing, establishment of operating limits with supporting data/rationale, validation of alternative analytical methods, and O&M/QA requirements — so the EPA's key reason (conditional approval subject to specified requirements) is represented."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Lime Manufacturing Plants (Subpart AAAAA)

criteria.criterion: If you have a new affected source, then you must comply with this subpart according to the startup and testing schedules in § 63.7083(a)(1) and (a)(2).

If you have an existing affected source, then you must comply with the applicable PM emission limitations and complete all applicable performance tests by the deadlines in § 63.7083(b) (subject to the exceptions in paragraph (g) or (h) as specified).

If you use a continuous opacity monitoring system (COMS) to monitor an add-on air pollution control device, then you must install the COMS at the outlet of the control device and install, maintain, calibrate, and operate the COMS as required by this subpart and Performance Specification 1 (PS-1) (see § 63.7113(g)).

If you are an existing lime kiln subject to an opacity limit and you meet any condition in § 63.7121(f)(1) through (f)(3), then you may perform visible emissions (VE) measurements in accordance with EPA Method 9 in lieu of installing a COMS or PM detector.

If you are required to install/operate continuous parameter monitoring systems (CPMS) or a COMS, then you must install, operate, and maintain each CPMS according to your OM&M plan required by § 63.7100(d) and comply with the monitoring operation, calibration, and maintenance provisions in § 63.7113(a) through (i).

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If you are the owner or operator of an affected source for which a relevant standard has been established, then the requirements of § 63.6 apply to you unless the Administrator or a State with an approved permit program has granted an extension under paragraph (i) or the President has granted an exemption under § 63.6(a)(1).

If the owner or operator of an existing source is unable to comply with a relevant standard because additional time is necessary for the installation of controls, then the owner or operator may request from the Administrator (or an authorized State) an extension of compliance of up to one additional year to install the controls (with limited extra time for specific mining waste operations) as provided in § 63.6(i)(4)(i)(A).

If the owner or operator requests an extension of compliance under § 63.6(i)(4), then the request generally must be submitted in writing no later than 120 days prior to the affected source's compliance date, except where the need arose after that date due to circumstances beyond reasonable control (in which case a later request may be submitted per § 63.6(i)(4)(i)(B) and (C)); nonfrivolous requests will stay applicability until granted or denied.

If you request a compliance extension, then your request must include the information specified in § 63.6(i)(6) (including a description of controls to be installed and a compliance schedule with dates for initiation and completion of construction/installation and final compliance).

If the Administrator (or State) grants an extension of compliance, then the extension will be in writing and will identify the affected source(s), specify the termination date, specify required intermediate dates, and list any additional conditions to assure installation of controls and protection of health as provided in § 63.6(i)(10).
If you have not been granted an extension, then until an extension is granted you must comply with all applicable requirements of this part (see § 63.6(i)(1)).

checklist: Confirm whether your facility (lime kilns) is an affected source subject to Subpart AAAAA (determine applicability for LMP category).

Determine whether each kiln is a 'new' or 'existing' affected source and record each kiln's initial startup date and any construction/reconstruction dates to identify the applicable compliance deadline per 40 CFR 63.7083.

Verify the specific compliance date that applies to your kiln(s) under 40 CFR 63.7083(g) and (h) (including whether your source commenced construction or reconstruction on or before the cited benchmark dates).
Confirm whether a COMS is currently installed on each kiln/control device and the COMS installation date (note if installed on or before Feb 6, 2001) and whether the COMS meets PS-1 requirements.

Assess whether COMS installation at the outlet of the control device is technically feasible for each kiln or whether one of the § 63.7121(f)(1)–(f)(3) conditions (positive-pressure FF with multiple stacks; control device exhausts through a monovent; installation infeasible) applies so VE can be used in lieu of COMS.

Confirm whether you have prepared and submitted the OM&M plan required by § 63.7100(d) (including monitoring schedules, calibration/certification procedures, and corrective actions) and whether OM&M addresses COMS/CPMS operation as required by § 63.7113(a).

If you intend to request a compliance extension, verify whether your compliance extension request can be submitted at least 120 days before the applicable compliance date or whether the need for an extension arose after that deadline (document dates and reasons) as allowed by § 63.6(i)(4)(i)(B)–(C).

Prepare the required information for an extension request per § 63.6(i)(6): description of controls to be installed, detailed compliance schedule with dates to initiate and complete on-site construction/installation and final compliance, and any other supporting documentation.

Determine whether your State has an approved part 70 permit program or delegated authority to grant extensions (the extension may be granted by the State if authorized) and whether an extension, if granted, must be incorporated into your Title V permit.

Assemble records showing efforts already taken to install COMS (purchase orders, contractor schedules, equipment lead times, permitting actions) to substantiate that additional time is necessary for installation of controls and to support a nonfrivolous extension request.

Be prepared to comply with all applicable requirements until an extension is granted (collect monitoring and operational records demonstrating efforts to minimize emissions and good O&M practices as required by § 63.6(e)(1)).

If granted an extension, be prepared to meet any written conditions in the extension (intermediate milestones, progress reports, and additional protective measures) and to have the extension incorporated into your title V permit per § 63.6(i)(10)–(11).

The answer cites the extension for installing controls and COMS installation requirements but fails to record the critical distinction that COMS are monitoring (not control) equipment, which is the basis of the EPA determination."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Phosphate Fertilizer Production Plants

criteria.criterion: if the facility includes phosphate fertilizer process lines, granular triple superphosphate process lines, or granular triple superphosphate storage buildings then the source is subject to the emission limits and requirements of Subpart BB

if a process line or storage building commenced construction or reconstruction on or before December 27, 1996 then it must comply with Table 1 beginning June 10, 2002, if it commenced after December 27, 1996 and on or before August 19, 2015 then it must comply with Table 2 beginning June 10, 1999 or at startup (whichever is later), and if construction/reconstruction commenced after August 19, 2015 then it must comply with Table 2 immediately upon startup

if you use a control device(s) to comply with the emission limits in Table 1 or Table 2 then you must install a continuous parameter monitoring system (CPMS) and monitor the operating parameter(s) specified in Table 3 and establish the applicable operating parameter limit or range as specified in § 63.625(d)

if you determine baseline operating parameter values for purposes of establishing operating limits then those value(s) must be the arithmetic average of operating parameter measurements recorded during the three test runs conducted for the most recent performance test

if you use an absorber and you monitor pressure drop across the absorber then the allowable range for the daily averages of pressure drop and absorber liquid flow is ±20 percent of the baseline average value determined per § 63.625(d)(1)(i), except the Administrator may reduce the adjustment (but not to less than ±10 percent) when performance test results indicate emissions are near the standard

if you elect the alternative methodology in § 63.625(d)(1)(ii)(B) then you may establish allowable operating parameter ranges based on baseline averages recorded during previous performance tests or results of performance tests conducted for that purpose provided you conduct tests using the methods in § 63.626, certify no modifications since the performance test used to establish ranges, and determine new ranges upon retest unless the retest indicates no change

if you use a continuous monitoring system (CMS) to demonstrate compliance then you must develop and keep a site-specific monitoring plan that includes probe location, equipment and performance specifications, performance evaluation procedures and acceptance criteria, ongoing O&M and QA/QC procedures, recordkeeping/reporting procedures, and a schedule for conducting initial and subsequent performance evaluations, and you must submit that plan to the Administrator for approval upon request at least 60 days before the initial performance evaluation

if you use a CMS then you must conduct performance evaluations of the CMS in accordance with your site-specific monitoring plan and the procedures specified in this subpart and must record required performance-evaluation information (for bag leak detectors, record sensitivity, range, averaging period, and alarm set points during the performance test)

if you use a fabric filter with a bag leak detection system then you must install, certify, continuously record and alarm the detector, calibrate by establishing baseline output and alarm set points, limit sensitivity/range/alarm adjustments as specified in the site-specific monitoring plan (sensitivity may not be increased more than 100% or decreased more than 50% over 365 days except after a complete inspection), operate so alarms do not sound more than 5% of operating time over a 6-month period, initiate procedures within 1 hour of an alarm and corrective action within 48 hours, and retain alarm records

if you are subject to Subpart BB then you must conduct an initial performance test within 180 days of the applicable compliance date and thereafter conduct a performance test once per calendar year (with special provisions when a unit has not operated since the previous annual test and more than 1 year has passed)

if you conduct a performance test then the test must be conducted at representative (normal) conditions that represent the range of combined process and control conditions under which you expect to operate and are likely to most challenge the emissions control measures, and operations during startup, shutdown, and malfunction do not constitute representative (normal) conditions

if you use blower design capacity or a regression model to determine gas flow through an absorber for use in liquid-to-gas ratio calculations then you must include the blower calculations or regression model calculations, constants, verification procedures, and annual updates in your site-specific monitoring plan

if you establish a new operating limit based on the most recent performance test then you must notify the Administrator and thereafter operate under the new operating limit, and if the Administrator determines the test was not conducted in accordance with requirements or is not representative you must conduct a new performance test and establish a new operating limit

checklist: Confirm each of the three ammonium phosphate trains is a phosphate fertilizer process line or otherwise an affected source under Subpart BB
For each train, document construction or reconstruction date to determine whether it is an "existing" or "new" source per 63.622(a)(1)-(3)
Identify whether each train uses a control device (e.g., absorber/scrubber, wet ESP, or fabric filter) to comply with the Subpart BB emission limits

For each control device, confirm whether a CPMS/CPMS-type parameter monitoring or a CMS is installed and which operating parameter(s) are being monitored (e.g., absorber pressure drop, liquid flow rate)

Verify the site-specific monitoring plan exists on-site and contains: probe location justification, equipment/specifications, performance-evaluation procedures and acceptance criteria, O&M procedures, QA/QC procedures, recordkeeping/reporting procedures, and a schedule for initial and subsequent performance evaluations (and whether it was submitted ≥60 days before the initial performance evaluation if requested)
Determine how baseline operating-parameter values were established (were they calculated as the arithmetic average of measurements from the three test runs of the most recent performance test?)

If relying on previous performance-test data to set operating ranges per the alternative method, document the date of the performance test used and certify that control devices and processes have not been modified since that test
Document the dates of the most recent and prior performance tests for each train and when the next annual performance test is scheduled

Confirm that performance tests are/will be conducted at representative (normal) conditions (not during startup/shutdown/malfunction) and retain records demonstrating representative conditions used during the test

If using bag leak detection systems, verify calibration/baseline procedures, alarm set points, adjustment limitations (+100%/−50% per 365 days rule), alarm response procedures and that alarm records are retained

Verify the CMS/CPMS performance-evaluation schedule and whether the site-specific plan specifies performance-evaluations timed relative to performance tests (and whether any request to the Administrator or petition under monitoring provisions has been or will be submitted)

If proposing to shift scrubber (absorber) performance-evaluation timing (e.g., performance evaluations within five days prior to performance tests rather than same day), identify where in your site-specific monitoring plan the schedule and justification for that timing is documented and whether you will submit the plan or any petition/notification to the Administrator as required

These elements capture the key reasons in the EPA Notes."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Phosphate Fertilizer Production Plants (Phosphate Fertilizer Production)

criteria.criterion: If you operate a phosphate fertilizer process line or a granular triple superphosphate process line subject to this subpart, then you must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate a continuous monitoring system (CMS) that has an accuracy of ±5 percent over its operating range and determines and permanently records the mass flow of phosphorus-bearing material fed to the process.

If you operate a phosphate fertilizer process line or granular triple superphosphate process line subject to this subpart, then you must maintain a daily record of equivalent P2O5 feed calculated using the procedures specified in § 63.626(f)(3).

If you conduct performance tests to demonstrate compliance with the total fluorides standards, then you must compute the equivalent P2O5 feed (P) using the mass flow measurement system described in § 63.625(a) to determine Mp and the P2O5 content (Rp) using the methods listed in § 63.626(f)(3).

If you use a CMS to demonstrate compliance, then you must develop and keep a site-specific monitoring plan that includes probe location and justification, performance and equipment specifications, performance evaluation procedures and acceptance criteria, ongoing O&M procedures, data quality assurance, and recordkeeping/reporting procedures and submit that plan to the Administrator upon request.

If you want to use alternative monitoring parameters or make major changes to monitoring requirements, then you must request approval (petition) and the Administrator retains authority to approve or deny such requests as specified for alternative monitoring under this subpart.

If you use a fabric filter system to comply with the emission limits, then beginning August 19, 2016 the fabric filter must be equipped with a bag leak detection system that is installed, calibrated, maintained, and continuously operated according to the requirements in § 63.625(e)(1)–(10) and the bag leak detection system requirements must be included in the site-specific monitoring plan.
If you use a CMS, then you must conduct a performance evaluation of the CMS consistent with § 63.8(e) in accordance with your site-specific monitoring plan and record performance-evaluation details.

If you use blower design capacity or a regression model to determine absorber gas flow for control-parameter monitoring, then you must include the calculations and supporting data (or regression model development and verification) in the site-specific monitoring plan as specified in § 63.628(e) and (f).

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If your affected source is subject to Subpart BB, then you must comply with the general provisions in Subpart A of this part as specified in appendix A to Subpart BB.

If you perform CMS performance evaluations or other monitoring and reporting required by Subpart BB, then you must follow the applicable general provisions and monitoring, performance-evaluation, O&M, QA/QC and reporting requirements established in Subpart A (as invoked by Subpart BB).

checklist: Identify whether you operate any of the following affected unit types: diammonium/monoammonium phosphate process lines, granular triple superphosphate process lines, or granular triple superphosphate storage buildings (see definitions in 40 CFR 63.621).
Determine whether each affected source is existing or new (construction/reconstruction date on or before vs. after December 27, 1996) per the definitions in 40 CFR 63.621.

Confirm whether you currently use a CMS to measure mass flow of phosphorus-bearing feed and document the CMS type (e.g., magnetic flow meter), model, installation location relative to the last control device, and whether permanent mass-flow records are captured.

Verify that the CMS (or proposed alternative monitoring method) can meet an accuracy of ±5 percent over its operating range and that this accuracy is documented (calibration records, QA/QC procedures) as required by 40 CFR 63.625(a)(1).

If using magnetic flow meters, document the effect of scaling on accuracy across the full operating range and whether calibration/cleaning frequency and performance evaluation can ensure ±5% accuracy.

Document how you will calculate and record daily equivalent P2O5 feed (P) including: mass flow rate of phosphorus-bearing feed (Mp) measured by the CMS and the method used to determine P2O5 content (Rp) using one of the methods listed in 40 CFR 63.626(f)(3).

Assemble or update a site-specific monitoring plan that includes: CMS probe location and justification, equipment/specifications, performance evaluation procedures and acceptance criteria, ongoing O&M, QA/QC procedures, recordkeeping and reporting, and a schedule for CMS performance evaluations (40 CFR 63.628(c)(1)-(3)).

If proposing an alternative monitoring procedure (e.g., converting signals, using surrogate parameters, or using a different measurement technology), prepare a petition or request consistent with the process referenced in 40 CFR 63.628(c) and note that approval authority for alternatives to monitoring requirements is retained by the Administrator per 40 CFR 63.632(b)(3).

If you use fabric filters as control devices, confirm whether bag leak detection is required and, if so, document detector locations, manufacturer sensitivity certification, continuous recording, alarm procedures, calibration/baseline settings, corrective action plan, and record retention as required by 40 CFR 63.625(e) and 40 CFR 63.628(d).

Plan performance tests using representative (normal) operating conditions, Method 13A or 13B for total fluorides sampling, and ensure the P2O5 feed rate (P) calculation uses the CMS-measured Mp and validated Rp per 40 CFR 63.626(d), (e), and (f)(1)-(3).

Maintain records of CMS performance evaluations (per 40 CFR 63.626(h)), CMS calibrations, adjustments, and any instances where alarm/exceedance procedures or corrective actions were implemented, retaining superseded versions of the monitoring plan for 5 years after revision per 40 CFR 63.628(c)(3).

If absorber liquid-to-gas ratios or blower-based parameters are used for CPMS/CPMS-derived monitoring, prepare and include blower-capacity calculations or regression model development/verification and annual updates in the site-specific monitoring plan per 40 CFR 63.628(e)-(f).

The answer includes the key regulatory criteria that cover alternatives (must request approval/petition and Administrator may approve/deny) plus the CMS accuracy, site-specific monitoring plan, and performance-evaluation requirements that underpin EPA’s acceptance decisions, so the EPA note is captured by the criteria provided."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Petroleum Refineries—Catalytic Cracking Units, Catalytic Reforming Units, and Sulfur Recovery Units (Subpart UUU)

criteria.criterion: If you operate a catalytic cracking unit (e.g., an FCCU) at your refinery, then you are subject to the emission limitations, operating limits, and monitoring requirements in this subpart and must meet the applicable items in Table 1 and Table 2 and install and operate continuous monitoring as required.

If your FCCU regenerator vent is subject to the NSPS PM limit at 40 CFR 60.102(a)(1), the unit uses a wet scrubber for PM control, and you have Administrator-approved alternative monitoring for the NSPS continuous opacity monitoring requirement, then you may request alternative monitoring requirements under this subpart for that same regenerator vent by submitting the approved NSPS alternative and a monitoring plan.

If you wish to monitor parameters other than those specified in this subpart (including alternative continuous parameter monitoring systems or other operating parameters for a wet scrubber), then you must request approval from the Administrator and include the descriptions, demonstration methods, supporting calculations, monitoring frequency, and averaging time specified in the request requirements.

If you perform a performance test to demonstrate compliance, then your continuous parameter monitor operating limits must be based on the performance test results and you may (with supporting documentation) adjust one monitored operating parameter (flow rate, total power and secondary current, pressure drop, or liquid-to-gas ratio) from the performance-test average to a worst-case (max or min) representative value, except that adjustments specific to equilibrium catalyst Ni concentration follow separate provisions.

If you want to change an established operating limit for a continuous parameter monitoring system, then you must do an additional performance test, a performance test with an engineering assessment, or an engineering assessment to verify that the affected source complies at the new operating limit.

If your wet scrubber is a jet-ejector type or otherwise uses atomizing spray nozzles, then you may use a daily check of the air or water pressure to the spray nozzles as an approved alternative to continuous pressure-drop monitoring provided you record the daily checks and repair faulty lines within 12 hours of identifying an abnormal pressure reading.

If you are subject to this subpart, then you must prepare, submit to your permitting authority, and implement an operation, maintenance, and monitoring (OM&M) plan that lists the process and control device parameters to be monitored and the established operating limits and related procedures.

checklist: Do you operate a catalytic cracking unit (FCCU) at this refinery?
Is the FCCU catalyst regenerator vent controlled by a wet scrubber?
Is the FCCU regenerator vent subject to NSPS PM limits at 40 CFR 60.102(a)(1)?
Have you elected which compliance option in 40 CFR 63.1564(a)(1) applies to your unit (Option 1a/1b/1c/2/3/4)?
Do you have Administrator-approved alternative monitoring under the NSPS (e.g., for continuous opacity at 40 CFR 60.105(a)(1)) for this regenerator vent?
Have you conducted the required initial performance test(s) for the FCCU (and do you have the test reports and supporting data used to set operating limits)?
What continuous/control parameters are you currently monitoring for the wet scrubber (e.g., pressure drop, liquid-to-gas ratio, pH, alkalinity, gas flow, nozzle pressure)?
Have you established site-specific operating limits based on the performance test results and documented any adjustments (and the supporting rationale) per 40 CFR 63.1571(d)?
Do you intend to change any established operating limit (and if so, have you planned an additional performance test or engineering assessment per 40 CFR 63.1571(e))?
If using the pressure-nozzle daily-check alternative, do you perform and record daily air/water pressure checks and have procedures to repair faulty lines within 12 hours?

Have you submitted the OM&M plan (including monitored parameters and operating limits) to your permitting authority and received any required approvals or been in contact with the Administrator about alternative monitoring requests?

Are your monitoring systems operated continuously and meeting the cycle, data-recording, and data-availability requirements specified in the subpart (e.g., minimum cycle times and hourly averaging rules)?

If proposing alternative monitoring parameters, have you prepared the approval request with descriptions, demonstration methods, supporting calculations, monitoring frequency, averaging time, and rationale as required by 40 CFR 63.1573(f)?
Has your permitting authority (or the Administrator) already approved any alternative monitoring under this subpart or under the NSPS that would apply to the FCCU wet scrubber?

These criteria capture the primary reasons underlying EPA's approval."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Steel Pickling—Hydrochloric Acid (HCl) Process and Hydrochloric Acid Regeneration Plants (monitoring requirements)

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator of a steel pickling facility or acid regeneration plant subject to this subpart uses a wet scrubber to meet the standard, then they must install, operate, and maintain systems to measure and record the scrubber makeup water flow rate and, if applicable, recirculation water flow rate, monitor these flow rates continuously, and record them at least once per shift while the scrubber is operating.

If a wet scrubber is used and a performance test is conducted, then the owner or operator must establish site-specific minimum scrubber makeup water flow rate (and minimum recirculation water flow rate for recirculating scrubbers) during the performance test, where operating parameters are monitored continuously and recorded with sufficient frequency (no less frequently than once every 15 minutes) to establish representative average values.

If the owner or operator operates the scrubber with makeup or recirculation flow rates less than the minimum values established during the performance test, then corrective action must be initiated as specified by the maintenance requirements of this subpart.

If the owner or operator seeks a monitoring approach other than the flow-rate monitoring specified for wet scrubbers, then they may develop and implement alternative monitoring requirements only with approval by the Administrator.
If required monitoring parameters are not recorded as specified in this subpart, then failure to record constitutes a violation of the monitoring requirements.

If a monitoring device is installed for this subpart, then each monitoring device shall be certified by the manufacturer to be accurate to within 5 percent and shall be calibrated in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions not less frequently than once per year.

candidates.title: Monitoring installation, operation, and maintenance requirements for continuous monitoring systems (CMS) and approval of alternative scrubber parameters

criteria.criterion: If you are required by this subpart to monitor an operating parameter, then you must install, operate, and maintain each CMS and collect data at all times the process is operating, collect data from at least four equally spaced periods each hour, obtain valid data for at least 75 percent of operating hours each day, calculate hourly averages when valid data exist for at least four equally spaced periods each hour, and calculate a daily average from the hourly averages.

If you seek approval to monitor parameters other than those specified for scrubber control devices, then you must submit a monitoring plan in accordance with § 63.8(f) that meets the requirements to identify the operating parameter, explain why it is appropriate for demonstrating ongoing compliance, and identify the specific monitoring procedures.

If you submit a monitoring plan for an alternative parameter, then you must conduct monitoring in accordance with the approved plan and record results for each inspection, calibration, and validation check as specified in the site-specific monitoring plan.

candidates.title: Process vent provisions—monitoring requirements (scrubber-related monitoring for halogenated vent streams)

criteria.criterion: If a process vent uses a scrubber with an incinerator, boiler, or process heater for halogenated vent streams, then a pH monitoring device equipped with a continuous recorder must be installed to monitor the scrubber effluent.

If a scrubber is used with an incinerator, boiler, or process heater as described in this section, then a flow meter equipped with a continuous recorder must be located at the scrubber influent for liquid flow and gas flow rate must be determined by one of the specified procedures.

candidates.title: General monitoring requirements for control and recovery devices (CPMS/alternatives and approvals)

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator of a regulated source is required to monitor under this subpart, then monitoring shall be conducted as set forth in this section and relevant referencing subpart provisions unless the Administrator approves minor methodology changes or alternative monitoring.

If a continuous parameter monitoring system (CPMS) is used, then the owner or operator must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate the CPMS according to manufacturer's specifications or other written procedures that provide adequate assurance of accurate monitoring and must maintain and operate each CPMS in a manner consistent with good air pollution control practices.

If the owner or operator desires to monitor a different parameter than those listed in paragraph (c)(6) of this section or to set unique monitoring parameters, then they may request approval to do so as specified in § 63.999(d)(2).

If CPMS are used as backups or replacements during a reporting period, then the owner or operator must report results from the CPMS used to meet the monitoring requirements and, if both were used during a reporting period, report results from each instrument for the time each instrument was relied upon.

checklist: Confirm whether the facility is an affected steel pickling facility or hydrochloric acid regeneration plant subject to Subpart CCC.
Confirm whether the HCl emissions control device is a wet scrubber (and whether it uses recirculation).

Determine whether a performance test has been (or will be) conducted for the scrubber and whether site-specific minimum scrubber makeup water flow rate and minimum recirculation flow rate were established during that performance test.

Verify current monitoring practice: is scrubber makeup water flow rate (and recirculation flow rate if applicable) measured continuously and recorded at least once per shift as required by Subpart CCC?

If current monitoring is by conductivity rather than direct flow measurement, document how conductivity correlates to makeup water flow and whether that alternative parameter was or will be included in the performance test record used to establish operating limits.

Prepare a monitoring plan (per §63.8(f)) describing the alternative parameter (conductivity), why it demonstrates ongoing compliance, and specific monitoring procedures if seeking Administrator approval.

Verify CMS/data-collection capabilities meet NNNNN requirements: collection at all times process is operating, at least four equally spaced measurements per hour, ability to calculate hourly and daily averages, and attainment of ≥75% valid data per day.
Confirm that monitoring devices intended for use are manufacturer-certified to ±5% accuracy and that calibration procedures and frequency (at least annually) are in place.
Assemble recordkeeping and reporting procedures to demonstrate continuous operation, calibration, inspections, and corrective actions per the applicable subparts.

Determine the appropriate Agency (Administrator) or permitting authority contact and obtain formal approval for any proposed alternative monitoring (conductivity in lieu of makeup flow) as required by the cited provisions.

candidates.title: Subpart HHHHHHH

criteria.criterion: If you are using an absorber or acid gas scrubber to meet an emission limit in Table 1 or 2 to this subpart and are required to use CPMS as specified in § 63.11925(c), then you must install and operate pressure gauges at the inlet and outlet of the absorber or acid gas scrubber to monitor the pressure drop through the absorber or acid gas scrubber unless an alternative is approved by the Administrator.

If you are required to use CPMS for process vent control devices, then you must install, operate, maintain, and record CPMS data at least once every 15 minutes and prepare and follow a site-specific monitoring plan and quality assurance procedures as specified in this subpart.

If you seek to use an alternative monitoring parameter or procedure in lieu of those specified in this section, then you may request Administrator approval for alternatives to the continuous monitoring requirements or to monitor a different parameter, but you remain subject to the subpart requirements until approval is granted.

If you must establish operating limits for monitored parameters, then the operating limit must be based on values recorded during a performance test demonstrating compliance and may be supplemented by engineering assessments or manufacturer's recommendations.

candidates.title: Subpart SS

criteria.criterion: If your source is required to monitor under this subpart, then monitoring shall be conducted as set forth in this section and the relevant referencing subpart unless the Administrator specifies minor changes in methodology or approves alternatives to the specified monitoring requirements or procedures.

If you wish to monitor a different parameter than those established in the referencing subpart or to set unique monitoring parameters, then you may request Administrator approval as provided in paragraph (d)(2) of this section.

If you install and operate CPMS under this subpart, then the CPMS must be installed, calibrated, maintained, and operated according to manufacturer's specifications or written procedures that provide adequate assurance of accurate monitoring, installed to obtain representative measurements, and verified operational prior to or in conjunction with performance tests.

candidates.title: Subpart EEEEE

criteria.criterion: If you want to use an alternative continuous monitoring method for compliance, then you may request approval by submitting a monitoring plan that describes the alternative monitoring method, operating parameters, test results demonstrating compliance, and operating limits, and you may not begin using the alternative monitoring method until the Administrator approves the plan.

candidates.title: Subpart G

criteria.criterion: If you use a scrubber to comply with the process vent requirements in § 63.113, then you must install a pH monitoring device to monitor the scrubber effluent and a flow meter at the scrubber influent to monitor liquid flow, and determine gas flow using one of the specified procedures.

If you seek to monitor parameters other than those listed in paragraph (a) of this section, then you may request approval to monitor other parameters according to the procedures specified in § 63.151(f) or § 63.152(e) as described in this section.

If you monitor parameters for a control or recovery device under this subpart, then you must establish a range that indicates proper operation of the device based on the results of the most recent performance test and submit required information in the Notification of Compliance Status or permit application.

checklist: Confirm whether the scrubber controls a process vent that is subject to Subpart HHHHHHH emission limits (Table 1 or 2) and whether the scrubber is being used to demonstrate compliance with those limits.
Verify whether CPMS are required for this control device under § 63.11925(c) (i.e., whether the process vent/control device is subject to CPMS requirements).

Document the current pressure-monitoring instrumentation for the scrubber (existence and location of inlet and outlet pressure gauges and whether outlet pressure is currently measured or referenced to ambient).

Specify exactly how you propose to substitute ambient pressure for the measured outlet pressure (calculation/method, sensor locations, sampling interface) and whether that approach yields representative measurements.

Assemble performance test data and engineering rationale showing that the proposed alternative monitoring parameter (ambient pressure used for pressure-drop monitoring) adequately indicates proper scrubber operation and maintains compliance with emission limits.

Prepare or update the site-specific monitoring plan and QA/QC procedures per the CPMS requirements, including data recording frequency (≥ once every 15 minutes) and the proposed operating limits and rationale per § 63.11935(d)(2).

Identify any prior Administrator approvals you have (for the other scrubber) and determine whether those approvals are transferable or whether a new approval/notification is required for this scrubber.

Determine the appropriate regulatory path for submitting the alternative (e.g., notification of compliance status, permit application amendment, or notification of construction/reconstruction) and whether state/local permitting authority involvement is required.
Confirm that you will not implement the alternative monitoring parameter until Administrator approval is obtained, and plan to retain required monitoring under the subpart until approval is granted.
