These elements capture the key reasons in the EPA notes."}

candidates.title: Standards and compliance requirements for existing sources (Subpart LLLLLL)

criteria.criterion: if you use a wet scrubber to control emissions from polymerization process equipment or monomer recovery process equipment then you must operate a CPMS that measures and records the scrubber water flow rate at least every 15 minutes and determine and record the daily average water flow rate

if you use a wet scrubber to control polymerization process equipment then you must maintain the daily average water flow at a minimum of 50 liters per minute and shut down the polymerization reactor(s) if the water flow ceases
if you use a wet scrubber to control monomer recovery process equipment then you must maintain the daily average water flow at a minimum of 30 liters per minute

if you do not use a wet scrubber for the polymerization process equipment or the monomer recovery process equipment then you must submit a monitoring plan to EPA or the delegated authority for approval that contains the description, performance test results, an operation and maintenance plan (including CPMS), the operating parameters to be monitored, and operating parameter limits based on performance test data

if you seek to revise the established wet scrubber operating limit then you must notify the Administrator, conduct a new performance test demonstrating compliance, and establish the revised operating limit using CPMS data collected during the test runs

candidates.title: General monitoring requirements for control and recovery devices (Subpart SS)

criteria.criterion: if you are the owner or operator of a regulated source required to monitor under this subpart then the general monitoring requirements in this section apply to your control or recovery device monitoring

if you want to use alternatives to the continuous operating parameter monitoring and recordkeeping provisions identified in referenced sections then you may request Administrator approval as specified in paragraph (d)

if you want to monitor a different parameter than those established in paragraph (c)(6) or set unique monitoring parameters as directed by certain sections then you may request Administrator approval as specified in paragraph (d)

if one CPMS is used as a backup to another CPMS then you must report results from the CPMS used to meet the monitoring requirements and, if both were used during a reporting period, report results from each for the time each instrument was relied upon

candidates.title: Continuous monitoring requirements for control devices for process vents (Subpart HHHHHHH)

criteria.criterion: if you are using an absorber or acid gas scrubber to meet an emission limit in Table 1 or 2 and you are required to use CPMS under §63.11925(c) then you must install a flow meter to monitor scrubber influent liquid flow and either monitor gas stream flow (to calculate liquid-to-gas ratio) or follow one of the allowed procedures to determine gas flow

if you are using an absorber or acid gas scrubber and the scrubbing liquid is a reactant you must install and operate a pH, caustic strength, or conductivity monitoring device for the scrubber effluent as specified

if you wish to use alternatives to the continuous operating parameter monitoring listed in this section or to monitor a different parameter than established then you may request Administrator approval as specified in §§63.11985(c)(4), 63.11985(c)(5), and 63.8

if you use a control device not listed in this subpart as part of your compliance then you must submit a description of planned monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting procedures and obtain the Administrator's approval, and establish Administrator-approved operating limits

candidates.title: Batch process vent monitoring equipment (Subpart JJJ)

criteria.criterion: if you use a scrubber with an incinerator, boiler, or process heater to control halogenated batch process vents or halogenated aggregate batch vent streams then you must install a pH monitoring device with continuous recorder and a liquid flow measurement device with continuous recorder and determine gas stream flow by one of the specified procedures

if you use an absorber then you must install continuous-recording scrubbing liquid temperature and specific gravity monitoring devices, and if you use a condenser or carbon adsorber there are specific temperature or regeneration/bed-temperature monitoring requirements as specified

if you wish to monitor parameters other than those required by paragraph (c) you may request approval to monitor alternative parameters by submitting a request according to the procedures in §§63.1327(f) and 63.1335(f)

if your vent system contains bypass lines that could divert emissions away from the control device then you must either install and operate a flow indicator that reads at least once every 15 minutes at the bypass entrance or secure the bypass valve in the non-diverting position and visually inspect it monthly

candidates.title: Process vent provisions—monitoring requirements (Subpart G)

criteria.criterion: if you operate a process vent that uses a combustion device, recovery device, or recapture device to comply with §63.113 requirements then you must install the monitoring equipment specified for the type of device used (e.g., temperature monitors for incinerators, pilot-flame detectors for flares, pH and liquid flow monitors for scrubbers, etc.)

if you use a scrubber with an incinerator, boiler, or process heater in the case of halogenated vent streams then you must install a pH monitor with continuous recorder and a flow meter with continuous recorder at the scrubber influent and determine gas flow rate by one of the specified procedures

if you use a recovery device that is an absorber, condenser, or carbon adsorber as the final recovery device then you must use the specific monitoring devices identified (e.g., scrubbing liquid temperature and specific gravity monitors, condenser exit temperature monitor, or integrating regeneration stream flow and carbon bed temperature monitors)
if you want to request approval to monitor parameters other than those listed in paragraphs (a) or (b) then you must submit a request according to the procedures specified in §63.151(f) or §63.152(e)

checklist: Determine whether your facility is subject to Subpart LLLLLL (i.e., existing source standards for acrylonitrile polymerization and monomer recovery) and identify which process equipment are polymerization process equipment vs monomer recovery process equipment (40 CFR 63.11395)
Confirm whether your scrubber(s) control polymerization process equipment and/or monomer recovery process equipment and whether the scrubber is a wet scrubber (40 CFR 63.11395(c), 63.11395(e))

Measure current daily average scrubber influent water flow rates and verify whether they meet the minima: ≥50 l/min for polymerization process equipment and ≥30 l/min for monomer recovery process equipment (40 CFR 63.11395(c)(1),(c)(2))
Confirm whether you operate a CPMS that records water flow every 15 minutes and calculates daily averages, and where CPMS data are stored and retained (40 CFR 63.11395(e),(f))

Identify whether your scrubber scrubbing liquid is a reactant (e.g., caustic) and whether pH, caustic strength, or conductivity monitoring is required under the applicable subpart (40 CFR 63.11940(c)(3))

Determine whether your control system is a listed device type (absorber/acid gas scrubber, condenser, regenerative or non-regenerative adsorber, thermal oxidizer, incinerator, boiler/process heater, flare) and which specific CPMS parameters each subpart requires (40 CFR 63.11940, 63.1324, 63.114)

Verify whether your facility is required to use CPMS under the referenced subpart (e.g., §63.11925(c) or the subpart LLLLLL CPMS requirement) and whether alternative monitoring would require Administrator approval (40 CFR 63.11940(h), 63.996(d), 63.11395(i))

Assemble prior performance test reports (e.g., tests under §63.1104 of subpart YY or other referenced test methods) to demonstrate control device performance or to support a revised operating limit or alternate monitoring plan (40 CFR 63.11395(h),(k))

If planning to propose alternative monitoring, prepare the required documentation (description of device, performance test data, O&M plan and CPMS description, list of parameters to be monitored, and proposed operating limits) consistent with the cited subpart procedures and be ready to submit per the referenced approval procedures (40 CFR 63.11395(i); 63.11940(g); 63.1324(d); 63.996(d))

Confirm whether vent streams are halogenated or non-halogenated (affects whether scrubber monitoring under certain paragraphs applies) and whether bypass lines exist that could divert emissions from the scrubber (40 CFR 63.1324(c)(4); 63.114(a)(4); 63.1324(e))

Identify applicable recordkeeping and reporting obligations (e.g., monthly compliance determinations, quarterly summary reports, 2-year retention of monthly compliance determinations) and notification timelines for exceedances or deviations (40 CFR 63.11395(f),(g))

Determine whether you need to request Administrator approval under the specific sections cited (identify applicable approval procedures: e.g., §§63.999, 63.11985, 63.8, 63.1327(f), 63.1335(f), §63.151(f), §63.152(e)) and prepare to follow those procedures

candidates.title: Subpart RRRRR

criteria.criterion: If a dynamic wet scrubber is applied to meet any particulate matter emission limit in Table 1 to this subpart, then the owner/operator must maintain the daily average scrubber water flow rate and the daily average fan amperage at or above the minimum levels established in § 63.9622.

If a dynamic wet scrubber is subject to a particulate matter performance test, then site-specific operating limits for scrubber water flow rate and fan amperage must be established by measuring and recording scrubber water flow rate and fan amperage every 15 minutes during each test run and setting the operating limits as the lowest average value from the individual test runs.

If a dynamic wet scrubber is subject to the operating limits in § 63.9590(b)(2), then the owner/operator must install, operate, and maintain a continuous parametric monitoring system (CPMS) and monitor the daily average scrubber water flow rate and daily average fan amperage according to the CPMS requirements.

If the daily average scrubber water flow rate or daily average fan amperage is below the operating limits established during the initial or subsequent performance test, then the owner/operator must follow the corrective action procedures and timelines specified for dynamic wet scrubbers (including initiating and completing initial corrective action within 10 calendar days and repeating or re-testing if unsuccessful).

If the owner/operator wishes to use an alternative to the monitoring requirements for wet scrubbers (including alternative parametric limits or monitoring methods), then the owner/operator may petition the Administrator for approval of an alternative monitoring approach as allowed under the cited provisions.

If the owner/operator wishes to change an established operating limit for any air pollution control device (including fan amperage operating limits), then they must submit written notification to the Administrator, conduct a new performance test demonstrating compliance with the applicable emission limitation, and establish revised operating limits according to the applicable procedures.

candidates.title: Subpart DDD

criteria.criterion: If you want to change control device or process operating parameter levels established during performance tests, then you must notify the Administrator of your desire to expand the range and upon approval conduct additional performance tests at the proposed new parameter levels to verify compliance with the applicable emission limits.

checklist: Confirm whether each of the twelve scrubbers are dynamic wet scrubbers used to meet any particulate matter emission limit in Table 1 to Subpart RRRRR.

Determine the construction/reconstruction and start-up dates for the affected sources relative to September 25, 2019, July 28, 2020, and the January 28, 2022 milestones to know which monitoring/operating-limit timing provisions apply (see § 63.9590(b)(2), § 63.9631(c), § 63.9634(f)).
Verify whether each dynamic wet scrubber has undergone the required initial particulate matter performance test per § 63.9620 and obtain the certified performance test reports.
Obtain the raw 15-minute CPMS data recorded during each performance test run for scrubber water flow rate and fan amperage (every 15 minutes per § 63.9622(b)(1)).

Calculate the average scrubber water flow rate and average fan amperage for each individual test run and identify the lowest average values to see what the site-specific operating limits would be per § 63.9622(b)(2).

Confirm whether a CPMS that measures and records fan amperage and scrubber water flow rate every 15 minutes is installed, calibrated, and operated consistent with § 63.9631(c) and applicable CPMS requirements.

Document the proposed method for deriving a fan-amperage operating limit (e.g., percent of full load amps defined as no-load full-load amps + 10%) and compare that method to the required operating-limit derivation (lowest average from performance test runs) to determine if you need to request an alternative monitoring approach.

If you plan to use an alternative parametric limit or monitoring approach, prepare a petition/notification to the Administrator (per § 63.9590(c) and § 63.9622(f)(1)) describing the proposed alternative and the justification.

If you intend to change an established operating limit, prepare to notify the Administrator, conduct the additional performance test(s) at the proposed new parameter levels, and obtain test results demonstrating compliance with the applicable emission limits (per § 63.9622(f) and § 63.1186).

Gather and retain records needed for continuous compliance: daily average fan amperage, daily average scrubber water flow rate, performance test reports, CPMS calibration/maintenance records, and corrective-action logs (to support § 63.9634(f) and § 63.9634(l) requirements).

The approval rationale (variability as a basis for granting the alternative) is not reflected in the criteria."}

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants: Surface Coating of Automobile and Light-Duty Trucks

criteria.criterion: if the previous transfer efficiency test was conducted using the methods and conditions specified in this subpart (for transfer efficiency, ASTM D5066-91 or the EPA protocol EPA-453/R-08-002), then you are not required to conduct a new initial transfer efficiency test

if either no process or equipment changes have been made since the previous transfer efficiency test or you can demonstrate that the previous test results reliably demonstrate compliance despite changes, then you are not required to conduct a new initial transfer efficiency test

if the previous transfer efficiency test established the required operating parameters or collected sufficient data to establish the required operating parameters, then you are not required to conduct a new initial transfer efficiency test

if the previous transfer efficiency test was conducted under non-representative conditions (including during startup, shutdown, malfunction, SSM, or nonoperation), then you are not eligible to use it in lieu of a new performance test

Verify you have obtained or will obtain Administrator/enforcement authority approval to use prior test results per §63.3160(c)

candidates.title: Monitoring installation, operation, and maintenance requirements (Subpart NNNNN)

criteria.criterion: If your scrubber is a scrubber control device subject to this subpart and you want to monitor parameters other than those specified in §63.9020(e), then you may request approval to do so by submitting a monitoring plan to the Administrator under §63.8(f) that meets the requirements of §63.9025(b).

If you are required by §63.9020(e) to monitor operating parameters, then you must install, operate, and maintain each continuous monitoring system (CMS) according to the operational and data-collection requirements in §63.9025(a), including continuous operation while the process is operating, collecting data from at least four equally spaced periods each hour, and calculating hourly and daily averages as specified.

If you use a caustic scrubber or a water scrubber to meet the emission limits in Table 1 to this subpart, then you must keep records of the daily average scrubber inlet liquid or recirculating liquid flow rate (as appropriate) and the daily average scrubber effluent pH to support your compliance demonstration.

If you adopt alternative monitoring under this subpart, then you must monitor and collect data continuously (except for allowed malfunctions/QA activities) as described in §63.9035(d)–(e) and must not use data from monitor malfunctions in compliance averages and calculations.

candidates.title: Monitoring requirements for steel pickling facilities and acid regeneration plants (Subpart CCC)

criteria.criterion: If you are a steel pickling facility or an acid regeneration plant subject to this subpart, then you must conduct performance tests to measure HCl mass flows at the control device inlet and outlet or HCl concentration at the control device exit at the frequencies specified in §63.1162(a)(1).

If a wet scrubber is used as the emission control device at a facility subject to this subpart, then you must install, operate, and maintain systems to measure and record scrubber makeup water flow rate and, if required, recirculation water flow rate continuously and record at least once per shift while the scrubber is operating, and operation with flows below minimums established during performance testing requires corrective action.

If you wish to implement alternative monitoring at a facility subject to this subpart, then you may develop and implement alternative monitoring requirements only subject to approval by the Administrator.

If your facility is an acid regeneration plant subject to this subpart, then you must also monitor and record process offgas temperature continuously and record at least once every shift and determine and record proportion of excess air at least once every shift while in production, with monitoring devices certified to ±5 percent and calibrated no less frequently than annually.

candidates.title: General monitoring requirements for control and recovery devices (Subpart SS)

criteria.criterion: If you are the owner or operator of a regulated source required to monitor under this subpart, then monitoring shall be conducted as set forth in this section and the referencing subpart unless the Administrator specifies or approves minor changes in methodology or approves alternatives as provided in paragraph (b)(1)(i)–(ii) or paragraph (d) of this section.
If your device is subject to this subpart, then flow indicators are not subject to the requirements of this section.

If your device is subject to this subpart, then you must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate monitoring equipment according to manufacturer's specifications and good air pollution control practices and establish a range for monitored parameters that indicates proper operation of the control or recovery device as specified in §63.996(c)(1) and §63.996(c)(6).

If you want to monitor a different parameter than those established in paragraph (c)(6) of this section or set unique monitoring parameters, then you may request approval to do so under the alternative-monitoring provisions in §63.996(d)(2).

candidates.title: Operating limits for web coating lines (Subpart JJJJ)

criteria.criterion: If you use an add-on control device other than those listed in Table 1 to this subpart or wish to monitor an alternative parameter for a web coating line subject to this subpart, then you must apply to the Administrator for approval of alternative monitoring under §63.8(f).

If you use add-on control devices to demonstrate compliance with the emission standards in §63.3320 and do not use a solvent recovery system with a liquid-liquid material balance, then you must meet the operating limits specified in Table 1 to this subpart established during the performance test and meet them at all times after establishment.

checklist: Is the scrubber used as an emission control device to meet a specific NESHAP emission limit (identify the affected source and applicable subpart/Table)?
Is the scrubber a caustic scrubber or a water scrubber (versus another technology)?
Is the facility a steel pickling facility or an acid regeneration plant subject to Subpart CCC?
Are emissions routed to the scrubber such that the scrubber functions as the control device for the covered emissions?
Are you seeking to monitor flow indicators or flow-only parameters (note: flow indicators are excluded from Subpart SS monitoring requirements)?

Can you continuously collect CMS data at all times the process is operating and collect data from at least four equally spaced periods each hour and have valid data for at least 75% of operating hours per 24-hour period (per §63.9025(a))?
Can you calculate hourly and daily averages as required (use all valid data or at least one measured value per minute when applicable)?
Can you record daily average scrubber inlet liquid or recirculating liquid flow rate and daily average scrubber effluent pH (required if a caustic or water scrubber under Subpart NNNNN §63.9035(b))?

Can you measure and record scrubber makeup water flow and, if required, recirculation water flow continuously and record at least once per shift while operating (required under Subpart CCC §63.1162(a)(2))?

Are your monitoring devices certified to the accuracy required (e.g., ±5% where specified) and can they be calibrated at least annually per manufacturer instructions (Subpart CCC §63.1162(a)(5)/(b)(3))?
Can you establish a parameter range indicating proper operation based on a prior performance test or other allowable basis for submission (required under Subpart SS §63.996(c)(6))?

Can you prepare a written monitoring plan meeting the referenced-subpart requirements that identifies the operating parameter, explains why it demonstrates ongoing compliance, and specifies monitoring procedures (as required by §63.9025(b)(1)–(3) and §63.9025(c)(1)–(3))?

Are you prepared to submit the monitoring plan and request alternative monitoring approval to the Administrator (under §63.8(f)) and to implement any Administrator comments or required alternate monitoring scheme?
Do your existing records and data systems support the required recording frequency and retention for CMS data, performance tests, and daily/shift logs as specified in the applicable subpart?

candidates.title: Ethylene Oxide Emissions Standards for Sterilization Facilities

criteria.criterion: If your affected source is subject to an emission standard in §63.362 and you are required to monitor using EtO CEMS, then you must install and operate EtO CEMS and comply with the monitoring requirements in §63.364 and the continuous-compliance provisions in §63.363.

If you use an EtO CEMS to demonstrate compliance, then the analyzer/system must be capable of continuous EtO measurement with the required cycle time, data reduction to hourly averages, and conversion to lb/hr as specified for EtO CEMS and Appendix A procedures.

If an analyzer is not certified and operated according to the applicable Performance Specification 19 (PS 19) and the certification/QA procedures required for EtO CEMS (including the certification, RATA/gas-audit, LOD, interference, calibration drift and other QA tests), then it is not an approved EtO CEMS for demonstrating compliance without Administrator approval.

If the proposed monitoring device is not continuous in nature with an averaging time of one minute or less, then it does not meet the instrumentation requirement for methods used under §63.365(b)(5)(i) for EtO concentration measurement.

If the analyzer's measurement range or method detection limit for outlet (stack) streams is not at least an order of magnitude below the concentration equivalent of the applicable emission limit, then the analyzer does not meet the EtO test-method sensitivity requirement in §63.365(b)(5)(i)(A).

If you propose to use an alternative monitoring method or analyzer that does not meet the PS 19 certification path, then you must obtain Administrator approval for that alternative method or follow the alternative/approved-method procedures in §63.365(b)(5)(i)(D) and include the method in your monitoring plan.

If your facility uses less than 100 lb/yr of EtO and you elect the alternative periodic performance-testing compliance route, then you may avoid continuous EtO CEMS monitoring provided you follow the performance test and operating-limit monitoring procedures in §§63.363 and 63.365.

checklist: Confirm whether your sterilization source(s) are 'affected sources' under §63.362 (identify SCV, ARV, CEV, Group 1/2 room air emissions) and whether Subpart O requires EtO CEMS for those sources.
Decide whether you will demonstrate compliance via continuous EtO CEMS or via the <100 lb/yr periodic performance test path (if eligible).

Obtain the CEA Instruments ET-6200R U series technical specifications: continuous output capability, averaging/cycle time (must be ≤1 minute), measurement range, and method detection limit (MDL) for EtO.
Verify the ET-6200R's MDL and measurement range are sufficient (outlet-stream MDL should be ~1 order of magnitude below the concentration equivalent of your applicable emission limit).

Determine whether the ET-6200R (or the CEMS configuration including that analyzer) is certified to Performance Specification 19 (PS 19) or can be certified (includes PS19 Section 13 items referenced by Appendix A); obtain documentation of certification or plan for certification testing.

Confirm the system can perform and document the required QA/QC and certification tests: daily/7-day calibration drift (CD) or calibration error, RATAs/gas audits, measurement error (ME) tests, LOD tests (controlled and/or field SADL), interference tests, quarterly RAAs/CGAs/DSAs, and response-time tests.

Confirm ability to convert concentration data to lb/hr: availability and certification of stack gas flow monitoring (Part 75 requirements) and data-reduction/software to compute hourly averages and lb/hr per Appendix A equations.

Decide whether the ET-6200R would be primary, redundant backup, non-redundant backup, or temporary like-kind replacement and confirm associated certification/usage limits and additional QA requirements (e.g., 720 hr/yr limits, RATA frequency) per Appendix A provisions.

Prepare/update the electronic and hard-copy monitoring plan (per Appendix A / §63.364 monitoring-plan content requirements) including make/model/serial, sampling method, formulas, span/range, and submit via CEDRI if deploying a CEMS.
If you intend to use the ET-6200R without PS19 certification, prepare and submit a request for Administrator approval showing equivalence and planned QA, per §63.365(b)(5)(i)(D).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Natural Gas Processing Plants (Subpart HH)

criteria.criterion: If the percent VHAP content of the process fluid that is contained in or contacts a piece of ancillary equipment or compressor can be reasonably expected never to exceed 10.0 percent by weight using the methods specified in this subpart, then that piece of equipment is considered not to be in VHAP service.

If an owner or operator determines VHAP content using Method 18 of 40 CFR part 60, appendix A, or ASTM D6420-99 (2004) following the provisions of paragraph (a)(1)(ii)(A) through (D) of §63.772, then those methods are acceptable for determining whether the 10.0 percent-by-weight threshold is met.

If target compounds to be measured by ASTM D6420-99 (2004) are not listed in Table 1.1 of the ASTM method but are potentially detected by mass spectrometry, then the additional system continuing calibration check after each run (section 10.5.3 of ASTM D6420-99 (2004)) must be conducted, met, documented, and submitted with the data report.
If a piece of ancillary equipment or a compressor contains or contacts the field gas before the extraction of natural gas liquids, then that piece of equipment is considered to be in wet gas service.

If ancillary equipment or compressors at a natural gas processing plant operate in VHAP service equal to or greater than 300 hours per calendar year, then the equipment leak standards in this subpart (§63.769) apply to those pieces of equipment.

If the total VHAP concentration of any fluid contacting ancillary equipment or compressors is less than 10 percent by weight as determined according to §63.772(a), then those ancillary equipment and compressors qualify for the exemption from the equipment-leak routine monitoring requirements under this subpart.

checklist: Confirm that your facility is a natural gas processing plant (i.e., extracts NGL or fractionates mixed NGL) as defined in 40 CFR 63.761 and that Subpart HH potentially applies.

For each ancillary equipment item and compressor, identify the specific process fluid(s) (gas or liquid) that the piece contains or contacts and whether it contacts field gas prior to NGL extraction (to assess wet gas service).
For each distinct process stream, obtain a VHAP weight‑percent determination using either Method 18 (40 CFR part 60, appendix A) or ASTM D6420‑99 (2004) per §63.772(a)(1)(i)/(ii).

If using ASTM D6420‑99 (2004), verify: a) the target compounds conform to section 1.1 of the ASTM method; b) the target concentration range is between 150 ppbv and 100 ppmv; c) perform and document the additional system continuing calibration check (section 10.5.3) for compounds not listed in Table 1.1 but potentially detected by MS; and d) do not use ASTM D6420 for compounds not amenable to MS, per §63.772(a)(1)(ii)(A)-(D).

For each ancillary equipment item and compressor, calculate annual operating hours to determine if it operates in VHAP service ≥300 hours/year (triggering §63.769 requirements) or <300 hours/year (possible exemption per §63.769/§63.764).

Document and retain the analyses and demonstrations showing VHAP < 10.0 wt% (or VHAP ≥10.0 wt%) for each piece of equipment, including raw data, method used, calibration records, and any ASTM D6420 calibration-check documentation, to substantiate service determination and exemptions.

Check whether any ancillary equipment or compressors are already subject to and controlled under 40 CFR part 61 subpart V, 40 CFR part 63 subpart H, or 40 CFR part 60 subpart OOOO, since those can affect which equipment-leak requirements apply (see §63.769(b) and §63.760(g)).

Determine whether the facility is a major or area HAP source and evaluate Subpart HH applicability and compliance dates per §63.760 (facility throughput/major‑source thresholds and affected‑source lists).

If VHAP concentrations are near the 10.0% threshold, consider repeating/confirming measurements and document reasoning that values can be reasonably expected never to exceed 10.0% by weight as required by §63.772(a)(1).

Maintain records of the determinations and any supporting modeling/measurements and be prepared to submit these with notifications/reports as required by Subpart HH (referenced recordkeeping/report sections cited in the subpart).

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If required to do performance testing by a relevant standard, then the owner or operator must perform such tests within 180 days of the compliance date unless a waiver or an approved extension applies.

If a force majeure is about to occur, occurs, or has occurred and the owner/operator intends to assert it to delay testing beyond the regulatory deadline, then the owner/operator must notify the Administrator in writing as soon as practicable (and before the performance test deadline unless delayed notice is caused by the force majeure) and provide a written description, rationale, measures to minimize delay, and a proposed date to conduct the performance test.

If a request for an extension of the performance test deadline due to force majeure is submitted, then granting the extension is solely within the Administrator's discretion and until an extension is approved the owner/operator remains strictly subject to the requirements of this part.

If the owner/operator is unable to conduct a scheduled performance test due to unforeseeable circumstances beyond their control, then the owner/operator must notify the Administrator as soon as practicable and without delay prior to the scheduled performance test date and specify the rescheduled date.

If a performance test is conducted, then it must be conducted under conditions specified by the Administrator based on representative normal operating conditions and operations during startup, shutdown, and malfunction shall not constitute representative conditions for performance tests and tests may not be conducted during periods of malfunction.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Iron and Steel Foundries (Subpart EEEEE)

criteria.criterion: If you are an iron and steel foundry subject to Subpart EEEEE, then you must conduct a performance test no later than 180 calendar days after the compliance date specified in § 63.7683 to demonstrate initial compliance with each emissions limitation that applies to you.

If initial compliance for a work practice standard or an operation and maintenance requirement under Subpart EEEEE is not demonstrated using a performance test, then you must demonstrate initial compliance no later than 30 calendar days after the compliance date.

If you commenced construction or reconstruction during specified timeframes referenced in this section, then you must follow the special initial compliance timing (e.g., dates in paragraph (c) and (d)) including possible alternate test timing under § 63.7(a)(2)/(ix).

If you conduct a performance test for Subpart EEEEE, then the test must be under conditions representative of normal operations (excluding startup and shutdown), you may not test during malfunctions, and you must record process information that documents representativeness.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Metal Melting Furnaces and Foundry Operations (Subpart ZZZZZ)

criteria.criterion: If your metal melting furnace or building housing foundry operations is subject to the emissions limits in § 63.10895, then you must conduct an initial performance test within 180 days of your compliance date and report the results in your notification of compliance status.

If you are an existing iron and steel foundry and have a prior performance test for PM or total metal HAP conducted within the last 5 years that meets the subpart's method and procedural requirements and either no process changes have occurred or you can demonstrate the prior results remain reliable, then you may choose to submit those prior results instead of conducting a new test, provided you notify the Administrator of that intent no later than 60 days after your compliance date.

If you are required to electronically submit reports through CEDRI/CDX, then you may assert a claim of force majeure for failure to timely submit by notifying the Administrator in writing as soon as practicable, providing a written description of the force majeure, a rationale linking it to the delayed submission, measures taken to minimize delay, and the proposed submittal date, and the decision to allow an extension is solely within the Administrator's discretion.

If you conduct a performance test under Subpart ZZZZZ, then you must conduct it under conditions representative of normal operations (excluding periods of startup, shutdown, and malfunction), may not test during malfunctions, must record supporting process information, and conduct subsequent tests at required intervals (e.g., every 5 years or when process changes likely increase HAP emissions).

checklist: Determine which specific NESHAP subpart(s) your facility is subject to (Subpart EEEEE and/or Subpart ZZZZZ) and identify the applicable compliance date(s) in the relevant standard(s).
Confirm whether an initial performance test was required for each affected emission unit and the original scheduled performance test date(s).

Verify whether the 180-day (or 30-day for certain work-practice/OM) initial test deadline has passed or will pass, using the compliance date from the applicable subpart (see 40 CFR 63.7730(a) and 63.10898(a)).

Document the exact dates, durations, and technical details of the furnace malfunctions and the labor strikes, and whether these events occurred within the period that could have caused or did cause a delay in testing beyond the regulatory deadline.

Confirm whether the events that delayed testing qualify as circumstances beyond your control (force majeure) and whether they prevented conducting representative testing (malfunction vs. inability to test).

Confirm whether you provided (or will provide) written notification to the Administrator as soon as practicable after learning the event may cause or has caused a delay, and whether that notification occurred before the performance test deadline (unless delayed notice was itself caused by the force majeure).

Prepare the written description required for a force majeure claim: description of the event, rationale linking it to the delayed testing, measures taken to minimize delay, and a proposed date for conducting the performance test (per 40 CFR 63.7(a)(4)(ii) and 63.10899(g)).

If you rescheduled a planned test because of unforeseeable circumstances, confirm you notified the Administrator as soon as practicable and before the scheduled test date and specified the rescheduled date (per 40 CFR 63.7(b)(2)).

If you have submitted a site-specific test plan or intend to, verify submission and timing relative to the 60-day notification requirement for performance tests and any Administrator requests (40 CFR 63.7(c) and 63.7(b)(1)).

If relying on prior performance tests (Subpart ZZZZZ), verify the prior test is within five years, used required methods/procedures, and either no process changes occurred or you can demonstrate the prior results remain reliable; if so, prepare the written notification to the Administrator within 60 days after your compliance date (40 CFR 63.10898(a)(1)-(2)).

If you submit reports or test results electronically via CEDRI/CDX, confirm whether an electronic submission failure applies and whether you need to assert force majeure or EPA outage per the electronic-submittal provisions (40 CFR 63.9(k) and 63.10899(g)).

Collect and preserve supporting records showing steps taken to minimize delays, communications with the Administrator, test scheduling records, contractor/test lab availability, and any safety or access constraints that prevented testing.

Document that any performance test, when conducted, will be under representative normal operating conditions and not during startup, shutdown, or malfunction, and retain process records that demonstrate representativeness (40 CFR 63.7(e)(1) and 63.10898(c)).

Be prepared that any extension or acceptance of a force majeure claim is discretionary by the Administrator and that until approval you remain subject to the regulatory requirements (40 CFR 63.7(a)(4)(iii)-(iv)).

candidates.title: Cellulose Products Manufacturing (Subpart UUUU)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate a cellulose products manufacturing operation located at a major source of HAP emissions, then your operation is subject to this subpart.
If the operation is a cellulose food casing operation (as defined) it is included in the Miscellaneous Viscose Processes source category covered by this subpart.

If a continuous monitoring system (CMS) is required by this subpart for an affected source, then you must develop and make available a site-specific monitoring plan that addresses installation location, equipment and performance specifications, and performance evaluation procedures (including calibrations).

If a CEMS is used to measure hydrogen sulfide or organic HAP emissions pursuant to this subpart, then the CEMS must be installed, operated, and maintained according to the applicable performance specification listed (PS-7 for H2S; PS-9 for GC measurement of organic HAP; PS-8 or PS-15 as applicable for VOC/FTIR).

If you have CMS required by this subpart, then you must operate and maintain the CMS in continuous operation according to the site-specific monitoring plan and conduct performance evaluations according to that plan.
If flow to a control device could be intermittent, then you must install, calibrate, and operate a flow indicator at the inlet or outlet of the control device to identify periods of no flow.
If you must monitor continuously, then you may not use data recorded during monitoring malfunctions, repairs, QA/QC activities, or periods of no flow in data averages and compliance calculations.

candidates.title: General Provisions — Monitoring requirements (Subpart A, 40 CFR 63.8)

criteria.criterion: If you seek to use an alternative monitoring procedure in lieu of a monitoring method specified in a relevant standard, then you must submit a written application to the Administrator and obtain approval per the procedures and timelines in § 63.8(f).

If a CMS is required by the relevant standard, then the CMS is subject to the provisions of § 63.8 (including installation, operation, maintenance, QA/QC, and recordkeeping obligations) and must be maintained and operated in a manner consistent with good air pollution control practices.

If you propose to use an alternative monitoring method as the performance test method, then the application must be submitted at least 60 days before the scheduled performance evaluation and include the elements described in § 63.8(f) and the site-specific performance evaluation test plan requirements of § 63.8(e)(3).

If a CMS is out-of-control (e.g., calibration drift exceeds limits or fails an audit), then you must take corrective action, repeat the necessary tests, and report the out-of-control period and corrective actions as required.

If a CMS is a CEMS or CPMS, then the system must meet the minimum cycle/frequency and data reduction requirements specified in § 63.8 (e.g., CEMS cycle = one cycle per successive 15-minute period; data reduced to 1-hour averages from four or more equally spaced data points unless otherwise specified).

If you develop a CMS quality control program, then it must include written procedures for initial and subsequent calibration, calibration drift determination and adjustment, preventive maintenance, data recording and reporting, accuracy audits, and corrective action procedures, and these procedures must be kept on record.

checklist: Confirm whether your facility is a 'major source' of HAP (any single HAP ≥ 9.1 Mg/yr (10 tpy) or total HAP ≥ 23 Mg/yr (25 tpy)) per 40 CFR 63.5485(b).

Confirm that the process at the affected unit is a cellulose food casing operation (match your equipment and processes to the 'cellulose food casing operation' / 'cellulose food casing process unit' definitions in 40 CFR 63.5610).

Determine whether Subpart UUUU requires CMS/CEMS/CPMS at the specific emission points you are monitoring (review applicable affected-source-specific monitoring provisions in this subpart and permits).

Identify the pollutants your Baseline-MOCON Model 8900 will measure (hydrogen sulfide and carbon disulfide) and decide which performance specification applies (e.g., H2S → PS-7; GC-based organic HAP → PS-9) per 40 CFR 63.5545(e)(1)(i)-(iii).

Determine whether the Baseline-MOCON 8900 meets the applicable performance specification(s) (PS-7, PS-9, PS-8, or PS-15) or whether it would be an alternative monitoring method that requires Administrator approval under 40 CFR 63.8(f).

If the new analyzer does not meet the specified performance specification(s), prepare an application for alternative monitoring per 40 CFR 63.8(f)(4) that includes a description addressing the definition of monitoring in § 63.2 and a site-specific performance evaluation test plan per 40 CFR 63.8(e)(3).

If you intend to use the alternative method as the performance test method, plan to submit the application and performance evaluation test plan at least 60 days before the scheduled performance evaluation per 40 CFR 63.8(f)(4)(i) and 40 CFR 63.8(e)(3)(i).

Update your site-specific monitoring plan to address sampling-probe location, equipment and analyzer specifications, data collection/reduction, performance evaluation procedures, and calibration procedures as required by 40 CFR 63.5545(a)–(c).

Plan for and document required performance evaluations, daily/periodic calibration drift checks, ongoing QA/QC, preventive maintenance, and recordkeeping and reporting procedures in accordance with 40 CFR 63.5545 and 40 CFR 63.8 (including procedures for handling out-of-control periods).
If a control device has intermittent flow, verify installation, calibration, and operation of a flow indicator at the inlet or outlet of the control device per 40 CFR 63.5545(g).

Retain records of performance evaluation plans, calibrations, audits, out-of-control periods, corrective actions, and prior versions of the performance evaluation plan for the retention periods specified in 40 CFR 63.8(d)(3) and associated subpart provisions.

These criteria capture the EPA note that modification is allowed but full (linearity-type) calibration is still required."}

candidates.title: General Provisions (Performance testing requirements)

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator is required by a relevant standard to perform a performance test and has not obtained a waiver under this section, then the owner or operator must conduct the required performance tests within 180 days of the compliance date.

If an owner or operator can demonstrate to the Administrator's satisfaction that the affected source is meeting the relevant standard(s) on a continuous basis, or is operating under an extension of compliance or has requested an extension that is still under consideration, then individual performance tests may be waived upon written application to the Administrator.

If a force majeure delays testing beyond the regulatory deadline and the owner/operator notifies the Administrator promptly with a description and proposed new test date, then the owner/operator may request an extension of the performance test deadline subject to the Administrator's discretion.

If an owner or operator proposes to use an alternative test method instead of the method specified in the relevant standard, then the owner/operator must notify the Administrator at least 60 days before the test, validate the method using Method 301, and submit the validation results for approval (or be authorized to proceed under the timelines in §63.7(f)).

candidates.title: Extension of compliance, and performance test, monitoring, recordkeeping and reporting waivers and alternatives

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator requests a waiver of an individual performance test in writing and the Administrator determines the source is meeting the relevant standard(s) on a continuous basis or the source is operating under (or has requested) an extension of compliance, then the Administrator may grant the waiver.

If an owner or operator submits an application for a waiver of an initial performance test, then that application must accompany any request for an extension of compliance or be submitted at least 60 days before the performance test if a site-specific test plan is not submitted.

If an owner or operator requests a waiver of a subsequent performance test, then the application may accompany required compliance reports but must be submitted at least 60 days before the scheduled performance test if a site-specific test plan is not submitted.

If installation of the required monitoring or test method would not provide accurate measurements or would be impractical (for example, due to interferences or infrequent operation), then the Administrator may approve alternative monitoring methods or procedures upon written application and justification.

candidates.title: Performance test requirements for new and existing sources (PM testing procedures and exceptions)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an existing affected source and a prior performance test using the same methods was conducted within the past 5 years and no process changes have been made since that test, then you are not required to conduct a new performance test.

If you own or operate an existing affected source and a prior performance test was conducted within the past 5 years using the same methods but process changes have occurred, then you may avoid a new performance test only if you demonstrate that the prior test results, with or without adjustments, reliably demonstrate compliance despite the process changes.

If you are required to conduct a performance test for PM, then it must be conducted within 180 days of your compliance date (unless an exception applies) and the test must follow §63.7 plus the PM test methods specified (Methods 1/1A, 2-series, 3-series, 4, and Method 5 or 17) with sampling at the outlet of the control device prior to any release to the atmosphere.

If you conduct the PM performance test, then during the test you must operate each emissions source within ±10 percent of its normal process rate and monitor and record the process rate during the test.

candidates.title: Initial compliance requirements for large copper or other nonferrous foundries

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an existing affected source at a large copper or other nonferrous foundry and a prior performance test using the same methods was conducted within the past 5 years and no process changes have been made since that test, then you are not required to conduct a new performance test.

If you own or operate an existing affected source at a large copper or other nonferrous foundry and a prior performance test was conducted within the past 5 years using the same methods but process changes have occurred, then you are not required to conduct a new performance test only if you demonstrate to the satisfaction of the permitting authority that the prior test results, with or without adjustments, reliably demonstrate compliance despite process changes.

If you are required to conduct an initial performance test at a large copper or other nonferrous foundry, then you must perform the test within 180 days of the compliance date and follow §63.7 and the specific test methods and procedures listed (Method 1/1A, 2-series, 3-series, 4, and Method 5/5D or 17); three valid runs are required and each run must cover at least one production cycle.

checklist: Determine which NESHAP subpart(s) actually apply to the argon stir stations (confirm whether your source is covered by the subpart(s) associated with PM testing or foundry NESHAPs).
Confirm whether the argon stir stations' emissions are vented to the baghouse that also controls the ladle metallurgical furnace and document the ducting and control-device outlet(s).

Check whether a prior performance test at the baghouse outlet (using the same PM methods referenced in the applicable subpart) was conducted within the past 5 years and obtain the test report and methods used.
Confirm whether any process changes affecting emissions from the argon stir stations or ladle furnace have occurred since the prior test (list dates and descriptions).
If there were process changes, prepare an analysis demonstrating whether the prior test results (with or without adjustments) still reliably demonstrate compliance.

Assemble continuous compliance records and monitoring data that would show the source is meeting the relevant standard(s) on a continuous basis (operation logs, continuous monitoring, maintenance records, visible emissions observations, control device operation records).
Verify whether you have an active extension of compliance or have already requested one (and gather the extension request or approval documentation, if any).

If planning to request a waiver, prepare a written waiver application including justification (technical impracticality, interference from co-vented sources, or economic infeasibility) and any supporting data; plan to submit it at least 60 days before the scheduled performance test if no site-specific test plan is being submitted.

If the testing difficulty arises because the baghouse exhaust contains emissions from other sources, document whether you can isolate the affected emission point(s) for testing (temporary total enclosure or shutdown of other sources) per the relevant subpart test method requirements.

If proposing an alternative test method or alternative monitoring location due to interference from co-vented sources, prepare Method 301 validation and plan to notify the Administrator at least 60 days before testing.

Document whether a force majeure or other unavoidable circumstance prevents testing within 180 days, and prepare the notice describing the event, measures to minimize delay, and proposed new test date for submission to the Administrator.
If conducting a PM performance test, be prepared to operate the source within ±10% of normal process rate during tests and to monitor/record process rate for the test period.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Hydrochloric Acid Production (Subpart NNNNN)

criteria.criterion: If you own or operate an HCl production facility that produces a liquid HCl product at a concentration of 30 weight percent or greater during normal operations and the facility is located at, or is part of, a major source of HAP, then the facility is subject to this subpart.
If the HCl production facility is part of a chlor-alkali facility producing HCl through direct synthesis of hydrogen and chlorine, then the facility is not subject to this subpart.

If all gaseous streams containing HCl and Cl2 from HCl process vents, HCl storage tanks, and HCl transfer operations are recycled or routed to another process prior to being discharged to the atmosphere, then the HCl production facility is not subject to this subpart.

If you use a caustic scrubber control device and conduct a performance test, then you must establish the minimum operating limit for scrubber inlet or recirculating liquid flow rate based on the flow rates measured during the performance test and must establish minimum and maximum operating limits for scrubber effluent pH based on the effluent pH values measured during the performance test.

If you use a caustic scrubber or a water scrubber/absorber to meet the emission limits, then you must keep records of the daily average scrubber inlet liquid or recirculating liquid flow rate and the daily average scrubber effluent pH to support your compliance demonstration.

If you are required by §63.9020(e) to monitor operating parameters, then you must install, operate, and maintain each continuous monitoring system (CMS) according to the specifications in §63.9025(a), including collecting data at least four equally spaced periods each hour and operating the CMS and collecting data at all times the process is operating.

If you wish to monitor operating parameters other than those specified in §63.9020(e) (for example, scrubbing liquid concentration rather than effluent pH), then you may request approval by submitting a monitoring plan to the Administrator under §63.8(f) as described in §63.9025(b).

If you use a caustic scrubber control device, then the device is an add-on device that mixes an aqueous stream or slurry containing a caustic substance with exhaust gases from an HCl process vent, HCl storage tank, or HCl transfer operation to control emissions of HCl and/or Cl2 (i.e., it meets the subpart's definition of caustic scrubber control device).
citations: 40 CFR 63.9075 (definition of caustic scrubber control device)

criteria.criterion: If you conduct a performance test for applicable emissions, then you must develop a site-specific test plan and conduct at least three separate test runs (each at least 1 hour) under representative conditions and not during startup, shutdown, or malfunction, as specified in §63.9020(a)(1)–(4).

If a performance test for an emission point was conducted within the previous 5-year period using the same test methods and either no deliberate process changes have been made since the test or you can demonstrate the prior results still reliably demonstrate compliance, then you are not required to conduct a new performance test for that emission point and the previous operating limits are sufficient for monitoring.

If you do not conduct a performance test for an HCl storage tank or HCl transfer operation that is not routed to a control device that also controls HCl process vent emissions, then you may prepare a design evaluation addressing vent composition, liquid-to-vapor ratio, scrubbing liquid flow rate and concentration, temperature, and reaction kinetics (or use engineering assessments/manufacturer recommendations) to establish operating limits.

checklist: Confirm whether your facility is an HCl production facility that produces liquid HCl product ≥ 30 wt% during normal operations.
Confirm whether the plant is a major source of HAP (≥ 10 t/yr single HAP or ≥ 25 t/yr combined HAP).
Confirm whether the facility is part of a chlor-alkali operation producing HCl via direct synthesis (exemption under §63.8985(d)).
Confirm whether all gaseous streams containing HCl/Cl2 are routed/recycled to another process prior to atmospheric discharge (exemption under §63.8985(f)).
Confirm that the Irgafos V-47 device is operated as an add-on caustic scrubber for HCl/Cl2 control (matches definition in §63.9075).
Determine whether the scrubber also controls HCl process vent emissions (affects eligibility for design evaluation in §63.9020(c)).

Decide whether you will conduct a performance test or rely on a design evaluation/engineering assessment; if a test, prepare a site-specific test plan and be prepared for ≥3 runs of ≥1 hour each under representative conditions per §63.9020(a).

If relying on previous performance testing, verify that a test was performed within the last 5 years, that it used the same methods, and that no deliberate process changes have occurred (or you can justify reliability) per §63.9020(d).
During any performance test, record scrubber recirculating/inlet liquid flow rates and scrubber effluent pH values to establish operating limits per §63.9020(e)(1).

If you want to use scrubbing liquid concentration (e.g., ≥ 2 wt% caustic) as an alternative operating parameter, prepare and be ready to submit a §63.8(f) monitoring plan as allowed by §63.9025(b) explaining why that parameter demonstrates ongoing compliance.
Verify ability to install/operate/maintain CMS that collects data at least four equally spaced periods per hour and produces required hourly/daily averages per §63.9025(a) and §63.9035.
Confirm capability to retain records of daily average recirculating/inlet flow rate and daily average effluent pH (or other approved monitored parameters) as required by §63.9035(b).

Document whether the minimum recirculation flow rate of 65 gpm and any proposed effluent pH and scrubbing liquid concentration values were measured during representative performance testing (required to establish those values as operating limits under §63.9020(e)(1)).

If proposing alternative monitoring parameters, prepare the monitoring plan to identify the parameter, justify appropriateness for demonstrating continued control efficiency, and specify monitoring procedures as required by §63.9025(b)(1)–(3).

These criteria capture EPA’s stated reason that it cannot approve the requested alternative parameters without additional performance testing data to demonstrate compliance."}

candidates.title: Subpart R (Bulk gasoline terminals)

criteria.criterion: If a bulk gasoline terminal is subject to the provisions in § 63.422(b)(1) and uses a carbon adsorption system, then a continuous emissions monitoring system (CEMS) capable of measuring organic compound concentration must be installed in the exhaust air stream.

If a bulk gasoline terminal is subject to the provisions in § 63.422(b)(1) and uses a refrigeration condenser system, then a continuous parameter monitoring system (CPMS) capable of measuring temperature must be installed immediately downstream from the outlet to the condenser section (or alternatively a CEMS may be installed).

If a bulk gasoline terminal is subject to the provisions in § 63.422(b)(1) and uses a thermal oxidation system, then a CPMS capable of measuring temperature must be installed in the firebox or in the ductwork immediately downstream from the firebox before any substantial heat exchange (unless an alternative parameter is approved).

If a bulk gasoline terminal is subject to the provisions in § 63.422(b)(1) and uses a flare meeting § 63.11(b), then a heat-sensing device (e.g., ultraviolet beam sensor or thermocouple) must be installed near the pilot light to indicate presence of a flame.

If a bulk gasoline terminal owner/operator demonstrates to the Administrator's satisfaction that an alternative operating parameter demonstrates continuous compliance with the emission standard in § 63.422(b) (or § 60.112b(a)(3)(ii)), then monitoring an alternative parameter (instead of the parameters listed) will be allowed.

candidates.title: Subpart BBBBBB (Bulk gasoline terminal monitoring and testing)

criteria.criterion: If a bulk gasoline terminal is subject to the emission standard in item 1(b) of Table 2 to this subpart, then it must comply with the testing and monitoring requirements in § 63.11092 (including conducting performance testing or qualifying for alternatives in paragraphs (a)(1)–(4)).

If a bulk gasoline terminal uses a thermal oxidation system, then the owner/operator must install a CPMS to measure temperature in the firebox or ductwork before substantial heat exchange, except that as an alternative the presence of the pilot flame may be monitored with a heat-sensing device that provides a positive/negative parameter value.

If a bulk gasoline terminal chooses to monitor the presence of the thermal oxidation pilot flame as allowed under § 63.11092(b)(1)(iii)(B), then the owner/operator must develop and submit a monitoring and inspection plan and ensure the system automatically prevents gasoline loading when the pilot flame is absent and performs daily verification and semi-annual preventive maintenance, with records of alarm/shutdowns and corrective actions.

If an owner/operator seeks to monitor an operating parameter other than those listed (including pilot flame in lieu of temperature or other alternatives), then the alternative parameter will be allowed only upon demonstrating to the Administrator's satisfaction that the alternative demonstrates continuous compliance with the emission standard in § 63.11088(a).

candidates.title: Subpart A (General provisions: control devices and work practices)

criteria.criterion: If a facility uses a flare to comply with an applicable subpart, then the flare must be operated with a flame present at all times and the presence of the flare pilot flame shall be monitored using a thermocouple or any other equivalent device to detect presence of a flame.

If owners or operators use flares to comply with provisions of this part, then they must monitor the control devices to assure operation and maintenance in conformance with their designs and follow monitoring provisions provided in the applicable subparts.

candidates.title: Subpart G (Process vent provisions—monitoring requirements)

criteria.criterion: If a process vent uses a combustion device (including a flare) to comply with § 63.113, then monitoring equipment is required and where a flare is used the owner/operator must install a device capable of continuously detecting the presence of a pilot flame (e.g., thermocouple, ultraviolet beam sensor, infrared sensor).

If an owner/operator of a process vent wishes to monitor parameters other than those specified in § 63.114(a) (for example, replacing temperature monitoring with another parameter), then the owner/operator must request approval under the procedures specified in § 63.151(f) or § 63.152(e).

checklist: Confirm whether the facility is a bulk gasoline terminal and whether it is subject to § 63.422(b)(1) or to the emission standard/item referenced in Table 2 of Subpart BBBBBB (i.e., applicability to § 63.11092).
Identify which vapor control device(s) are used for the affected loading racks or storage tanks: carbon adsorption, refrigeration condenser, thermal oxidation (thermal oxidizer), or flare.

If using a thermal oxidation system: determine whether existing monitoring is temperature-based in the firebox/ductwork and whether temperature data from a performance test exists to set operating limits.

If proposing pilot-flame monitoring instead of firebox temperature: prepare a monitoring and inspection plan that documents how pilot monitoring demonstrates continuous compliance and whether the system will automatically prevent gasoline loading when the pilot is absent (and be prepared to submit this to the Administrator).

Confirm whether the flare or thermal oxidizer pilot monitoring device type (thermocouple, UV beam, IR sensor) provides a positive/negative parameter and meets the daily/ongoing verification, alarm/shutdown, and recordkeeping requirements cited (including semi-annual maintenance and logs of activations and corrective actions).

Assemble performance test history and dates (e.g., initial performance test and any tests within last 5 years) and determine whether prior test data meet the criteria in § 63.11092(e) to establish operating limits or whether a new performance test is required.

Verify that proposed pilot-flame monitoring and any automatic loading interlock will function during intermittent loading operations and that monitoring covers periods when gasoline vapors are being displaced to the vapor processor (i.e., while loading occurs).
Check permit or enforceable state/local rules that might specify an approved monitored parameter or operating limit (if such a parameter is in your permit, § 63.11092(b)(5)(i) may apply).

Confirm that any flare meets Subpart A operational requirements (pilot present at all times when emissions may be vented, and design/velocity/heat-content requirements if relying on those provisions) to ensure substitution of pilot monitoring is consistent with broader flare requirements.

Prepare documentation/calculations to demonstrate to the Administrator how the alternative parameter (pilot-flame monitoring) demonstrates continuous compliance with the applicable emission standard (e.g., data, rationale for operating parameter value, monitoring frequency, averaging time) as required by the cited provisions.

It does mention other approval paths (e.g., §§63.151/63.152) but omits the two specific regulatory provisions cited by EPA, so only some key reasons are captured."}

candidates.title: Monitoring requirements

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator operates a new, reconstructed, or existing steel pickling facility or acid regeneration plant subject to this subpart, then they must conduct performance tests to measure HCl mass flows or HCl concentration at the control device inlet and outlet and must install, operate, and maintain systems to measure and record the appropriate operating parameters for their control device.

If a wet scrubber is used as the emission control device, then the owner or operator must install, operate, and maintain continuous measurement and recording of scrubber makeup water flow rate and, if required, recirculation water flow rate, with recordings at least once per shift while the scrubber is operating and corrective action required if operation is below minimum values established during performance testing.

If the owner or operator wishes to implement alternative monitoring requirements for sources subject to this subpart, then they may develop and implement alternative monitoring requirements only with approval by the Administrator.

candidates.title: What are my monitoring installation, operation, and maintenance requirements?

criteria.criterion: If you are required by § 63.9020(e) to monitor an operating parameter, then you must install, operate, and maintain each continuous monitoring system (CMS) and collect data at all times the process is operating, collect data from at least four equally spaced periods each hour, meet the valid-data and averaging requirements, and record inspection/calibration/validation results as specified in your site-specific monitoring plan.

If you use a scrubber control device and wish to monitor parameters other than those specified in § 63.9020(e), then you may request approval in accordance with § 63.8(f) by submitting a monitoring plan that (1) identifies the operating parameter to ensure control efficiency is maintained, (2) explains why it is appropriate, and (3) identifies the specific monitoring procedures.

If you request to monitor alternative parameters, then your request must include the description of each affected source and parameter, methods to demonstrate the parameter’s validity, frequency/content of monitoring and reporting (if not continuous), supporting calculations, and averaging time as specified in § 63.9025(f).

candidates.title: General monitoring requirements for control and recovery devices

criteria.criterion: If you are the owner or operator of a regulated source required to monitor under this subpart, then monitoring shall be conducted as set forth in this section and in the relevant sections of this subpart unless the Administrator specifies or approves minor changes in methodology or approves alternatives.

If you want alternatives to the continuous operating parameter monitoring and recordkeeping provisions or want to monitor a different parameter or set unique monitoring parameters, then you may request approval to use alternatives as provided in paragraph (d) of this section.

If you install and operate continuous parameter monitoring systems (CPMS), then they must be installed, calibrated, maintained, and operated according to manufacturer’s specifications or other written procedures and be operated in a manner consistent with good air pollution control practices, with prompt repair or replacement for routine malfunctions.

candidates.title: What are my monitoring alternatives?

criteria.criterion: If you propose to use alternative monitoring approaches for a wet scrubber or other control device (including monitoring other process or control device operating parameters), then you may request approval and, where specific alternatives are described (e.g., alternatives for measuring gas flow rate, pressure drop checks, pH/alkalinity checks, or automated data compression), you must meet the conditions and procedures specified for each alternative.

If you wish to request approval to monitor parameters other than those required in the subpart, then you must submit a request to the Administrator that explains why the alternate parameter is appropriate and must include the monitoring plan elements and QA provisions required by this section.

checklist: Confirm whether your facility is a steel pickling facility or an acid regeneration plant that is subject to Subpart CCC.
Confirm whether the HCl bubbler control devices are considered a wet scrubber or another type of control device under the applicable subpart definitions.

Assemble existing performance test data: HCl inlet/outlet mass flows or concentrations and the minimum operating parameter values (e.g., makeup water flow, recirculation flow) established during performance testing.

Determine whether you have continuous monitoring systems currently installed and whether they meet CMS requirements (data collection at least four equally spaced periods per hour, ≥75% valid data per 24-hr period, hourly and daily averaging methods) per 40 CFR 63.9025(a).

Decide precisely which alternative parameters you want to propose (e.g., minimum dipleg immersion depth, maximum time between liquid change-outs) and how they relate to control efficiency demonstrated in performance tests.

Prepare a monitoring plan per § 63.8(f) and 40 CFR 63.9025(b)/(f) that: identifies the parameter(s), explains why they demonstrate ongoing compliance, describes monitoring procedures, specifies frequency/averaging time, provides supporting calculations, and specifies performance specifications and QA/QC.

Confirm that monitoring instruments meet manufacturer certification and calibration requirements (accuracy within 5% and at least annual calibration) where required by the referencing subpart (e.g., 40 CFR 63.1162(a)(5)).
Verify procedures and resources to record inspection, calibration, and validation checks as required in your site-specific monitoring plan.

Confirm you will not implement the proposed alternative monitoring until you receive approval from the Administrator (and determine whether to submit the request in an initial notification, notification of construction/reconstruction, or at any time as allowed by the applicable subpart).

Prepare documentation to demonstrate that proposed operating limits (e.g., dipleg immersion depth, maximum liquid change-out interval) represent the conditions when the control device meets the emission limitation (include test data, rationale, and any O&M procedures tied to corrective action).
Identify how you will demonstrate and maintain prompt repair/replacement and good O&M practices for any CPMS or CMS as required by 40 CFR 63.996(c) if that subpart applies.

If proposing noncontinuous monitoring, specify the proposed monitoring frequency, data averaging method, and how you will meet the required percentage of valid data or provide a rationale for alternate validity criteria.
