candidates.title: Subpart VVVV

criteria.criterion: If your facility uses enclosures that route captured emissions to an add-on control device (for example, an RTO), then you must install and record either the gas volumetric flow rate or the duct static pressure in the duct from each enclosure to the add-on control device.

If you have a permanent total enclosure as defined in Method 204 (Appendix M to 40 CFR part 51), then the operating limits for that permanent total enclosure are specified in Table 4 to this subpart and must be used.

If any enclosure contains bypass lines that could divert emissions away from the add-on control device, then you must monitor or secure the bypass valve/closure in a nondiverting position using one of the specified methods (flow control position indicator, car-seal/lock-and-key, valve position monitoring, or automatic shutdown) and record inspections/occurrences.

If you install pressure measurement devices (including duct static pressure sensors or pressure drop sensors), then those sensors must be located to provide representative measurements, minimize pulsation/vibration/corrosion, have daily pressure tap checks, specified calibration checks, and at least monthly integrity inspections as described.

If you establish operating limits based on an initial emission test, then during that emission test you must monitor and record either volumetric flow rate or duct static pressure at least once every 15 minutes during each of the three test runs and use the three-run average as the minimum operating limit.

candidates.title: Subpart A

criteria.criterion: If an applicable subpart of part 63 refers you to §63.11, then the control device and alternative work practice requirements in §63.11 apply to your facility for administrative convenience.

If the applicable subpart requires monitoring with a 40 CFR part 60, appendix A-7, Method 21 monitor, then you may instead elect to use the alternative optical gas imaging work practice and must follow the procedures, daily instrument checks, survey, recordkeeping, and reporting requirements in §63.11(c)–(e).

candidates.title: Subpart EEEEE

criteria.criterion: If you are seeking to use an alternative monitoring method to demonstrate compliance with VOHAP emissions limits for automated pallet cooling lines or automated shakeout lines at a new iron and steel foundry, then you may request approval and must submit a monitoring plan containing the items in §63.7747(c) and not begin using the alternative method until the Administrator approves it.

If you wish to request approval for an alternative monitoring method at any point (including in the notification of construction/reconstruction), then you may submit the request at any time as allowed by §63.7747(b).

candidates.title: Subpart QQQQQ

criteria.criterion: If you use a control technique other than solvent recovery and/or solvent substitution and wish to use an alternative method to demonstrate compliance with the emission limitations in §63.9500(a) and (b), then you may request approval and must submit the proposed testing, monitoring, recordkeeping, reporting, and the proposed basis for demonstrating compliance as required in §63.9570(c), and you must not begin use of the alternative until Administrator approval.

If you are seeking approval based on previously performed testing, then you must submit the test results, a description of procedures followed in testing, and pertinent testing conditions as specified in §63.9570(c)(1).

checklist: Verify whether each enclosure at your facility is a permanent total enclosure as defined by Method 204 (Appendix M to 40 CFR part 51).
Verify that emissions from each enclosure are routed to the regenerative thermal oxidizer (RTO) (i.e., confirm the RTO is the add-on control device for each enclosure).

Identify any bypass lines that could divert emissions from an enclosure to the atmosphere and document whether those bypass valves are secured, monitored, or equipped with automatic shutdowns per §63.5725(c).

Document current monitoring points and methods: confirm where facial velocity through natural draft openings is measured now (locations, frequency, sensors used) and whether those are separate from the duct-to-RTO locations.

Confirm you can install duct static pressure sensors at representative locations between each enclosure and the RTO that meet the placement, pulsation/vibration mitigation, daily tap checks, calibration schedule, and monthly inspection requirements in §63.5725(f)(4).

Plan for the required performance test monitoring: confirm ability to record duct static pressure or flow at least once every 15 minutes during each of three test runs and to calculate the three-run average to set the operating limit as required by §63.5725(f)(5)(i)-(ii).

Determine whether your applicable NESHAP subpart(s) reference §63.11 or require Method 21 monitoring, and if so, decide whether the optical gas imaging alternative work practice in §63.11(c)-(e) is applicable.

Assemble a monitoring plan consistent with the applicable alternative-monitoring procedures in the provided subparts (describe control technique, monitors and parameters, test results, proposed operating limits, QA/QC, measurement frequency, and recordkeeping) per the submission content listed in 40 CFR 63.7747(c) and/or 40 CFR 63.9570(c).

Confirm your continuous parameter monitoring system design will meet the operational requirements in §63.5725(b) (minimum cycle per 15-minute period, minimum valid-data percent, 3-hour averaging method, and required records of inspections/calibrations).

candidates.title: Natural Gas Processing Plants (Subpart HH)

criteria.criterion: If a piece of ancillary equipment or a compressor is located at a natural gas processing plant and operates in VHAP service equal to or greater than 300 hours per calendar year, then it is subject to the equipment leak standards in this subpart.

If ancillary equipment or compressors are subject to and controlled under the requirements of subpart H or are subject to and controlled under 40 CFR part 60, subpart OOOO, then the equipment leak standards in §63.769 do not apply to those items.

If the percent VHAP content of the process fluid contacting a piece of ancillary equipment or compressor can be reasonably expected never to exceed 10.0 percent by weight as demonstrated using the methods in §63.772(a), then that piece of equipment is not in VHAP service and the VHAP-service-based equipment-leak requirements do not apply.

If a pressure relief device is subject to this subpart, then it must be monitored quarterly and within 5 days after each pressure release to detect leaks (with limited exceptions), and a leak for a pressure relief device is detected at an instrument reading of 10,000 ppm or greater.

If the plant is a nonfractionating plant that does not have design capacity to process 283,000 standard cubic meters per day or more of field gas, then pumps in VHAP service, valves in gas/vapor and light liquid service, and pressure relief devices in gas/vapor service at that plant are exempt from the routine monitoring requirements referenced in this section.

If a potential leak interface is being evaluated for 'no detectable emissions' under this subpart, then the no detectable emissions procedure of Method 21 must be used (with specified instrument calibration gases and options to adjust for background) and an interface is determined to have no detectable organic emissions if the measured value (or background-adjusted difference) is less than 500 ppmv.

candidates.title: General Provisions (Subpart A)

criteria.criterion: If an applicable subpart requires monitoring of equipment with a 40 CFR part 60, appendix A-7, Method 21 monitor, then the owner or operator may choose to use the alternative work practice (optical gas imaging) in lieu of Method 21 provided the requirements and instrument specifications in §63.11(e) are met.

If the alternative work practice (optical gas imaging) is used to detect leaks, then the owner or operator must perform daily instrument checks at the calculated mass flow rate, keep video records with date/time stamps, perform an annual Method 21 screening at the applicable leak definition, and keep the required records as specified in §63.11(e).

If the alternative work practice is used instead of Method 21, then the owner or operator must select one of the monitoring frequencies listed in Table 1 to subpart A in lieu of the frequency specified in the applicable subpart and certain provisions (skip periods, QIP, allowable percent leaking) do not apply for equipment using the alternative work practice.

checklist: Confirm the facility is a natural gas processing plant as defined in §63.761.
Identify which pieces of equipment are 'ancillary equipment' (pumps, pressure relief devices, sampling connection systems, open-ended valves/lines, valves, flanges, connectors) per §63.761.
Determine whether any ancillary equipment or compressors are already subject to and controlled under subpart H or 40 CFR part 60, subpart OOOO (if so, §63.769 may not apply) per §63.769(b).
For each piece of ancillary equipment/compressor, determine the number of hours it operates in VHAP service per calendar year and whether it is ≥ 300 hours to test applicability per §63.769(a).

Measure or calculate the percent VHAP (weight fraction) of the process fluid contacting each piece of equipment using Method 18 or ASTM D6420 per §63.772(a)(1) to confirm if VHAP service (>10% by weight) applies.
If the plant is nonfractionating, verify the plant's design capacity to process field gas (is it < or ≥ 283,000 standard cubic meters per day) to assess monitoring exemptions in §63.769(c)(5).

List which devices are pressure relief devices, pumps, and valves and note intended monitoring frequencies and repair schedules (pressure relief devices: quarterly and within 5 days after release; leak definition 10,000 ppm for PRDs) per §63.769(c)(1)-(3).

If using 'no detectable emissions' testing, confirm Method 21 instrument calibration each day, calibration gases (zero air and methane in air <10,000 ppm), and that the detection limit and background adjustment procedures are applied per §63.772(c)(2)-(7).

Decide whether to use the alternative work practice (optical gas imaging) instead of Method 21 and, if so, ensure the OGI instrument meets §63.11(e)(1) specs, perform and document daily instrument checks per §63.11(e)(2), maintain video records with date/time stamps, and plan annual Method 21 re-screening per §63.11(d)(7) and §63.11(e)(4)-(5).

Prepare to maintain all required records (equipment list for AWP, detection sensitivity chosen, daily instrument check records and videos, annual Method 21 screening results) and retain for the periods specified in §63.11(e).

If a leak is detected, determine the applicable repair schedule under the referenced requirements (repair-as-soon-as-practicable and applicable deadlines) and whether delay of repair is allowed under the cited provisions in this subpart and referenced part 61 provisions per §63.769(c)(3) and §63.773(c).

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If the owner or operator intends to conduct a performance test, then the owner or operator must notify the Administrator in writing of the intention at least 60 calendar days before the performance test is initially scheduled to begin to allow review of the site-specific test plan and to permit an observer to be present during the test.

If the owner or operator wishes to change an applicable time period or postmark deadline (for example, the 60-day notification period), then the owner or operator may request an adjustment in writing as soon as practicable before the subject activity and the Administrator may approve the adjustment by mutual agreement.

If a force majeure is about to occur, occurs, or has occurred and the owner or operator intends to assert a claim of force majeure causing delay in testing beyond the regulatory deadline, then the owner or operator shall notify the Administrator in writing as soon as practicable and provide a description and proposed new test date, and the Administrator may in its discretion grant an extension of the performance test deadline.

If the owner or operator submits a written application for a waiver of an individual performance test and demonstrates to the Administrator that the conditions (such as continuous compliance or other justification) are met, then the Administrator may waive the performance test.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Asphalt Roofing Manufacturing (Subpart LLLLL)

criteria.criterion: If an affected source under this subpart is required to conduct a performance test, then the source must submit a notification of intent to conduct the performance test at least 60 calendar days before the performance test is scheduled to begin as required by § 63.7(b)(1).

If the source is an existing affected source, then the source must conduct initial performance tests no later than 180 days after the compliance date specified for the source and according to § 63.7(a)(2).

If the owner or operator intends to use results of a previously-conducted emission test in lieu of performing an initial performance test, then the owner or operator must demonstrate to the Administrator that no process changes occurred, that operating conditions and test methods conform to subpart requirements, that control device and parameter values from the previous test will be used for continuous compliance, and that the previous test was completed within the last 60 months.

If the owner or operator uses previously-conducted test data instead of performing an initial performance test, then the source must submit those test data in lieu of initial performance test results with the Notification of Compliance Status as specified for this subpart.

If the source conducts the initial compliance demonstration for emission limitations under this subpart, then the owner or operator must submit the Notification of Compliance Status containing the results of the initial compliance demonstration according to the requirements of § 63.8692(e).

checklist: Confirm whether your facility is an affected source subject to Subpart LLLLL (Asphalt Roofing Manufacturing) and identify the applicable compliance date in § 63.8683 or other subpart provisions.
Determine whether you are a new or existing affected source (new source deadlines differ) and whether a Title V permit has been issued.
Identify the planned date(s) for the performance test and whether the planned date is within 180 days after your compliance date for initial testing.
Verify whether you have a previously-conducted emission test completed within the last 60 months and that no process, control device, or operating-condition changes have occurred since that test.
If relying on prior test data, assemble documentation showing the prior test methods, operating conditions, control device parameters, and that those conform to Subpart LLLLL requirements.
Check whether you have already submitted a site-specific test plan and/or a 60-day notification; note the dates submitted.

Decide whether you will request (a) an adjustment to the 60-day notification period by written mutual-agreement with the Administrator, (b) a waiver of the performance test (with justification of continuous compliance), or (c) an extension or relief due to a force majeure event, and prepare the written justification and supporting information accordingly.

Identify the appropriate recipient for notifications (EPA Regional Office or delegated State authority) per § 63.9(a)(4) and whether electronic submission via CEDRI/CDX is required for your notifications.
If planning electronic submission, confirm CEDRI/CDX availability and, if unavailable, document dates/times and follow the procedures for asserting EPA system outage or force majeure as applicable.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If an owner or operator wishes to use an alternative monitoring procedure, then the Administrator may approve alternatives to any monitoring methods or procedures of this part after receipt and consideration of a written application.

If the alternative monitoring procedure will serve as the performance test method to demonstrate compliance, then the application must be submitted at least 60 days before the performance evaluation is scheduled to begin.

If permission to use an alternative monitoring procedure has not been granted by the Administrator, then the owner or operator remains subject to the monitoring requirements of this section and the relevant standard.

If an owner or operator submits an application to use an alternative monitoring procedure, then the application must include a description of the proposed alternative monitoring system addressing the four elements in the definition of monitoring in §63.2 and a performance evaluation test plan as specified in paragraph (e)(3).

If the Administrator approves the use of an alternative monitoring method for an affected source, then the owner or operator must continue to use the approved alternative monitoring method until the Administrator approves another monitoring method allowed by §63.8(f).

candidates.title: Chromium electroplating and anodizing NESHAP

criteria.criterion: If the facility operates enclosed hard chromium electroplating tanks, then the emission limitations and monitoring/operation requirements for enclosed hard chromium electroplating tanks in §63.342(c)(2) and the associated compliance provisions apply to those tanks.

If the owner or operator uses an air pollution control device that is not listed in the rule (e.g., a device not identified in Table 1), then the owner or operator must submit a description of the device, Method 306 test results verifying performance, a copy of the operation and maintenance plan, and appropriate operating parameters and a monitoring plan subject to the Administrator's approval.

If an owner or operator requests an alternative monitoring method to demonstrate continuous compliance with this subpart, then requests and approvals shall be considered in accordance with the procedures and timelines of §63.8(f) as referenced by this subpart.

If the proposed change to monitoring is a major alternative to monitoring as defined in §63.90, then approval of such major alternatives under this subpart is retained by the Administrator and cannot be delegated to State, local, or Tribal agencies.

If installation or use of the monitoring devices specified in this subpart would not provide accurate measurements due to interferences or when alternate monitoring locations would provide more representative measurements, then the Administrator may approve alternative monitoring methods for this subpart.

checklist: Confirm tanks are enclosed hard chromium electroplating tanks (number of tanks: 3) and whether they are new or existing (affects which §63.342 limits apply).

Determine whether the facility is a 'large' or 'small' hard chromium electroplating facility (calculate/verify cumulative rectifier capacity or any federally-enforceable rectifier-capacity limit as described in §63.342(c)(3)).

Confirm the control device type (Palm Technology Emission Eliminating Devices) and verify whether that device is one of the control techniques listed in Table 1 (CMP, PSB, fiber-bed, wetting-agent/foam) or is an unlisted APCD requiring submission under §63.342(d).

Assess whether standard monitoring/test methods (e.g., Method 306/306A/306B or monitoring devices prescribed in the subpart) are technically infeasible or produce inaccurate measurements for the Palm device (document interferences or measurement limitations).

Decide whether the alternative monitoring procedure will be used as the performance test method; if so, identify the scheduled performance evaluation date and ensure application is prepared ≥60 days before that date per §63.8(f)(4)(i).

Prepare the alternative-monitoring application content: description addressing the four monitoring elements in §63.2, and a site-specific performance evaluation test plan meeting §63.8(e)(3) requirements (data quality objectives, QA program, procedures).
Determine whether the requested alternative constitutes a minor, intermediate, or major change under §63.90 (this affects approval authority and delegation per §63.348(c)(3)).

If the control device is unlisted, assemble Method 306 test results (three-run average per §63.344(c)(1)), the proposed O&M plan, and proposed operating parameters and monitoring plan for submission/approval per §63.342(d) and §63.344(c).

Verify whether implementation/enforcement authority for this subpart is delegated in your state (contact EPA Region or permitting authority) because approval of certain alternatives (especially major monitoring alternatives) may be retained by the EPA Administrator per §63.348(c)(3).

Be prepared to continue to meet existing monitoring requirements until explicit Administrator approval of any alternative monitoring method is received (do not rely on an alternative prior to approval).

candidates.title: Heat exchange system requirements (Subpart F)

criteria.criterion: If you monitor cooling water for the presence of organic HAP or other representative substances using analytical methods, then the concentration must be determined using an EPA-approved method listed in 40 CFR part 136 that is sensitive to concentrations as low as 10 parts per million and the same method must be used for both entrance and exit samples.

If you collect samples to detect leaks in a heat exchange system, then samples shall be collected at the entrance and exit points (or equivalent locations) and a minimum of three sets of samples must be taken at each entrance and exit and the average entrance and exit concentrations calculated.

If you propose an analytical or sampling approach different than the methods in part 136 or the sampling approach specified for heat exchange monitoring (for example, a composite sampling technique where the rule expects separate sets of entrance/exit samples), then the alternative method may be used only upon approval by the Administrator.

candidates.title: Process vent and transfer operations provisions (Subpart G)

criteria.criterion: If you use Method 18 or Method 25A (or Method 320 / ASTM D6420-18 where allowed) to measure concentration for process vent group determination or mass flow calculations, then the minimum sampling time for each run is 1 hour and the run must use either an integrated sample or four grab samples (if grab sampling is used, take the grabs at approximately equal intervals during the run).

If you are conducting a performance test for control devices (transfer operations or other process-vent control-device tests), then each performance-test run shall consist of a minimum sampling period (typically 1 hour) using either an integrated sample or a minimum of four grab samples taken at approximately equal intervals.

If you wish to monitor parameters or use a monitoring approach other than those specified in the monitoring requirements for process vents (for example, proposing composite sampling in lieu of the specified integrated or grab sampling), then you must request approval of the alternative monitoring parameter/approach under the petition procedures for this subpart.

If you use grab sampling to meet the minimum-sampling requirements under these procedures, then the grab samples must be taken at approximately equal intervals in time during the required minimum sampling period (for example, four grabs at ~15 minute intervals during a 1-hour run).

checklist: Determine whether the measurement target is cooling water (heat exchanger monitoring subject to Subpart F) or a gas/vapor process vent or transfer operation (subject to Subpart G).

Identify which specific test/method you intend to use (e.g., EPA part 136 water method, Method 18, Method 25A, Method 320, Modified El Paso Method, ASTM D6420-18) and confirm the method’s sampling requirements and whether it treats composite samples as an allowable 'integrated' sample.

For heat-exchanger cooling-water monitoring (Subpart F): verify that the chosen part 136 method is sensitive to 10 ppm or lower and that you will collect entrance and exit samples at the designated locations and take at least three sets at each location.

For process-vent or transfer-operation testing (Subpart G): verify whether you are performing a performance test (three runs) or an initial/periodic measurement and confirm the required run duration (typically 1 hour) and whether sampling must be integrated or a minimum of four grab samples taken at equal intervals.

If you plan to use composite sampling instead of the required integrated sample or specified grab-sample scheme, determine whether the composite qualifies as an 'integrated' sample per the referenced EPA method or if it constitutes an alternative method requiring Administrator approval.

If proposing an alternative method/parameter (including composite sampling), prepare the documentation and formal request for approval under the subpart’s alternative-monitoring approval procedures (per the subpart’s petition/approval references) and identify the responsible Administrator/authority for submission.

Document sampling locations (entrance and exit points for heat exchangers; after last recovery device and before control device for process vents), sampling frequency, and how sample sets or runs will be composed and preserved for recordkeeping and reporting.
Confirm whether the monitoring is part of routine periodic monitoring or a required performance test (different requirements for number of runs, sample handling, and reporting).

For heat-exchanger monitoring, verify whether your situation could instead qualify for surrogate monitoring under Subpart F(c) (and if so, prepare a monitoring plan that documents how the surrogate reliably indicates leaks).

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Primary Aluminum Reduction Plants

criteria.criterion: If the facility is an existing primary aluminum reduction plant with a pitch storage tank subject to subpart LL, then each pitch storage tank must be equipped with an emission control system designed and operated to reduce inlet POM emissions by 95 percent or greater.

If an existing pitch storage tank was shut down at the time compliance would have otherwise been required and is subsequently restarted, then the owner/operator must conduct the required performance test by the 30th day following startup of the pitch storage tank.

If demonstrating initial compliance for a pitch storage tank by design evaluation or performance test, then the owner/operator must submit the specified documentation for a design evaluation or conduct a Method 315 performance test and include the detailed carbon adsorber design/operating parameters (e.g., carbon amount, number of beds, humidity, feed flow, desorption/regeneration schedule) where carbon adsorption is used.

candidates.title: General Provisions

criteria.criterion: If the owner/operator of an existing affected source subject to a section 112(d) standard is unable to comply because installation of controls is necessary, then the owner/operator may request that the Administrator (or a State with an approved permit program) grant up to one additional year to comply for the purpose of installing controls.

If requesting an extension under §63.6(i)(4), then the owner/operator must submit the written request no later than 120 days prior to the affected source's compliance date unless the need for the extension arose after that date due to circumstances beyond reasonable control, in which case a later submission is permitted if it includes the reasons and the date the owner/operator first learned of the problems.

If requesting a compliance extension under §63.6(i)(4), then the request must include a description of the controls to be installed and a compliance schedule listing milestone dates (initiation of on-site construction/installation, completion, and final compliance) as specified in §63.6(i)(6).

candidates.title: Extension of compliance, and performance test, monitoring, recordkeeping and reporting waivers and alternatives (example provisions)

criteria.criterion: If the owner/operator of an existing source subject to this subpart is unable to comply with a section 112(d) standard because installation of controls is necessary, then the Administrator may grant up to one additional year to comply for installation of controls.

If requesting an extension under §63.1112(a)(4) for a section 112(d) standard, then the owner/operator must submit the written request not later than 12 months before the affected source's compliance date (or 18 months before the compliance date if the source is including emission points in an emissions average).

If requesting an extension under §63.1112(a)(4), then the request must include the description of controls, a compliance schedule with milestones (contracts/orders, start of on-site construction/installation, completion, and final compliance), and interim emission-control steps as specified in §63.1112(a)(6).

If requesting an extension and also seeking a waiver of an initial performance test, then the application for the performance-test waiver should accompany the extension request as described in this subpart.

checklist: Confirm whether the facility is a primary aluminum reduction plant and whether it has a paste production plant and one or more pitch storage tanks (i.e., whether Subpart LL applies).
Confirm whether the pitch storage tank at issue is an existing tank or a new/reconstructed tank (affects which emission-limit section applies).

Verify the facility shutdown and restart dates (idled on 2016-03-31 and actual or planned restart date) to determine applicability of the restart provisions and the 30-day performance-test timing under §63.847(c)(3)(iv).
Verify which compliance date applies to the pitch storage tank POM requirement (whether the Oct 16, 2017 compliance date in §63.847(a)(3) applies to your tank).

Determine whether the tank's control requirement is the 95% POM inlet reduction and whether the planned carbon adsorber design is expected to achieve ≥95% removal and document carbon adsorber parameters (carbon amount per bed, number of beds, flow, humidity, temperature, desorption/regeneration schedule, vacuum desorption pressure drop) for a design evaluation per §63.847(g)(2)(v).

Determine whether the pitch tank vents share a control device with other emission points (if so, identify those emission points to include in any design evaluation or performance test per §63.847(g)).

Establish whether you will demonstrate compliance by design evaluation or by conducting a Method 315 performance test, and if by test, note that a performance test for a restarted tank must be done within 30 days of startup per §63.847(c)(3)(iv).

Check whether the State has an approved part 70 (Title V) permit program and whether the State (rather than EPA) is the appropriate authority to receive an extension request per §63.6(a)(1) and §63.6(i)(4)(i)(A).
Record whether the facility is subject to emissions averaging (affects the subpart YY submission deadline of 12 vs 18 months).
Note whether a Title V permit application or revision will be required to incorporate extension conditions if an extension is requested (per §63.6(i)(4)(i)(A)).

Document the date any extension request was or will be submitted and verify whether submission meets the deadline requirements (§63.6: no later than 120 days before compliance date unless later-submission criteria apply; §63.1112: no later than 12 months (or 18 months) before compliance date).

Assemble the contents for an extension request: description of controls to be installed, compliance schedule with milestone dates (contracts/orders, start of on-site construction/installation, completion, final compliance), description of interim emission-control steps, and whether a waiver of an initial performance test is requested (per §63.6(i)(6) and §63.1112(a)(6)).

Verify whether the extension request constitutes a nonfrivolous request (so it will stay applicability pending decision) and retain records to show when the need for extension first arose if submitting after the standard 120-day/12-month deadline (per §63.6(i)(4)(i)(C) and §63.1112(a)(4)(i)(B)).

Keep evidence and supporting documents (contract/tender dates, delivery lead times, supplier communications, construction/installation schedules) to support the compliance schedule and any demonstration that additional time is necessary for installation of controls.
